Android 21 (Evil) Realistic Multi-Color Parted Statue 1. Concept & Design This statue reimagines Android 21 (Majin form) with a realistic anatomical style while preserving her iconic dangerous aura and allure. The physique is intentionally stylized—finely detailed abdominal muscles, tense dynamic limbs, and a confident forward-leaning battle stance—amplifying the intimidating elegance behind her character. Engineered as a fully multi-color parted model, every major visual element is physically separated: her volumetric silver-gray hair, black tube top, gold arm rings, gloves, boots, belt, baggy pants, face features, and even her long pink tail. Each color exists as an individual printed part, meaning no AMS, no filament swapping required , yet the final assembly achieves a near-collectible finish straight off the print bed. 2. Engineering & Recommended Assembly Order The model is engineered to significantly reduce print time and failure risk. All parts are intentionally designed with forgiving tolerances. Since printers often vary slightly in dimensional accuracy, each part is meant to be joined securely using CA glue (super glue) . Gently heating joint areas with a heat gun before applying glue helps the adhesive cure faster and bond stronger. ⚠️ CRITICAL ASSEMBLY STEPS & PRO TIPS: To avoid top-heavy balance issues during gluing, please follow this precise assembly sequence : Upper Torso (Important Note): Assemble the upper chest and shoulders first , and then attach the black tube top clothing piece . This ensures a smooth fit and seamless alignment. Head & Hair Module: Combine the main volumetric hair and face piece first . Next, attach the neck and front bangs , and finally mount the complete head assembly onto the upper torso. Lower Body & Tail: Pre-assemble the pants, boots, and belt completely, then attach the pink tail . Final Upper-to-Lower Merge (Pro Tip): Complete the lower body group (pants + boots + belt + tail) first before joining it with the upper body. Installing top parts too early creates heavy top-weight from the massive hair, making lower joint gluing extremely difficult and forcing awkward holding angles while waiting for glue to set! 3. Display & Customization Although fully colored through part separation alone, painters may optionally enhance shadows on the black top, gold trims, or skin folds to further elevate realism. Her fierce stance and striking silhouette make this statue ideal as a standalone centerpiece or as part of a paired display alongside Majin Buu. The clean part boundaries also make it enjoyable for hobbyists who prefer hybrid finishing—mixing raw printed colors with light airbrush detailing. 4. Conclusion Following the release of Majin Buu, this Android 21 statue marks another exciting milestone in multi-color parted sculpture design. It delivers an accessible printing experience while maintaining professional visual depth. Your support and patience made this milestone possible, and more multi-color parted designs are actively in development. Quick Tips: For complex prints, avoid photography mode: It increases carriage travel and print failure risks. Calibrate your machine and use dry, stable filament to maximize printing reliability. Filament preference: Bambu’s gray remains my personal favorite. Cleanup tools: Needle-nose pliers and Bambu’s FAC002-N scraper make support removal significantly easier.

description: Large Xenomorph! The time if finally here to post a project I have been working on over the last month. After the recent set of my smaller Xenomorph models, I got peer-pressured into making one that was lifesized (ish). This model model stands 5ft tall from floor to tip of tail, measures almost 6ft long diagonally from the back foot to the tip of the head, and is almost 4 foot wide! In order to get it to fit through my doorways I ended up leaving the Head, Right Arm, and half othe tail removable and not fully glued in place. This project is not for everyone and requires quite a bit of dedication and printing resouces to make. At the time of the upload I only sliced the model to fit the H series and A2L printers (to maximize the the size of pieces I could print). Please note that if you are changing your printer from the current H2D that is seleted in the profile you may need to move some pieces around to make sure they fully fit within the build volume. Most are OK, but some have next to no wiggle room for placement. Please also note that the current profile is set to be printed with a .6mm nozzle. This helps speed up print time and the use the .3x layer heights* I printed my model with a very low infill amount (3-4% for most of the print) with the exception of some of the support/critical stress pieces where I increased the infill. This allowed to print quick and not use too much filament. I printed my model in MATTE PLA from Bambu, but due to the low infill amount, and the size/geometry of the model I REALLY wish I did it PETG so that I could display it outside and not worry about the tail melting/bending in the sun (still a risk with PETG I guess, but not as much). The assembly requires and advaced level of skill, this is not for first time large model printers. I did my best to make hexagonal pegs to help align everything, but you will likely need to sand all of the surfaces to ensure a good fit. I used CA glue on the pegs, with a 2-part expoxy to hold the flat surfaces together. To fill the joints I useda 2-part epoxy putty that I found on Amazon. Please note that the Base Tail section and the main body has an interference that I didn't catch until after the model was fully sliced and will need to be manually trimmed/sanded when doing the test fitting. I just used my scraper and knife to snip away bits of the main body until the tail section could fully fit. Please be careful test fitting pieces, due to the low infill amount it can be easy to break*** After the resin cured and the gaps were filled I sanded the joints using 320 grit sand paper before applying a bit of primer, and I used a Gloss Black spray paint to the the entire model. I ended up using a total of 6 spray paint cans* so plan accordingly. The Drool was accomplished using a 2-part epoxy resin (for fiberglass in my particular case) and I used some 2" brushes to coat the entire model and make it appear more wet than the gloss paint achieved by itself. To get the drool effect, I waited until the resin was just about dried, and kept applying over the mouth area until it didn't fully run off. A good/easier way to do this may be with some UV activated epoxy that cures in 5-10 seconds, but I have not tried this route. The teeth were painted in steps between the epoxy using an air brush.

description: In Book Five of the Odyssey , Odysseus is finally within sight of home when the sea itself turns against him. Poseidon, the Earth-Shaker, the dark-maned lord of the deep has not forgotten that this man blinded his son, the Cyclops Polyphemus. So he gathers the clouds, takes up his trident, and calls every wind down onto a single raft. This is that moment made solid. Not a calm sea-king on a throne, but the god rising out of his own storm: the wave curling into a fist beneath him, the trident already lifted, the grudge that will keep a hero wandering for ten more years. Homer never lets us forget that the sea has a memory, and a temper. I wanted the base to carry that: the water isn't scenery, it's Poseidon's will taking shape. Sculpted as a single figure rising from a sculptural mass of sea, so the wave does the storytelling instead of a second character competing for the eye.

description: “Big Chap” (Alien) Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed, “Big Chap” Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 18" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 19" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 19" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. I had 4 machines running test prints none stop. I promise though, it is worth it at the end. **Please also be aware that the model images you see are 100% real, with 0 use of AI, but they have been post-process colored using some Rub'n Buff waxes, 2-part epoxy resin, and then some gloss clear coat layer application at the end. ASSEMBLY REQUIRED ** Discard the small round cylinder that prints on the 2nd plate with the arms and foot. It is an uneeded part that was a result of slicing the model in the studio* The 19" tall, multipiece print will require some glue. I have used both super glue, as well as hot glue. Hot glue was my preference. With all the parts printed, and supports cleaned up (TAKE YOUR TIME REMOVING THE SUPPORTS AS THE PARTS ARE HIGHLY DETAILED AND FRAGILE ) do a dry-fit of all the parts to ensure proper fitment. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff Antique Gold wax for the Xenomorph, and Brass color for the base. Wear gloves and apply the wax to a towel and gently go over the details. Avoid pressing really hard so that the void remain black/dark, this helps with final contrast of the model. As you can tell from these two photos the difference between the plain model and the colored one is pretty phenomenal and I HIGHLY recommend going through the effort!

This project is a highly customizable 3D Car Profile Desk Sign. Create the perfect personalized gift for any car enthusiast by blending their name directly into the silhouette of a sleek car model. Fully parametric in OpenSCAD. ⚠️ BETA VERSION - COMMUNITY FEEDBACK NEEDED!⚠️ This is the beta release of our Car Sign generator. Due to the high level of customization, there are still several challenges regarding part positioning, support generation, and overall print optimization. We want to build this project together with the community and are actively looking for your feedback on: * Best printing orientation(laying flat vs standing up) * Support settings** (if needed for overhanging letters) * General optimizations to make printing easier Please leave a comment with your tips, pictures, and suggestions to help us improve the final version! --- CUSTOMIZATION --- Choose from 5 distinct car models and adjust sizes, thickness, and text spacing to create a completely unique desk piece. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Size Selection - Médio (Medium): 97x20x35 mm - The perfect balanced size for shelves and desk displays. - Grande (Large): 145x30x50 mm - A striking centerpiece for a desk or garage. 2. Car Settings & Base - Car Model: Choose between Sedan, Hatchback (Default), Retro Muscle, Supercar, or Original Sports Car. - Solid Base (Use_Solid_Base): **Enabled by default!** Adds a solid backing plate behind the letters in the exact shape of the car profile. This greatly improves structural rigidity, prevents fragile letters from snapping, and makes the side-profile look stunning. You can adjust the base thickness. - Flip Car (Flip_Car_Horizontally): Mirrors the car horizontally so the front points the other way, ensuring it flows perfectly with your chosen name. 3. Text Customization - Name / Text: Type any name or word (Default: "TESLA"). - Font Style: Currently locked to a robust, bold font (*Courier New Bold*) that works exceptionally well for 3D printing and Boolean intersections. - Letter Spacing & Thickness: Adjust how close the letters sit (Default: 0.85) and add extra boldness (Default: 1.2) if needed for better fusion. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS --- - Flawless Geometry: The model uses an advanced OpenSCAD boolean intersection technique to guarantee a 100% solid, gap-free model (manifold) that imports perfectly into your slicer without errors. - Smooth Vector Curves: The car profiles have been algorithmically smoothed to completely eliminate jagged pixel-stepped edges. --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- Depending on your chosen car model and specific letter combination, you might need to adapt your slicing approach. Here are some potential strategies you can use to reduce supports and improve print quality: - Orientation: Rotate the part in the X and Y axes on your build plate. Finding the perfect angle depending on your specific car model and letter combination can drastically reduce overhangs! - Supports: Enable supports only for critical areas. - Layer Height: Use Variable Layer Height. This keeps print times low while creating perfectly smooth curves on the car's roof and hood. - Top Surface Pattern: Rectilinear. - Ironing: Test Enabled (Topmost surface only) for a perfectly smooth finish on the front face of the letters. - Wall Generator: Arachne (Crucial for sharp letter details). - Outer Wall Speed: Reduce the speed of the outer walls to ensure a flawless, premium surface finish. - Infill: 10% Gyroid.

“The Odyssey - Achilles” I have wanted to recreate and color my take on Achilles from The Odyssey for quite some time.. and figured what better time than when the contest is ongoing? This is a 20" tall, highly detailed, multi-piece print. Please note that the print profile is SINGLE COLOR ONLY. The coloring of the model was achieved in post-process application of coloring wax, as well as acrylic paints applied via air brush. This is not your typical AI colored model, this is truly what this could look like! I only spent 30 minutes on mine! The model prints in several pieces in order to maximize the build volumes of the P and X series machines. Some gluing is required. ASSEMBLY Assembly of the model is very straightfoward - first glue the upper torso to the lower body, and then test fit the arms. The arms stay in place pretty good, and I highly recommend waiting to glue the arms/shield on until after you're doing with painting just so you can have better access. Once the modle is painted, just add a drop of glue on each joing and press them into place. Wait to glue the arrows into their respective holes until the end of the process. COLOR APPLICATION I used a very straightforward process for my coloring via application of some Rub'n Buff waxes - Antique Gold, Copper, Brass, etc. Below is an example of this application process on my Alien model I posted earlier. I simply use a microfiber towel, wear gloves, dab a bit of the Rub'n Buff (I buy mine on amazon) and lightly spread it on the model. For this particular model I could have stopped at the first Bronze look.. but I decided to try out some acrylic paints and see what I can do to really bring it to life. After about 20 minutes of spraying this was the end result! I use really cheap, hobby store acrylic paints that are water based. I dilute them with distilled water to make them sprayable. Clean up is a breeze, and so far I have been loving the color effects. As a finishing step, I applied to Matte Clear Coat to the model. The Before and After really give you a good idea of just a little added effort can REALLY make for an awesome print!

description: F1 - Redbull Racing RB20 - 1/12 Scale model! Next on my list is this my take on Redbull's RB20 F1 Car done in 1/12 scale! The main idea behind this model was to try and (finally) make a model with some spinning wheels. I had a bunch of 608 bearings from an old project and models this size/wheels around it. The car body is split into 3 pieces to fit the X/P series machines. The wheels and wheel covers print separately. Gluing is required. Size This is a 1/12th scale model Assembly Assembly is straightfoward. The body of the car has hex pegs and needs to be glued. I use Contact Adhesive but any glue will work. The only thing to watchout for is to make sure that your body is perfectly aligned, or your wheels won't sit square across all 4 corners. While the body is drying, take your 608 bearings and press them into the wheel/tire. With that done, install the wheels onto the body (paying attention to which is the front and rear) by pressing the bearing onto the stub shaft. The fit should be somewhat snug, but not too tight. If you are having issues sliding the wheel on, I recommed sanding the wheel stud around just a bit to smooth it out. With the wheels pressed onto the body, proceed to install the retainer washer by pressing it onto the shaft. Don't press it too tight against the wheel or it will prevent free wheel spin. If you want added assurance that this stays in place, you can add a dab of glue to the washer/stubshaft, but it will make it impossible to remove later. With the wheel retainers installed, proceed to press in the covers (again paying attention to the front/rear as they are different). You're done! Only thing left is to paint it you want to go an extra step!

description: The Story behind the Sculpture Humanity has forever been caught in a silent, beautiful tug-of-war. description: Hades & Persephone – Between Two Worlds ( 3 part sculpture, no AMS needed ) A story of light drawn toward darkness, and darkness softened by light. Inspired by the ancient Homeric Hymn to Demeter , this dual sculpture captures the fateful moment when Persephone is offered the pomegranate—the fruit that will forever connect her to the Underworld. As the old tale tells it, Hades gave her the sweet pomegranate seed, quietly binding her to his realm and dividing her life between the darkness below and the blooming world above. Persephone can be displayed in two different positions , allowing you to change the meaning of the scene: Place her slightly farther back, with her hand only reaching toward the pomegranate—a moment of hesitation, temptation, and choice. Move her forward so her hand is touching the pomegranate , capturing the instant when her fate becomes intertwined with Hades and the Underworld. The bright floral details and flowing dress of Persephone contrast with Hades’ dark crown, powerful form, and gothic Underworld base. Display them together as one dramatic scene or separately to emphasize the distance between their two worlds. A striking mythological statement piece about love, longing, temptation, and the eternal balance between darkness and spring. Printing Use a clean print plate with some glue (unless you are using a super tack plate) Use dried out filament (Different filament and printers impacts the print differently, please adjust your settings accordingly.) Keep the models in the provided positions Support Removal Instructions Allow the print to cool completely before removing it from the build plate. Use small flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, and tweezers to remove the support branches in smaller pieces. Patience and careful handling are important for protecting the hands and the leaves. Be especially careful around the hands and leaves. Gently pull/wiggle the support downwards. Break the branches into smaller sections and alternate around each supported section as needed. I needed to alternate between the front and backside around the leaves on the Persephone sculpture. After removing the supports, clean up potential rough contact points with a precision knife, small file, or fine-grit sandpaper if needed. Light sanding and gentle, controlled heat may be needed to clean up areas where the supports were attached. I used a handheld mini torch, but apply heat carefully to avoid warping or damaging the print. Wood PLA is very sensitive to heat! description: "Internecivus Raptus" (Alien) - Ultra Detailed Sculpture Staying on the recent Xenomorph Theme, here is another absoutley awesome, and highly detailed “Internecivus Raptus” - Xenomorph Sculpture! There are 2 size profiles being made available at the time of the model upload - 20" tall version as well as a 10" tall version. Please note that the 20" tall version is printed in pieces, and is maximized in size to fit the P/X series printer beds. The 10" tall version is printed a simplified one-piece print. I should know that I have printed 6 different size variants and will note that you can easily scale this between 10" and 20" tall models. **Please be aware that the print times are lengthy. You may need to file down some pieces if they do not fit. All 4 of my models went together with no issues, but different printers/filaments may have some tolerance issues. With the Dry fitting completed, if you are satisfied with the fitment you can take the piees apart and proceed to glue them together. As with the above test-fit process. If you are planning to paint/apply color to the model I highly advise doing so with Xenomorph OFF of the base. For final assembly, apply some glue to the foot mounting pegs and firmly place the model on to the base. Proceed with extreme patience and follow this exact extraction sequence to prevent accidental breakage. 🚫 Golden Rule: Always snip contact tips with fine flush cutters and pull support branches DOWNWARD , never outward or toward yourself, to avoid applying snapping leverage against the thin bone connections. 🌾 Step 1 - The Scythe & Blade: Begin by freeing the top rune-engraved scythe blade and the upper hand grip. Isolate and clip the tree interface tips around the elbows before pulling the outer supports away. 👗 Step 3 - The Tattered Skirt: Gently disengage the support columns surrounding the lower tattered loincloth/skirt. description: Carved Walnut Parlor Suite VEF-SUITE-0053 1:12 How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model To Change the Scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊 [End]

description: FULLY ARTICULATED or FLEXI, Glow In The Dark Anglerfish Detailed Description of the Model Bring the deep ocean trenches right to your desk with this fully articulated, print-in-place Anglerfish model! Designed with intricate textural scales, razor-sharp teeth, and its iconic illuminated lure, this model features zero assembly and requires no supports. It prints entirely as one piece with fluid, snaking articulation across its body segments, allowing it to slither and pose naturally. To achieve that authentic bioluminescent deep-sea look, print it using TECBEARS PLA Glow in The Dark (Luminous) 3D Printer Filament . Because glow-in-the-dark filaments contain abrasive phosphorescent particles, we highly recommend pairing your setup with SUNLU PLA Glow in the Dark Filament or using a hardened steel nozzle to prevent premature wear. How It's Used & Functional Applications Fidget & Desk Toy: The multi-segment flexible spine makes for an incredible sensory fidget toy that relieves stress and looks striking resting on any shelf or monitor stand. Nighttime Display: Charge the filament under a bright light or UV source to watch the deep-sea predator cast an eerie, glowing green light in a dark room. History & Background Anglerfish are famous inhabitants of the aphotic zone of the ocean—the pitch-black depths of the sea where sunlight never reaches. Using a modified fin ray acting as a glowing bioluminescent lure (the esca) to attract unsuspecting prey, these creatures represent some of the most fascinating evolutionary traits in marine biology. This 3D model captures that natural wonder, translating deep-sea mythology into a modern mechanical print-in-place design. Alternative Uses & Remixing Ideas Aquarium Decor: Scale up the print and seal it with safe coatings to use as an eye-catching centerpiece for a themed freshwater or faux-aquarium setup. description: Chinese Rosewood-inspired Storage Chest – 1:12 Scale A detailed 1:12 scale Chinese rosewood-inspired storage chest designed as a functional miniature furniture piece. This ornate chest features an opening lid with a working captured hinge and two separate functional sliding drawers. It is well suited for dollhouse interiors, historical room scenes, miniature displays, and collector showcases. The model is supplied as three separate STL files: One chest frame with its integrated captured hinged lid Two individual sliding drawers Printing Notes The chest frame and lid print together as a permanently captured assembly. The hinge components capture one another during printing; the lid cannot—and should not—be separated from the chest afterward. Before attempting to open the lid fully, carefully inspect the hinge area. A small amount of adjoining filament may need to be cut away from between the male and female hinge surfaces. Use the tip of a sharp hobby or X-Acto knife carefully, removing only the unwanted filament. Once cleared, gently work the lid through small movements until the hinge operates freely. Do not force the lid open, as excessive pressure may damage the printed hinge. The original model measures: 60 mm W × 65 mm D × 100 mm H Reducing the model size will also reduce the hinge clearances. Smaller prints will require more careful hinge cleanup and release before the lid can move freely. With its decorative detailing, functional drawers, and opening upper compartment, this chest makes an attractive feature piece for miniature bedrooms, studies, period-inspired interiors, and display collections. How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Bambu Settings for this Model For those of you who want the model but in a different scale: Here is the Victorian wall image for you to download and use as a simple 1:12 scale reference. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for checking dollhouse scale. 😊

description: Welcome to Camp Crystal Lake. Jason Voorhees stands full-figure in this tall printed "stained glass" panel — the hockey mask, the work coveralls and gloves, machete in hand — planted on a stone path with the cabin, the pines, and a crescent moon behind him in a green-and-blue night sky. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, turning the whole Friday the 13th scene into glowing glass. 🔪 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Full-scene panel — not just a portrait: Jason stands on a stone path with the cabin, forest, and crescent moon behind him. Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by black "lead came" lines. The full Jason — hockey mask, coveralls, gloves, and machete all rendered in glass. Tall portrait format — an upright panel that fills a vertical window pane. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the fine detail lines — the mask, the coveralls, the cabin logs — crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Mask Translucent white / bone The hockey mask Coveralls & gloves Translucent grey + brown Jason's work clothes Machete Translucent silver + red Blade and blood accent Sky & moon Translucent blue + white The night sky behind him Forest & foliage Translucent greens + brown Trees, cabin, and ground Stone path Translucent tan / sand The path he stands on 📏 Scale to fit your window. The tall format suits a vertical pane — keep the full figure and scene in frame when you scale. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes the night scene light up in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it in a tall window to suit the upright format. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. description: You'll float too. Pennywise leers out of this printed "stained glass" panel — the pale domed forehead, the sweep of orange hair, the red nose and grin, and that huge pleated ruff over the yellow costume, all set against a burst of pale-blue rays. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, the Dancing Clown glowing from your glass. 🎈 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by a black "lead came" outline. Full-face detail — the domed forehead, arched orange hair, red-lined eyes, red nose and grin, all in glass. The pleated ruff — the big radiating collar rendered as a fan of grey-and-white panes. Radiant background — pale-blue rays burst out behind the head like light off a fairground sign. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the fine face lines and the thin red accents on the costume crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Hair Translucent orange The swept-back clown mane Face Translucent white / bone The pale domed forehead Eyes, nose & mouth Translucent red The red-lined eyes, nose, and grin Ruff collar Translucent grey + white The big pleated fan Costume Translucent yellow + red accents The suit and red pom-pom button Background Translucent pale blue / ice The radiating rays 📏 Scale to fit your window. Keep the thin red costume lines in mind if you scale down — very fine leading can get delicate at small sizes. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes the clown light up in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it where the light moves — an east or west window gives the best changing glow through the day. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. description: Chairs of the Past — 1:12 Miniature Series Chairs of the Past brings unusual, historic, and sometimes wonderfully peculiar chair designs back to life as printable 1:12 miniatures. Each model begins with an old engraving or documented chair from another era, then is carefully interpreted as a three-dimensional object suitable for a dollhouse, miniature room, display, or historical scene. Some chairs are elegant, some practical, and others hide surprising stories—but every one offers a small glimpse into how people once sat, worked, rested, and lived. Tennyson Armchair The Tennyson chair is an elegant cane-seated study armchair with a tall arched back, slender turned uprights, and gracefully scrolling arms. Its light, refined construction gives it a more polished and decorative appearance than many of the heavier historic chairs in the series, while the shaped front rail and small hanging pendant details add a touch of Gothic character. This chair was associated with Alfred, Lord Tennyson, and was described as a modern French-type cane-bottomed study chair. The original was sketched in the poet’s study at Haslemere, where it stood near his writing table. That connection gives the chair a quiet literary presence, while its refined silhouette makes it especially appealing as a miniature furnishing. In 1:12 scale, the Tennyson chair would work especially well in: • a study or writing room • a library • a parlour • a literary interior • any miniature setting needing an elegant antique armchair Its open back, cane seat, and decorative details also make it an appealing piece for painted finishes, wood-toning, and fine miniature display work. How I Established the 1:12 Dollhouse Scale The image below shows how I estimated the final 1:12 scale dimensions for this model. I use an image editing application called Pixelmator Pro, but most image editing programs should work. The process is simple: I place the model image into a Victorian room reference image where the back wall has been set to 254 mm high. At 1:12 scale, 254 mm represents a 10-foot ceiling. Once the wall height is set, I resize the model image until it looks correct inside the room. The image editing application then gives me the approximate width and height of the model. I use those measurements as the starting point in my slicer and adjust the 3D model to match. This method helps me scale the model visually, rather than guessing from numbers alone. Important: The wall image must be set to exactly 254 mm high. The width will adjust automatically once the height is set. I have included the wall image near the bottom of this description, after the Buy Me a Coffee notice, so you can download it and use the same method to help scale models for your own 1:12 dollhouse. This is not a precision engineering method, but it is a very useful visual guide for dollhouse room scale. Set the height of this wall image to 254 mm in your image editing application. That represents a 10-foot wall at 1:12 scale. Then import the image of the model you want to scale and place it into the room. Resize the model image until it looks correct visually. Record the model’s height and width from your image application, then use those measurements as a starting point in your slicer. That’s it. description: 2" Virgin Mary Concrete Casting Mold Create a beautiful, 12-inch tall statue of the Virgin Mary with this custom-designed, multi-part 3D printable mold. This project is designed for those who enjoy the challenge of high-quality concrete casting and want to produce professional-looking results at home. Project Overview This mold is comprised of 8 distinct parts, engineered to lock together to create a seamless casting cavity. The intricate details on the inner faces are designed to capture the delicate features and flowing fabric textures of the statue perfectly. Instructions for Casting The process for using this mold requires patience and attention to detail: Printing: Print all 8 segments of the mold. For the best results, I recommend using SUNLU PLA+ Filament , which provides the durability and surface finish needed for intricate molds. Assembly: Connect the printed parts using clips and rubber bands to ensure they are held tightly in place during the pour. No glue is required for this assembly. Concrete Preparation: Select a high-quality concrete mix. Crucially, you must sift out ALL large rocks from the mix to ensure a smooth, detailed surface. Pouring: Add water according to the manufacturer’s instructions and carefully fill the assembled mold. Setting: Allow the concrete to set for the full recommended time specified by the manufacturer. Removal: Once set, place the mold in an oven at a low temperature to slowly and carefully melt the 3D-printed pieces away, revealing your finished statue. Remixing and Applications This design can be adapted for various purposes beyond religious decor: Garden Art: Scale up or down for custom garden accents. Custom Plaster Casting: Use the same mold with plaster of Paris for indoor display pieces. Abstract Sculpture: The modular nature of the 8-part system allows for creative re-orientation to produce abstract, geometric concrete art. model_name: Chucky Stained Glass Suncatcher — Good Guys
description: Wanna play? This is the Good Guy doll himself rebuilt as a printed "stained glass" suncatcher — wild red hair, stitched-up scars, those piercing blue eyes, and the blue "Good Guys" overalls, knife in hand, all ringed by a wheel of red, blue, and yellow glass panes with flames licking up the sides. Hang it in the sun and the translucent PETG lights up like a real leaded window, with a heavy black frame doing the work of the lead came. 🔪 Fan tribute: an original stained-glass interpretation of a horror icon, made as a printed window panel. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the rights holders. Features Backlit "stained glass" effect — translucent panes glow when light passes through, framed by a black "lead came" outline. Loaded with detail — the scarred face, red hair, blue eyes, striped sleeves, raised knife, and the "Good Guys" overalls all rendered in glass panes. Radial glass wheel — a full ring of red, blue, yellow, and orange panes with flame motifs surrounds the figure. Flat, no-support print — one piece, straight on the plate. No supports, no assembly. Multi-color or paint — run it multi-color for the show-piece look, or lay the frame and fill the panes by hand. Two material paths — translucent/transparent PETG for a true glow, or solid PLA for an opaque mosaic look. Print Settings Setting Value Nozzle 0.4 mm Layer height 0.24 mm Infill 100% Wall generator Arachne Top / bottom / infill pattern Aligned Rectilinear Material Translucent/Transparent PETG (show finish) — solid PLA also works Supports None — flat panel Orientation Flat on the build plate ⚙️ Why these settings: 100% infill with Aligned Rectilinear on top, bottom, and infill fills every pane in one even, continuous pass — so backlight diffuses smoothly across the glass instead of looking blotchy. Arachne keeps the many thin black leading lines crisp and unbroken. The show pieces are translucent PETG so the color panes actually glow; solid PLA prints just as cleanly for an opaque mosaic look. Color Guide Area Suggested color Notes Frame / leading Black The outline that defines every pane Hair Translucent red / orange The wild Good Guy mane Face & hands Translucent tan / flesh Scarred doll skin Eyes Translucent blue The piercing stare Overalls Translucent blue The "Good Guys" dungarees Ring panes Translucent red, blue, yellow, orange The radial glass wheel + flames 🎨 No multi-color setup? Print the black frame solid and backfill panes with translucent filament swaps by color, or paint clear panes with glass paint. It reads great either way. 📏 Scale to fit your window. If you scale down, keep an eye on the thin leading lines — they're what hold the piece together. Tips & Tricks Print flat, no supports — the panel lies on the plate and needs nothing under it. Go translucent for the glow — transparent/translucent PETG is what makes it read as real stained glass in a sunny window. Keep the aligned rectilinear pattern — it's what gives the even, light-through-glass diffusion. Hang it where the light moves — an east or west window gives the best changing glow through the day. Solid PLA is a valid look too — an opaque mosaic version reads great on a wall or shelf. description: Команда Флоры — Полный набор главных героев! 🌿 Привет! Это мой первый опыт создания и покраски 3D-фигурок. Я смоделировал и напечатал всех главных героев мультсериала «Команда Флоры» для своей трехлетней дочки. Она в полном восторге и вовсю играет с ними! Проект полностью настроен в Bambu Studio и готов к печати. 🛠️ Рекомендуемые настройки (уже в профиле): Материал: PLA Matte. Прочность (Wall Loops = 5): Количество стенок увеличено до 5, чтобы сделать тонкие части (руки, шеи, косички) максимально крепкими для детских игр. Ориентация деталей: Модели специально размещены на столе под углом. Это меняет направление слоев и делает фигурки гораздо устойчивее к изломам. Настоятельно рекомендую оставить их именно так. Поддержки (Tree Strong): Оптимальный выбор для этого проекта. Удерживают тонкие ножки моделей на столе в процессе печати. Скорость: Профиль настроен на низкую скорость для идеальной детализации. Если хотите сэкономить время — можете попробовать ее увеличить. 🎨 Пост-обработка и покраска: Очистка от поддержек. Покрытие грунтом для пластика. Покраска обычными акриловыми маркерами. Финишный слой матового лака для защиты краски. 💡 Маленький лайфхак: Фигурки прошли жесткий краш-тест трехлетним ребенком. Во время очень активной игры у Бака сломалась шея. Проблему решил обычный суперклей (цианакрилат) — место стыка стало как будто даже прочнее, чем было изначально, и больше никаких поломок не случалось! ⚠️ Правовая информация / Copyright: Создателем и законным держателем прав на персонажей мультсериала «Команда Флоры» является компания Klaxon Production . Официальный сайт правообладателя: klaxprod.ru Flora's Team — Full Main Character Set! 🌿 Hi everyone! This is my first time designing and painting 3D figurines. I modeled and printed all the main characters from the "Flora's Team" animated series for my 3-year-old daughter. She absolutely loves them and plays with them all the time! The project is fully configured in Bambu Studio and ready to print. 🛠️ Recommended Settings (Already in the Print Profile): Material: PLA Matte. Strength (Wall Loops = 5): I increased the wall loops to 5 to make the thin parts (arms, necks, pigtails) as sturdy as possible for active toddler playtime. Part Orientation: The models are intentionally placed on the build plate at an angle. This changes the direction of the layer lines, making the figures much more resistant to snapping. I highly recommend keeping them oriented this way. Supports (Tree Strong): The optimal choice for this project. They keep the thin legs of the models securely attached to the bed during printing. Speed: The profile is configured at a lower speed for maximum detail. If you want to save some time, feel free to try increasing it. 🎨 Post-Processing & Painting: Support removal. Priming with a plastic primer. Painting with regular acrylic paint markers. Applying a clear coat of matte varnish to protect the paint. 💡 Quick Tip: These figures have survived a rigorous crash test by a 3-year-old. During some intense playtime, Buck's neck snapped. I fixed it with regular superglue (cyanoacrylate)—the joint honestly feels even stronger now than it did before, and there haven't been any breaks since! ⚠️ Legal Notice & Copyright: The characters from the "Flora's Team" animated series are created and copyrighted by Klaxon Production . About the process and Print Profile : There are 3 plates depending on your needs and 3d printer set up: AMS facing up : this is the Logo with the text facing up ("looking" at the top of the printer). You need to use this with 2 colors on the AMS. AMS facing down : this is the Logo with the text facing down on your build plate if you want to get the plate texture. You need to use 2 colors on the AMS. No AMS : if you are just like me, and you don't have an AMS yet, you have to use this plate. The process is simple but a bit manual, you have to: chose the position of all objects and never change it again during the process (make sure that you choose a position where the nozzle does not touch the build plate during the start up process), for each of the colors that you want to use, you're going to have to do a “new” print, without removing the previously printed objects: enable each of the same color objects to print (eg all the parts that you want to be gold) and disable the rest of the colors (Process > objects > No AMS Plate > check/uncheck given the color). Print that, when that print ends, manually set up the build plate temperature to prevent the print from ungluing from the plate, remove everything that got printed on the startup process except the actual Logo objects (eg: skirt, nozzle cleaning line, etc), enable a new set of objects of the same colors (and disable the one you just printed) and change the external spool in your 3d printer to that new color you're going to print, eg red repeat the process with all the colors, make sure that the last one is the background one, in this printed example the last one would be white background . NEVER EVER THINK ABOUT TOUCHING OR REMOVING THE BUILD PLATE UNTIL YOU PRINT ALL COLORS!!! Enjoy your multi-color print without AMS! In this particular case, I recommend the following order for the colors: gold > red. I found out that if I did white first, then the blue would unglue the white parts, so this is the order that worked for me. If any of the small parts get unglued, don't get discouraged! you can choose only that object in a new print and re print just that, without needing to start over! I know it's a pretty laborious process and seems hard at first, but feel free to reach out if you have any questions! Once you get the hang of it, it becomes easier and makes your prints more versatile! If you liked this print and process, follow my profile to find out more about my designs. And if you loved it, you can help me out with a boost or a like, that helps me to continue to develop designs like this one :)

description: This is my original concept and design. Personal use only unless purchased from my website: www.themakerseditco.com OR subscribing on MakerWorld. This interchangeable badge reel system was designed so you could easily swap out badge reel toppers by simply attaching a new lid with a glued on topper. The lid is thin and prints very quickly. Note: Make sure to align topper on lid properly. Glue-On Versions: I have designed 2 versions: The twist & lock version is best for PETG or ASA . PLA will fail with this design because the part that keeps it locked in will wear down quickly. This design requires a bit of force to lock the topper in place. Because of this, you will most likely need to glue the badge reel topper design on the lid before trying to twist it on the base. This design has been extensively tested. It 100% works, but it is a tight fit. If it does not “click” into place, you have not gotten it all the way on. I have inlcuded a looser fit base for anyone having issues with the original base. This was my first design, but it can be difficult to use for some people. To make this interchangeable system easy to use for everyone, I created the threaded, screw on version. The threaded, screw-on versions works with PLA. I personally use Bambu Lab Basic PLA. There are alignment slots on this design. I recommend .12mm (High Quality) layer height and 4 wall loops. I cannot guarantee that the slots will align properly if you use different settings. Due to different printers and filament, there is a possibility that your slots won't line up perfectly, even with using my settings. I have included an option with no alignment slots. This design allows you to easily twist the lid on the base and then glue your topper on if that is easier for you. Badge Reel Cover: It fits standard badge reels that are no more than 33mm in diameter. This was intentionally designed to cover the entire badge reel and to not use magnets. This badge reel holder is 43.5mm in diameter and is better suited for jumbo badge reel toppers. Due to the diameter of this design, it works exceptionally well for jumbo badge reel toppers by helping it to sit flatter and not flop over as much.

description: Create a custom print-in-place chain in the length and style you want. ChainMaker is a fully parametric OpenSCAD generator for classic interlocking chains and sculpted Cuban chains. Choose a target length or link count, customize the link geometry, and arrange the chain to suit your build plate. Smart sizing, layout, spacing, and validation systems handle the technical work behind the scenes, so you can focus on designing the chain instead of constructing it. Click Customize to open the generator. 🚀 Quick Start 1. Choose the Chain Select Classic for alternating interlocking links or Cuban for smooth, flattened links. Set a target stretched length, enter a manual link count, and resize the complete design with Link Scale . 2. Choose the Layout Arrange the chain as a Closed Loop , Closed Snake , Straight line, or compact Spiral . Use Print Spacing to control the distance between neighboring links, and adjust the bend or layout-specific settings when needed. 3. Customize the Links Classic links support rounded or chamfered paths, multiple profiles, profile twist, thickness, and interlocking angle. Cuban links provide control over radii, thickness, Bezier shaping, and face flattening. Enable Connector Link to open one end link for attachments or reconnecting the chain. Enable Debug to view calculated chain and layout information. 4. Preview and Export Inspect the complete layout in your slicer and check that all links remain separate. Once satisfied, export your chain at the desired resolution and print. Have fun! ⭐ Features Two Link Families Create two distinct chain families with one shared sizing and layout system. Smart Length Solving Enter a target length or choose the exact number of links yourself. Flexible Print Layouts Use rounded loops, compact closed snakes, straight chains, or spirals. Measured Diagnostics View solved length, link count, pitch, bend, and layout size. Print-Focused Workflow Tune spacing, test clearances, and export clean printable geometry. 🖨️ Printing Advice Print-in-place chains depend heavily on first-layer accuracy and clearance. Use a brim for small chains with limited build-plate contact. Enable variable layer height for smoother steep curves. Inspect the chain carefully in the slicer. Print the Clearance Test before committing to unfamiliar geometry or materials. ChainMaker uses mathematical spacing, envelope, closure, and bend calculations, but extreme custom shapes should still be checked visually before printing. Closed chains have no clasp. For wearable designs, make sure it passes over the hand or head, or use an open chain with your own clasp. Integrated functional clasps may be added in a future update if there is enough interest. ℹ️ Notes For additional guidance and troubleshooting, see the Frequently Asked Questions attached to this post. Versión B — Cara visible contra la placa La pieza se imprime con la cara frontal apoyada directamente sobre la placa , lo que hace que adopte la textura de la superficie de impresión. Esta versión no requiere soportes y ofrece un acabado limpio, ideal para quienes buscan una apariencia pulida sin posprocesado adicional. En este caso, la parte inferior debe quedar así. El modelo TASY lo deberás imprimir en impresoras con 5 filamentos o la nariz en blanco y pintarlo con rotulador acrílico. 🎯 Recomendación de uso Versión A : ideal si prefieres una superficie con relieve, aceptando el trabajo extra de retirar soportes. description: 水果主题便携折扇 安装说明视频： 配色说明： 创作灵感：复刻童年折扇回忆 作品取材于儿时经典层叠圆形纸折扇，依托3D打印技术重塑怀旧物件，赋予老折扇现代设计形态。 以水果横截面作为扇面核心视觉，结合扇子消暑的使用属性，借助热带水果清新甜美的气质，强化清爽氛围感，兼具实用性与创意趣味。 系列包含八款独立水果造型，自带专属图案，色彩搭配丰富，可匹配不同家居风格。 无AMS多色打印机也能制作单色版本 ，仅外观存在差异，功能性能完全相同。 手柄依照对应 水果特质定制专属纹理 ，每款握持手感各不相同； 指尖大小的开关按钮也采用水果造型 ，细节设计呼应整体主题。 机身尺寸适配大人与孩童握持，体积迷你可收纳进裤袋、包包。成品重量约50g，耗材仅60g，长时间手持不易疲惫。 扇体坚固耐用，开合手感顺滑，打印精度出众，参数经过优化，操作简单易上手。 整体全卡扣结构拼装，不用胶水与额外配件。 设计过程分享： 一开始做这把折扇，我以为弄懂结构就很容易成型，结果实操处处碰壁。 想要做出童年那种超小巧的扇子，可 FDM 机器精度有限，没法一味缩小尺寸。只能反复改模型，兼顾小巧体积、免胶卡扣组装和结构牢固度。 受打印平台限制放弃了方形扇面，改用圆形设计。加上水果图案后，打印纹路复杂，折叠很容易开裂，放射纹理的款式更是改了好几版才修好。 原本计划只做三款水果样式，越设计越觉得多款切面都很好看，一路追加到八款。全部利用下班业余时间，整整花了一个月才做完，难度远超预想。 期间还试了很多配色、不同品牌耗材，材质差异带来不少突发打印问题，都逐一调试解决。 这把小扇子耗费了不少心血反复打磨，喜欢的朋友不妨自行打印支持一下。谢谢！

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

description: One customizable OpenSCAD generator for everyday personalized tags: keychains, luggage tags, fridge magnets, screw plates, bin labels, door signs, and desk nameplates. Universal Personalized Tag Generator Pro expands a simple winning keychain label into a broader personal-label generator. Choose a mode, type your text, and generate a practical tag for keys, bags, storage bins, fridge notes, tool panels, doors, desks, and workshop organization. The first build includes seven fast MakerWorld-ready modes: `keychain` , `luggage_tag` , `fridge_magnet` , `screw_plate` , `bin_label` , `door_sign` , and `desk_nameplate` . Each mode has sensible default size, shape, text layout, and mounting, while manual overrides let you tune the width, height, thickness, shape, mount type, and text style. Mounting options include single ring hole, double ring holes, strap slot, blind magnet pockets, screw holes with counterbores, adhesive tape recess, and no-mount plates. The default text style uses raised lettering so color changes near the top layers are easy on a standard FDM printer. Optional text styles include engraved, recessed, and inlay-ready lettering for paint, resin, or filament-fill workflows. The desk nameplate mode prints as a simple support-free wedge with text on the sloped face. Customization Notes - Use `tag_mode` first, then leave `size_preset` , `mount_type` , `text_layout` , and `shape_style` on `mode_default` for a quick printable result. - Leave `color_style` on `raised` for the easiest two-color print with a filament swap near the top layers. - Use `inlay_ready` for deeper lettering pockets that can be filled after printing. - Use `fridge_magnet` or `magnet_pockets` for blind underside magnet pockets; glue magnets in after printing. - Use `screw_plate` or `door_sign` for screw holes with counterbores. - Use `back_side` for simple underside ID text such as phone number, serial number, property label, or emergency info. - Keep very long labels short or reduce the font size for narrow tags.

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.

Make personalized letter beads for friendship bracelets, craft projects, classroom name strings, zipper pulls, gift tags, and keychain accents. This parametric OpenSCAD generator creates a full batch of matching beads with adjustable size, thickness, stringing hole, and per-bead face lettering, so you can generate a complete name/word bracelet instead of downloading each letter as a separate file. Features: - Cube, coin, and barrel bead styles. - Adjustable bead size, thickness, bead count, and spacing. - Up to 12 separate label fields, one per bead. - Horizontal side-stringing hole by default for classic bracelet-bead layouts. - Optional vertical hole mode, offset below the letter, for name-string or tag layouts. - Raised or recessed label text. - Optional back-side label. - Rounded cube corners and optional barrel rib detail. - Cutaway preview mode for checking hole and label depth. The default prints a small `FRIEND` bracelet-bead set with horizontal side-stringing holes. The default 3 mm holes bridge cleanly on normal tuned printers, so it can print without supports while looking more like classic bracelet beads. For bracelet stringing, test your cord/elastic against `hole_diameter` ; different filaments and printers can make small holes tighter than expected. Safety note: these are small parts. Not for children under 3, and not for any use where broken or loose beads could become a choking hazard. Customization Notes - `bead_style` : choose cube, coin, or barrel. - `bead_count` : number of beads in the batch, up to 12. - `bead_size` / `bead_thickness` : bead face size and height. - `hole_diameter` : string/elastic hole size. Increase for fuzzy cord or printers that close small holes. - `hole_orientation` : horizontal is the default for classic side-stringing; vertical is available for top/bottom stringing or tag-style use. - `hole_y_offset` : moves the vertical hole away from the label when vertical mode is selected. - `label_1` through `label_12` : text for each bead. One letter per bead works best; short symbols or numbers also work. - `label_style` : raised lettering is easiest to see; recessed lettering gives a cleaner engraved look. - `show_back_label` : duplicates the label on the back face.

description: Badge reel to show your love of Silence of the Lambs or Buffalo Bill, or maybe it just looks cool. Looks super clean in person. It fits neatly with a readily available and inexpensive badge reel available on amazon or elsewhere (very inexpensive). Generic badge reel pictured is just over 32mm wide. I have found that a few 25mm circles cut out of paper towel or toilet paper help for strong adhesion to the reel. To assemble the reel cover, put a few drops of glue into the cavity where the reel will go. place a few layers of paper towel down and press them so the glue soaks through. Place a few more drops of glue in the center of the paper towel and press down the badge reel. I use more glue on this than I normally do on such a small model, but the paper helps to overcome the difference in the shape of the cavity and the reel itself creating a really solid finished product. In this example I use a small amount of Gold Leaf colored “Rub'n Buff” to highlight the details. a similar effect could be done dry brushing with acrylic paint or even a crayon followed by a little heat to set it in. I have taken this same model and given it a few coats thin of black primer before then applied the rub n buff followed by a coat of clear sealer and the effect is even better, but the pictured model is just the rub n buff.

Premium sunglasses case. There are a few varieties to choose from. They by default have fuzzy skin turned on for parts of it to make it look more proffesional. This summer, I went on several trips. I like to take sunglasses, because they're convenient for driving, and we were in the sun a lot. However, (I have four pairs that I took on the trips) I had to store them in a zip up pocket that I hoped would protect them. It didn't sadly. I stored them in there with books, chargers, devices - anything you'd take on a vacation. I opened up the pocket and there my fancy pink aviators were, bent all out of shape. I had to try to bend them back into shape, and even then they fit too loosely on my head. This is designed to completely prevent things like that from happening. Looks good in almost any color. Here's a few instructions: Magnets You need 10 8x2mm round magnets for this, linked below in the BOM. If you don't want to use that much, just put 6 in; two pairs in the corners, and one in the hole closest to the center. Works very well either way. The magnets should friction fit pretty well but if any are too loose just put a drop of superglue. TPU padding. You can optionally print a TPU pad for the lenses to not get scratched. You don't need it, but it is recommended. I have also included a DXF file if you want to lasercut it out of something else, like cork (for looks), felt, foam, etc. If you slice it yourself, don't forget to turn off the top and bottom layers so it is directly cushioned by the infill. I simulated the case getting smashed in a suitcase by, say a laptop corner or just something. I know that it simulates solid PLA instead of printed, so I tested it with a 15mm cube pushing with 500 lbf of force to make completely sure. With that force it deformed by 2.5~mm . Should be completely fine with whatever you're taking it in! If you have any suggestions just comment!

description: 骨羁・荒墟（Bone Bond・Desolate Ruin） 骨羁・荒墟白瓷戒指，是暗黑先锋雕塑美学与德化高白瓷烧制工艺碰撞诞生的艺术首饰，打破大众对骷髅配饰冰冷粗粝的固有印象，以温润瓷质重构生死艺术。整件首饰以写实人类颅骨为视觉核心，匠人手工精雕颅骨全部细节，深邃眼窝、立体鼻骨、整齐齿列完整复刻人体骨骼肌理，凹凸起伏精准写实，既还原骨骼原生力量感，又不会带来狰狞压迫感。环绕骷髅的镂空结构由仿生掌骨、指骨交错编织而成，一节节骨节轮廓饱满圆润，骨骼线条纵横交错，层层围合形成牢笼框架，如同肉身羁绊困住灵魂，极具故事氛围感。 主材选用顶级德化羊脂白瓷，历经 1300℃高温多次入窑烧制，瓷胎密度紧实坚硬，抗磕碰、耐磨损，釉面呈现柔和细腻的亮白光泽，没有工业塑料的廉价惨白，触感顺滑温润。镂空是整件作品的灵魂，错落的骨骼缝隙让光线自由穿梭，转动戒指时光影不断流转，骨骼的硬朗线条与白瓷的温润质感形成强烈反差，刚柔平衡恰到好处。戒圈做加厚圆弧打磨，保证结构稳固的同时减轻整体重量，长时间佩戴不会硌压手指，内圈全圆角处理，亲肤顺滑。 设计内核探讨束缚与本我的博弈，交错骨骼象征世俗规则、外界标签层层桎梏，居中骷髅代表最真实的自我，寓意挣脱他人定义，接纳完整的自我，拥有直面本心的勇气。穿搭适配度极强，无论是街头高街、机能工装、哥特暗黑穿搭，还是极简黑白通勤风都可以适配，男女皆可佩戴，风格辨识度独一档。不同于金属骷髅配饰容易氧化发黑、触感冷硬，白瓷性质稳定，防水防汗，常年佩戴依旧莹白干净。全程手工修雕，骨骼缠绕走向没有标准化模板，每一枚纹路都具备独一无二的手工痕迹，兼具穿搭装饰价值与小众收藏属性。它拒绝流水线的千篇一律，把哲学思考藏于指尖方寸，酷感内敛高级，小众不易撞款，既是穿搭点睛配饰，也是承载精神态度的微型雕塑。 Bone Bond · Desolate Ruin white porcelain ring is an artistic jewelry born from the collision of avant-garde dark sculptural aesthetics and Dehua high-white porcelain firing craftsmanship. It subverts people’s stereotype of cold and rough skull accessories, reshaping life-and-death art with tender porcelain texture. Centered on a realistic human skull, the ring is manually carved with exquisite details, including deep eye sockets, three-dimensional nasal bones and neat teeth, perfectly restoring physical bone texture. It retains the primitive power of bones without intimidating ferocity. The hollow frame wrapping the skull is woven by bionic metacarpals and phalanges. Full and round knuckles interlace to build a cage, implying the soul trapped by physical bonds and creating rich narrative charm. The tough bone lines contrast sharply with soft porcelain, striking a perfect balance of rigidity and gentleness. The thickened smoothly rounded band ensures structural stability and lightweight comfort, avoiding finger indentation after long wear. Its fully polished inner curve brings skin-friendly experience. The design interprets the game between restriction and inner authenticity. Interlaced bones stand for worldly shackles and external labels, while the central skull symbolizes true self. It encourages wearers to break stereotypes and embrace their whole selves. Unisex and highly versatile, it matches streetwear, techwear, gothic outfits and minimalist daily attires. Unlike metal skull ornaments prone to oxidation and icy touch, porcelain resists sweat and discoloration, keeping milky white permanently. All bones are hand-shaped without mass-produced templates, so every ring bears exclusive carving traces with great collectible value. Bring your favorite football memes to life on your wardrobe! This unique DIY project features the iconic silhouette of Erling Haaland, 3D printed with an ultra-thin thickness of 0.4 mm . How It's Made (PLA+ Method): For this specific shirt, PLA+ was used. Since this filament is tougher to melt, it requires a specific technique combining high heat and immediate pressure: Setup: Lay the t-shirt perfectly flat on a smooth, heat-resistant surface (like floor tiles). Placement: Position the main Haaland design, then carefully place the 2 or 3 small detached pieces that aren't connected to the rest. Protection: Cover the entire design with tightly stretched baking paper. Heating: Use a heat gun to melt the filament onto the fabric through the baking paper. Pressing (The key step): Immediately after heating, firmly press a wooden cutting board directly onto the hot baking paper to force the melted filament into the fabric mesh for a solid bond. ⚠️ Warning: Do not stay in one spot for too long with the heat gun! Heat evenly and keep moving, then press immediately to avoid deforming the plastic. 💡 Pro Tip: Which filament should you use? Standard PLA with a household iron (Possible, but not recommended): You can technically try using regular PLA with a standard iron (no steam) and baking paper, but the result isn't great. The plastic doesn't bond well to the fabric and tends to peel off easily. TPU Filament (The absolute best option): For the best results, we highly recommend using TPU (flexible filament) instead. It works beautifully with a regular household iron (no steam) . When heated, the TPU melts right into the fabric mesh, blending with the textile. This gives you maximum flexibility, a softer feel, and incredible longevity. 🧼 Care Instructions: To ensure your design lasts as long as possible, always wash the t-shirt at a low temperature and inside out .

description: Different Eyeglass Temple Designs This project was born from my passion for 3D printing, which is my favorite hobby. I wanted to create a collection of interchangeable eyeglass temples with different styles, so everyone can choose the design they like best. All temple designs are included in a single project. Simply keep the model you want to print and remove the others. Colors and Materials You can print the temples in a single color or use multiple colors if you have an AMS (or any compatible multi-material system). Feel free to customize them with the filament colors you prefer. The models were designed using measurements taken from my own glasses, and they fit me very well. Since every frame is different, you may need to slightly scale the model to obtain the perfect fit. Print Settings For the best surface finish and logo quality, I recommend: Layer height: 0.10 mm Nozzle: 0.20 mm Assembly To mount the temples to the frame, I used two M3 × 7 mm screws . Depending on your eyeglass frame, you may need slightly shorter or longer screws, so simply choose the length that fits your frame. Filament Recommendation These temples can be printed with PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA , or other suitable materials. PLA works perfectly well and is the easiest material to print. However, because eyeglasses are often left inside a car or exposed to direct sunlight during summer, I personally recommend ABS (or ASA) for their higher heat resistance and better long-term durability. The examples shown in the photos were printed using Bambu ABS Silver and Bambu ABS Green . I also printed one version in Bambu PAHT-CF , which offers excellent rigidity and heat resistance. Support If you have any questions or encounter any problems with the model, feel free to send me a private message. I'll be happy to help. description: A functional, aesthetic charging and display stand based around the Pebble Time 2! Includes an indent for the heart rate sensor and a non-slip TPU 95A foot. HARDWARE This project requires a couple things: Your Pebble magnetic charger. If you don't want to use the one that came with your watch, I have had luck with this one from Amazon . There are a few like this, but if you buy one without the USB C port make sure it has a thin (preferably flat), flexible cable. Right-angle USB-C adapter. If you don't use a charger with an attached cable, you will need one of these. Make sure it is slim. The fitment was modeled after one similar to these from Ugreen . USB-C cable, if you aren't using a charger with one attached. Just use one of the hundreds you have laying around at this point! 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws. Mine came from this set . These are optional, but I like the look of screws instead of using glue and it's easier to take apart. PRINTING TIPS I have carefully painted supports, infill & walls on the included print profiles. There should be no need to tweak them. Ironing is enabled on the Pebble logo to look nice and smooth. This can be tweaked or disabled to your preference. If printing from the step files, note the following: The stand is best printed on its side so that the curves are smooth and the inset on the bottom is accurate. Ensure that your bridging is calibrated and well-tuned Ensure that the widest part of the stand at least is supported; tree supports can angle into the cavity about 10mm while remaining on the build plate and I found that to be sufficient Ensure that the inset at the bottom of the stand for the foot is supported; I had to paint on supports manually since the slicer kept wanting to print that as an overhang. The inlay side (pebble logo) of the watch holder should be printed face down and should not need supports - they're hard to remove. However, the cantilever for the heart rate sensor does need support. Print the stand and foot at 100% infill (or 1000 walls, your preference). This is to ensure they are weighty enough to offset the high weight when the watch is on the stand. Print the foot on a textured PEI plate if using TPU. I recommend 95A TPU or SEBS. The texture on the plate, when applied to the foot, greatly enhances grip. Assembly Print and Gather your parts Insert the charger (with right angle connector if applicable) into the cavity. There is an indent for the lanyard if you do not want to remove it. The lanyard can also be used to add some friction by sliding it underneath the magnetic charger. Plug the cord in and feed it through the cavity in the stand. Slide the stand onto the watch holder. Fitment is tight, so a small amount of force may be necessary. It may be easiest to slide the watch holder onto the stand, feeding the charger into the cavity as you do so. Secure 4x M3x25mm self-tapping screws into the four holes on the side of the stand. Screw them all the way in so their heads are flush to ensure that they have secured the holder to the stand. Click the logo inlay into place. It should not require glue, but a little dab does not hurt. Insert the foot into the inset in the bottom. The small peg should align to the small hole next to the cord cutout. Do not glue this in or the cord will be impossible to remove later. Fill your coffee!

description: Turn your favorite design into a unique 3D T-shirt 👕🖨️ These thin and flexible 3D prints are designed to be heat-transferred directly onto fabric using a household iron. The result is a durable and eye-catching 3D design that combines modern 3D printing technology with fashion. Instructions 🛠️👕 Download the model and open it in Bambu Studio 💻 Print the model using the recommended settings and carefully remove it from the build plate. ⚠️ Handle with care — the model is extremely thin (approximately 0.3 mm) and may tear or deform if bent too aggressively. Prepare your ironing area: Place the T-shirt on an ironing board or a flat heat-resistant surface. Set your iron to a very high temperature (almost maximum heat, without steam) 🔥 Allow the iron to fully preheat before starting. Position the printed model on the desired area of the T-shirt and cover it with baking/parchment paper 📄 Apply firm pressure with the preheated iron for 15–20 seconds. For larger designs, move the iron slowly and evenly to ensure the entire model receives sufficient heat. Maintain consistent pressure throughout the process. ⏱️ Allow the area to cool for a few seconds, then carefully remove the paper. ✅ The model should remain attached to the fabric while the paper lifts away easily. (Optional) Turn the T-shirt inside out and iron the reverse side of the applied design for an additional 5–10 seconds to improve adhesion. 👕✨ Important ⚠️ Always use the iron at a very high temperature (near maximum setting) and with the steam function turned off. Insufficient heat or pressure may result in poor adhesion to the fabric. Test on a small area first if using delicate or heat-sensitive fabrics. Care Instructions 🧼 Wash garments at temperatures not exceeding 50°C (122°F). Turn the T-shirt inside out before washing whenever possible. Avoid bleach and aggressive washing programs. Do not tumble dry at high temperatures. ⚠️ Washing or drying at excessive temperatures may cause the 3D print to loosen or peel from the fabric over time.
