Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast round ornaments with a pumpkin design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 6.5cm diameter with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 6.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier. This version has an additional larger slot in the print with a removable insert to stop plaster from leaking during casting. Remove the insert once you're ready to demould the plaster, then the added flexibility will allow the print to pop right off!

description: Parametrische Kabeldurchführungen & Kippschalter-Panel Dieses Set enthält individuell anpassbare Montageplatten für Kabeldurchführungen und Miniatur-Kippschalter. Die Modelle eignen sich für Elektronikgehäuse, Maschinenverkleidungen, Steuerpulte, Werkstattinstallationen, Modellbau und zahlreiche DIY-Projekte. Alle Platten besitzen eine saubere, technische Gestaltung mit abgerundeten Ecken, einer umlaufenden Fase und versenkten Befestigungsbohrungen. Die flache Rückseite ermöglicht eine einfache Platzierung auf dem Druckbett. Parametrische Kabeldurchführungsplatte Die Kabeldurchführungsplatte kann mit bis zu zehn individuell einstellbaren Kabelöffnungen erzeugt werden. Jede Öffnung kann unabhängig aktiviert, deaktiviert und in ihrem Durchmesser angepasst werden. Je nach Anzahl der verwendeten Öffnungen und den gewählten Außenabmessungen ordnet das Modell die Kabeldurchführungen automatisch in einer oder zwei Reihen an. Dabei können innerhalb einer Platte sowohl gleich große als auch unterschiedlich große Öffnungen verwendet werden. Um jede Kabelöffnung befindet sich ein erhöhter Verstärkungskranz. Dieser stabilisiert die Öffnung, schützt die Plattenkante und sorgt für eine saubere Kabelführung. Der Übergang zwischen Kranz und Grundplatte ist abgeschrägt und für einen stützmaterialarmen Druck optimiert. Anpassbare Eigenschaften Breite und Höhe der Platte Dicke der Grundplatte Anzahl der Kabelöffnungen individueller Durchmesser jeder Öffnung automatische Anordnung in einer oder zwei Reihen gleich große oder unterschiedlich große Öffnungen erhöhte Verstärkungskränze abgerundete und gefaste Außenkontur versenkte Befestigungsbohrungen in den Ecken Die Platte eignet sich für einzelne Leitungen, Kabelbündel, Schläuche und andere runde Durchführungen. Nicht benötigte Öffnungen können einfach deaktiviert werden. Parametrisches Kippschalter-Panel Das Kippschalter-Panel ist für kompakte Schalter mit rundem Gewindehals vorgesehen. Die Schalter werden von vorne durch die runden Öffnungen eingesetzt und anschließend mit ihrer Befestigungsmutter am Panel fixiert. Die Anzahl der Schalter, der Durchmesser der Öffnungen und die Abstände zwischen den einzelnen Positionen können an das jeweilige Projekt angepasst werden. Dadurch lassen sich sowohl kompakte Bedienfelder als auch längere Schalterreihen erstellen. Anpassbare Eigenschaften Breite und Höhe des Panels Dicke der Montageplatte Anzahl der Schalterpositionen Durchmesser der runden Schalteröffnungen Abstand zwischen den Schaltern gleichmäßige Positionierung innerhalb des Panels abgerundete und gefaste Außenkontur versenkte Befestigungsbohrungen in den Ecken Das Panel eignet sich für Steuerungen, Netzteile, Fahrzeuge, Modellbauprojekte, Prüfgeräte, Werkstattmaschinen und individuelle Elektronikgehäuse. Hinweise Die dargestellten Kabel, Schalter und Schrauben dienen lediglich der Veranschaulichung und sind nicht Bestandteil der Druckdateien. Die Modelle sind als universelle Montageplatten ausgelegt. Für sicherheitsrelevante Anwendungen, Netzspannung, Außenbereiche oder Installationen mit besonderen Anforderungen sollten geeignete und zugelassene Komponenten verwendet werden.

Next, squeeze the front of the magwell and do the same thing, making sure the front edges are also inside the channels. description: This is a 45-degree directional return jet designed for above-ground pools with a 32 mm water outlet, such as compatible Bestway and Intex systems. The original pool outlet sends the filtered water straight ahead. This replacement nozzle redirects the water at approximately 45 degrees, allowing the flow to be aimed downward or sideways to improve water circulation inside the pool. The model consists of two printable parts: Directional outlet nozzle Threaded retaining ring It replaces only the original water outlet nozzle. The remaining original pool fitting, seals and internal components are reused. The nozzle can be rotated before tightening the retaining ring, allowing you to choose the direction of the water flow. Compatibility Tested on a Bestway pool with a 32 mm outlet. It should also be compatible with Intex and other above-ground pools that use the same style of 32 mm return outlet, although small differences may exist between models. Please compare the original fitting and dimensions before printing. Printing Recommended material: PETG PETG is recommended because the part will be exposed to water, sunlight and outdoor temperatures. No supports required Print both parts in the orientation provided Recommended layer height: 0.20 mm Recommended walls: 4 Recommended infill: 25–40% A brim can be used if your printer has adhesion problems Print the threaded ring slowly for better thread quality Assembly Turn off the pool pump. Remove the original directional outlet nozzle. Keep the original pool fitting and rubber seals in place. Insert the printed directional nozzle. Rotate it to the desired position. Tighten it using the printed retaining ring. Turn the pump back on and check for leaks. Do not overtighten the threaded ring. Hand tightening should be enough. Important This model has been tested on my own Bestway 32 mm pool outlet. Always check the connection for leaks after installation. The model is not intended for high-pressure plumbing systems. If you successfully test it on another Bestway or Intex pool model, please leave a comment with the exact model so the compatibility list can be expanded.

Powerful printable foam dart sniper pistol blaster capable of up to 250FPS These are alternative cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50, with a new more tactical design. This listing contains all parts needed for the Zinc .50, including unchanged ones. This listing includes new parts for the following Zinc .50 configurations: 160mm barrel compact front, 160mm barrel BCAR front, and 205mm barrel BCAR front. These parts require no hardware changes and so use the original hardware kit for the Zinc .50. See here for the original Zinc .50 model listing (check out all the amazing makes from everyone!). About the Zinc .50 blaster: Technically all standard Nerf darts are ‘50 caliber’ as the darts have a diameter of half an inch, though the Zinc .50 brings the essence of 50 caliber into foam dart hand-cannon format. The Zinc .50 is a high-powered, mag fed (7-13 dart capacity) foam dart springer pistol blaster capable of up to 250 feet-per-second muzzle velocity for 205mm barrel configurations, and up to 230 FPS for 160mm barrel configurations. If you have no reference for those velocities - don't hit your tv or it may break. It may also leave divots in your drywall. Everything You Need To Build Your Own Purchase a hardware kit: Hardware Kits can be found here. Discounted 'Duel Bundle' (2x Hardware Kits) for this blaster can be found here. Discounted 3-Blaster Hardware kit Bundle pack (Zc Aus, Znc Aus, Zinc .50) can be found here. The hardware kit can make any blaster configuration, just choose your barrel length! Affordable international shipping available, fast and tracked! Please note: Hardware kit sales support me in developing upcoming designs. They include several custom-machined parts, not just off-the-shelf parts. They are priced for an order frequency that I can keep fast dispatch times up with while also remaining competitive with similar kits. Download the print files, or Bambu Studio 3MF with all parts and preset settings (contains one of every part, remove unused parts for your configuration, duplicate parts as desired), from this model listing. Download the print and assembly guide here . Buy some half-length darts if you don't already own any, here are some links: US - Frontline Foam , OutOfDarts EU - Blaster Time AU - Blaster Tech Although the files include some printable tools to make assembly easier, you will also need some basic common tools for assembly, see the assembly guide linked above. Lubricant is included in the hardware kit. Demo Video Warning Note This blaster has a large spring with a somewhat heavy prime weight. Said spring may present danger if the blaster is not assembled, used, or cared for correctly. This is your responsibility. Information on correct assembly, use and care is provided in the assembly guide linked above. If you are looking for a blaster with a lighter prime and less powerful spring: check out the more compact Znc Aus / Znc Aus Cosmetic Part Variants , or even the ultra-compact Zc Aus . IMPORTANT NOTE - PRINT IN BRIGHT COLOURS Due to it's design this blaster must be printed in bright colours and with an orange tip so it is clearly visible as a toy, for your safety and other's. Use responsibly and in responsible settings. Details Textured Grip Note The textured grip shown on the frame part in the images is done with fuzzy skin fill-painting in the slicer. The grip sections are bordered by a small deboss which allows them to be easily fill-painted with the fuzzy skin fill-painting tool. The settings used for fuzzy skin in the blasters in the images are 0.18 thickness and 0.25 point distance. The Bambu Studio 3MF file already has the fuzzy skin set up with these settings. Variants A bearing scar (BCAR) uses rings of flanged bearings with each at a slight angle to impart spin on the dart as it exits the barrel, vastly increasing accuracy with little effect on fps. These new cosmetic parts for the Zinc .50 can make 3 total configurations (all shown in the cover image), two of which include a 9-bearing (3 rings) BCAR. The hardware kit can make any configuration, just choose your desired barrel length (all hardware kits come with 9x BCAR pins and bearings): 160mm barrel with a compact front (no BCAR) Up to 230FPS Not very accurate due to lack of BCAR but fun in that it's super powerful for it's size 160mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 230FPS Good balance of size and accuracy/power 205mm barrel with a 9 bearing BCAR Up to 250FPS Proper sniper pistol configuration, longer barrel for maximum FPS and BCAR for accuracy Zinc .50 Additions and Changes vs Ziiiinc and Zinc The Zinc .50 is based on the Ziiiinc by Misplaced Moose, and is modified and sold with his permission, though it includes many changes and upgrades including a slightly larger diameter plunger tube, a longer barrel, many customisable part options allowing for many different configurations, revised hardware, and modified/remodeled part designs and tolerances in the interest of performance, ease of assembly, and aesthetics. Hardware changes include a tighter-toleranced aluminum plunger tube over the original polycarbonate one, refined closed-end springs for all springs to fix issues of the original Zinc such as the stiff catch and weak mag release, double O-rings on all seals, lubricant oil included, tapping screws replacing machine screws with nuts (caused part splitting or the nuts would turn in place, making removal impossible), and more. See images for further details. Assembly Assembly is relatively straightforward. The assembly guide is detailed and includes troubleshooting steps for common issues. Unlike the original Zinc 2.0, no excessive sanding is required to get parts to fit and function. A dimensionally accurate printer such as a Prusa or Bambu model is recommended for easy assembly. See the print guide for printing tips. Care and Safety Print in bright colours and use in responsible locations/settings. Do not leave the blaster outside under sunlight or in a car that may get hot when not in use. Do not leave the blaster primed when not in use as this will fatigue the main spring and other parts. Use responsibly. Do not aim at eyes or face. Eye protection for skirmishing is essential. Not recommended for use by young children. Note Like the Ziiiinc, the Zinc .50 is an unofficial descendant of the Zinc 2.0 blaster by 118 Design.

model_name: BC-6 Cooler – Ice Pack for the BC-6
description: The BC-6 Cooler is a reusable ice pack designed specifically for the BC-6 can carrier. It sits between the two rows of cans, while the curved sides follow the shape of the cans to provide a large contact area and more effective cooling. The cooler is filled with water through the removable plug and then placed in the freezer. Features Designed specifically for the BC-6 carrier Cools cans on both sides Refillable and reusable Large contact area against the cans Removable plug for easy filling Can be stored ready to use in the freezer Designed for straightforward 3D printing and assembly How to Fill It Carefully remove the filling plug using the correct Allen key (8mm). Make sure the inside is clean. Fill the cooler approximately 80–85% with ordinary water . Leave at least 15% empty space because water expands when it freezes. Reinstall the plug and tighten it gently. Do not overtighten it, as this may damage the threads or printed part. Wipe the cooler dry and check it carefully for leaks. For the first leak test, place it on a paper towel before freezing. Do not fill it completely. A fully filled container may crack or split when the water freezes. How to Use It Freeze the cooler for at least 8–12 hours , preferably overnight. Place the frozen cooler in the centre of the BC-6 carrier. Place three cans on each side of the cooler. After use, wipe it clean and return it to the freezer. For the best cooling performance, both the cans and the cooler should already be cold before being placed in the carrier. Important Information Ordinary water is recommended. Avoid unnecessary additives. Check regularly for cracks, damage or leaks. Do not use the cooler if it is damaged. The contents are not intended for drinking. Wash by hand using lukewarm water. Do not place it in a dishwasher or microwave, and avoid hot water. A watertight print and a properly sealed filling plug are required. PETG is generally more suitable than PLA for repeated freezer use.

description: Click the Customize button to use this Cutter maker! Built for potters who want repeatable, precise mug sizing without performing the math themselves!! Stop eyeballing paper templates. This tool calculates the exact flat pattern for a tapered or straight-sided mug, compensates for your specific clay's shrinkage, and outputs a ready-to-print cutter - sharp blade, comfortable press rim, and built-in bracing so it holds its shape under real hand pressure. How it works Enter your target top diameter, bottom diameter, and height (or just tell it the volume you want - in mL or oz - and it'll solve the height for you, with headroom left below the rim so your coffee doesn't spill). Punch in your clay body's shrinkage percentage, and the tool mathematically "unrolls" the cone shape into the precise 2D pattern, then oversizes it so the fired mug comes out at your intended size. Features True cone-development math (not an approximation) - works for tapered mugs and straight-sided cylinder mugs alike Shrinkage compensation for any clay body (stoneware, porcelain, whatever you're working with) Set height directly, or calculate it from a target fill volume (mL or fl oz) with adjustable headroom Sharp cutting blade with a durable (non-fragile) edge, tapering up to a flared rim you can press with your palm Structural cross-ribs keep the loop rigid so it doesn't flex out of shape mid-cut Cutter has clean, rounded corners, no print artifacts Prints rim-down for the strongest bed adhesion, auto-centered and auto-rotated to fit your plate Optional bed-size check with an unmissable warning if your mug size won't fit your printer Quick start Set your top and bottom diameter and height (or switch to volume mode) Enter your clay's shrinkage % from the spec sheet Generate, print, and press into a rolled slab Trim the seam, join, and you've got a perfectly sized mug blank Want more control? Open the Advanced sections in the customizer — blade sharpness, rim grip width, rib count/bracing, and the bed-fit checker all live there. The four basics up top get you a great mug fast, but the advanced tabs are where you fine-tune it exactly to your studio and printer. Notes before you print Ignore the build plate graphic shown in the preview - it's a fixed generic size and doesn't reflect your actual printer or update with your settings. Changing a value doesn't update the model automatically - after adjusting any option, click Generate to see it reflected in the preview. Once it looks right, click Download in the top right to get your 3MF or STL. Want a real fit check for your printer? Turn on the bed-size checker in Advanced - Printer Bed Size Check - it's off by default. Print settings PETG or PLA, 100% infill on the walls (they're already thin), no supports needed. A taller cutter wall (default 20mm) makes it easier to keep your cut vertical through a thick slab. Got changes or suggestions? Want another parameter parametized? Drop me a comment below and I will see what I can do! Enjoy!

Before you print: An AMS is required. You must have PETG and PLA, or any two filaments that don't stick together, or soluble support material. This does not fit on an A1 mini and rescaling will yield unpredictable (and often undesirable) flight characteristics compared to the original size. This boomerang does indeed work, but boomerang throwing is not easy. If this is your first time throwing this sort of boomerang, expect to take at least 1-2 hours of practice before you have even one successful catch. Printing Make sure you choose the correct file. I have made a different print profile for the left-handed version so that my signature isn't mirrored. Set the green material to whatever PETG you have, and the white material to whatever PLA you have. The bottom of the boomerang is designed to print my signature in a different colour of PETG. If you only have one colour of PETG, use the fill tool under the paint menu to make the whole boomerang one colour. Make sure your buildplate has been cleaned with soap and water, and that bed-levelling is enabled to ensure optimal adhesion. VERY IMPORTANT: While the printer is printing the purge line , start to peel it off before the whole purge line has printed . The boomerang will be printed over the purge line if it is not removed immediately, and you will have to try again. When finished printing, peel off the supports using the little tabs that stick out, and then pop out the chamber supports by poking an object through the hole on the other side with something like a screwdriver. Optional: Sand or scrape the edges and the ‘transitions’ to and from the undercut as they may have a slightly bumpy edge. Safety: This boomerang is not a toy. Treat it as a piece of sporting equipment that has the capacity to injure or even kill very young children or small animals if you throw within the vicinity of others. This boomerang can be thrown without much power, but please keep in mind that it is designed to be thrown in excess of 75mph (120km/h) and is a spinning piece of solid plastic. I do not take any responsibility for any injuries this may cause if thrown carelessly. If you are actually going to use this boomerang for fast-catch (5 consecutive throws and catches, timed), I recommend wearing safety glasses and a thick glove on your non-dominant hand. Restrain any hair that may block your eyesight and wear sunglasses if sunlight hinders your ability to see the boomerang in flight. I would recommend throwing this boomerang during wind speeds of under 10km/h, and never during wind speeds of 15km/h or more. About this Boomerang I am very proud to present this boomerang as I truly believe that it is currently my magnum opus - my best work to date. This current design has taken about 5 iterations to perfect, and is now my go-to for practicing fast-catch and endurance. Previously, I had thought it would be impossible to incorporate chambering and undercut, something that is very common on hand-made boomerangs into 3D printed boomerangs due to the limitations of supports and the very steep angles required. I worked around this by designing custom supports in my CAD software, and had them print in a filament that wouldn't stick to the main boomerang. I print my boomerangs in PETG, so PLA was the obvious choice for the support material, which ended up giving me very clean bottom surfaces. Many people would probably already have these two filaments on hand too, which is a plus. This boomerang also features a stepped airfoil on the trailing edge of each wing which was inspired by Denis Suprana's ‘Turbo’ boomerang. From my testing, I found that it reduced the likelihood of the boomerang swooping up during the end of the flight, but the exact reason for why is still unclear. Range: 19-23 metres (adjustable by twisting wings - angle of attack) Flight time: around 3.4 seconds, calculated from one of my fast-catch rounds Below is a video of the boomerang being tested, thrown by Grant Perry, captain of the Australian Boomerang team. Throwing Guide Pinch grip the boomerang as shown: Throw at shoulder height and straight forward or just very slightly up (as seen in the video). Use your wrist and the whipping motion from your elbow to give the boomerang spin. It is very important to keep the boomerang vertical, i.e. the plane of rotation is perpendicular to the ground when you throw, and never throw sidearm. If you have a weaker throw and/or there is little to no wind, throw with about 5 to 10 degrees of layover (lean the boomerang towards the right rather than releasing it completely vertical). Adjusting throwing direction for better accuracy: Like with most boomerangs, throwing 45 degrees to the right of the wind is a good starting point, but this must still be adjusted most of the time. With a fast-catch in very light wind, you can try throwing directly into the wind, or about 10 degrees to the right of it (a so-called ‘backdoor’ approach). Adjust your throwing direction with the following guide (flip left/right if you are left handed but not front/behind): Lands in front of you or to your right . Turn to the right a little bit. Lands behind you or to your left . Turn to the left a little bit. Simply repeat this until you can catch the boomerang while standing from the same spot or until you are satisfied with the accuracy. You will have to adjust this every time the wind changes direction. Enjoy the boomerang and I wish you many happy returns! Throw safely and responsibly :)

description: Important! For optimal results, see the Customization Guide below Filament Zero The last baseplate you'll ever need. If you are doing Gridfinity, you'll need baseplates that are: standard: compatible with standard Gridfinity bins practical: reliably prints on all Bambu printers (0.4mm nozzle, PLU) strong: holds bins securely in place & stand up to 100s of bin take-outs and drop-ins If you care about maximum efficiency, or just want to save a buck, you'll need Filament Zero: First-principles, ground-up re-engineered, endgame Gridfinity baseplate system Up to 10x lighter than standard Gridfinity baseplates (0.133g/tile) Up to 12x faster than standard Gridfinity baseplates (18.8s/tile) Filament Zero comes in three models. Whatever your needs, one of these Filament Zero models is the most efficient baseplate you can print. Full stop: ultralight Net (0.133g, 18.8s/tile) semi-rigid Tape (0.295g, 33.4s/tile) rigid Beam (0.460g, 66.1s/tile) Print up to 7,500 tiles per KG at over 190 tiles per hour . Up to 2x lighter and 2.7x faster than anything else on MakerWorld (July 2026). Features Filament Zero is designed to save you money and time: Impossibly light & fast: not 0.1g more than absolutely necessary & it'll be done before you notice it started Choose from 3 strength options: flexible Net, semi-rigid Tape and rigid Beam Sparse Gridfinity - beyond impossibly light & fast: halve your print time and filament again with sparse baseplates Filament Zero lets you create any gridfinity layout you need effortlessly: Interlocking: strong baseplate interlocking system Any Custom Grid Size: set any width and length (half-unit increments) Built-In, Custom Drawer Spacers: add drawer-fit spacers to any side (mm increments) Any Custom Shape: Ls, circles, triangles, etc… Powerful Multi Baseplate Generator: all the plates you need to cover any area in one click Four Filament Zero Models Filament Zero comes in four models to meet all your baseplate needs. There are trade-offs between model weight and model strength. During design, I realized there were three main tradeoff points for various use cases. Rather than making one model to meet everybody's needs, I made three main models to address the three main optimal weight strength trade-offs. The fourth model, FZBeam+ is an interlocking vs aesthetics & time trade-off. FZ Model Quick Selection Guide There are two main decisions you need to make to choose your model: Strength? How rigid and strong do you need your baseplates to be? Flexible : FZNet+ (lightest) X-Y rigid : FZTape+ (balanced) X-Y-Z rigid : FZBeam / FZBeam+ (strongest) Interlocking? Do you prefer to have your baseplates fully interlocked? The “+” in the model name indicates interlocking. Yes: FZNet+ , FZTape+ or FZBeam+ No: FZNet+ , FZTape+ or FZBeam About the Models FZ Net+ (lightest, flexible) — Think fisherman's net. Choose this if you want the lightest, fastest option and you are going to fully fill your grid with bins. The primary structural requirement for baseplates is to hold your bins together. Net does exactly that and nothing more… at 190 tiles per hour and 7,500 tiles per kilogram . Nearly 2x the tiles per kilogram and 2.7x the tiles per hour of the lightest base on MakerWorld, of any kind. FZ Tape+ (optimal, X-Y rigid) — Semi-rigid: rigid in the X/Y plane when placed on a flat surface, flexible in Z. The best overall performance. Strong in all the ways that matter yet still unbelievably fast and lightweight to print. It's in the same weight class as the best flexible base on MakerWorld, yet is strong and prints 1.5x faster . FZ Beam (strongest, X-Y-Z rigid) — Fully rigid, strong and the most like classic gridfinity-like styling. To me, this is the most aesthetically pleasing lightweight model anywhere while also being the most efficient rigid base on MakerWorld: 1.7x more tiles per kilogram and 1.5x more tiles per hour than the previous rigid record holder. FZ Beam+ (FZ Beam + Interlocking) – For slightly more print time, but about the same weight, you can print FZ-Beam plates with full interlocking capabilities. How strong does a baseplate actually need to be? Step back and ask what a gridfinity baseplate actually does: it holds your bins in place. Once bins are seated and the plate is resting on a flat surface, the surface provides all the vertical support. Gravity holds everything down. The only job left for the baseplate is resisting horizontal forces: keeping bins from sliding apart when you push, pull, and rummage. Structurally, that's a tension-and-shear problem in the plane of the plate, not a stiffness problem. That insight is what makes the three regimes possible: Net takes the insight to its logical conclusion. Like a fisherman's net, it only resists tension. On a flat surface with bins seated, that's genuinely all you need, and it's why Net can be so radically light. The trade-off: it has essentially no rigidity of its own. It's a conforming skeleton, not a structure. Handle it empty and it flops; that's the point. Tape adds in-plane rigidity. Sitting on a flat surface, it's rigid in X and Y: bins stay locked in their grid, and the plate keeps its shape as you load and unload. It still flexes in Z, so it conforms to slightly uneven surfaces and pops out of drawers easily. For most real-world use, this is the sweet spot: everything a baseplate must do rigidly, it does rigidly. Beam is rigid in all directions, the classical gridfinity experience. It resists twisting and bending even when picked up and feels like a solid foundation in the hand. If you move plates around with bins on them, or your surface isn't flat, or you simply want the familiar feel, Beam is the one, and it's still lighter and faster than any other rigid base on MakerWorld. The progression is simple: each step up adds rigidity in a new direction, and costs filament and time. Pick the regime that matches how you actually use your grid. Aesthetics (for the few seconds you'll see it) Let's be honest: a baseplate spends its life hidden under bins. Once your grid is loaded, you'll never see it. So Net and Tape make no apologies for looking like what they are: pure function, though beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Beam is the exception. Its strength comes from triangles, arranged to maximize strength per gram as printed, and a key innovation was removing all the rounded, extended parts of the original gridfinity profile: they serve no mechanical purpose and dramatically slow down printing. What's left is a faceted, multi-triangle surface that looks almost prismatic. The goal was always strength per weight; the looks are what optimization happens to look like. The Interlock System Need your baseplates locked together? No sliding, no drifting — a single unified grid before a single bin goes down. We've got you covered. The system itself was a happy accident. In stripping out every gram of unnecessary filament, the corners emptied out since the bins never touch them. That empty corner space turned out to be the natural home for an interlocking cap. Net and Tape became interlocking the moment I designed the cap; the only real work was creating Beam+, the interlocking variant of Beam. The result: small caps that snap into the corners where plates meet, resisting both tension and shear. They print in minutes by the dozen, and every interlocking plate is compatible with every other, so you can mix and match Net+, Tape+, and Beam+ freely in one locked grid. Interlocks also unlock more advanced custom shapes: while the customizer handles basic shapes like Ls, circles, triangles etc, shapes with a holes or a complex perimeters may need to be printed in two or more pieces. The interlock system then lets you connect those parts together to form a solid whole. Filament Zero Performance Weight: Filament is Money How much filament do you need to complete your Gridfinity baseplate job? One way to answer that is to figure out the average weight per tile for a particular gridfinity base plate. Filament Zero is so light, though. (down to 0.133g/tile ), that it's hard to compare this way. Instead, I've started comparing models by how many tiles can you get out of a kilogram of filament: Tiles per Kilogram or TpKG. Speed: Time is our most precious resource I don't know about you, but I hate waiting for 3D prints to complete. To me, print speed is even more important than filament use, though the two go hand in hand. Though I aggressively optimized every print profile, I did not change the print speed settings. That means you can probably use Sport Mode or even Ludacris Mode to print these in even less time (not tested!). However, These models already print so fast that the final print time is dominated by the printer's prep time. Performance by The Numbers Models Type 4x4 print weight 4x4 print time (*) 6x6 print weight 6x6 print time (*) Tiles /kG Tiles /Hr Filament Zero Net+ flexible, interlocking 2.29g 5.5m 4.8g 11.3m 7,500 191 Filament Zero Tape+ X-Y-rigid, interlocking 4.88g 9.5m 10.6g 20.1m 3,387 108 Filament Zero Beam X-Y-Z-rigid 7.68g 17.5m 16.6g 39.7m 2,173 54 Filament Zero Beam+ X-Y-Z-rigid, interlocking 7.91g 19.6m 16.9g 43.2m 2,128 50 3DMM Baseplates v1 X-Y-Z-rigid 13.95g 16.3m 29.8g 42.0m 1,208 51 Customization Guide Your drawer isn't 4x4. Nobody's is. The whole point of gridfinity is a system that fits your space — and stock rectangular baseplates almost never do. The customizer is where Filament Zero goes from "efficient baseplate" to "the exact baseplate your drawer has been waiting for": any size, half-unit precision, spacers for a perfect friction fit, custom shapes for odd corners, even auto-generated plate sets for big areas. Beginner Customization Guide: Pick a model, Pick a size → Download & Print Start Customizing: Click “Customize” below the print profiles Select the “Single Baseplate” option Look for the customization options in the Customize panel, usually on the left. Pick your Filament Zero Model: In the Customize panel, the Model dropdown chooses which base style to build: Beam — rigid, classic feel (choose Beam+ if you plan to interlock multiple plates) Tape+ — semi-rigid: holds bins firmly, flexes to lift out of drawers Net+ — ultralight and flexible: absolute minimum filament and print time Set your size: Under Grid , set columns (squares wide) and rows (squares deep). A gridfinity square is 42mm, so a 4x4 plate is 168x168mm. Generate: Click “Generate” and after few moments, you'll see your model in the preview. Download: See the Download and Print Guide below That's it. A custom-sized baseplate in under a minute, no modeling required. Parametric Model Maker Download & Print Guide Question: “Why are my custom FZ prints way slower and use way more filament than claimed?” Answer: The MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker doesn't support all the print-profile controls Filament Zero needs. Here's how to use the customizer AND get FZ's full performance: Customize & Export you Filament Zero Baseplate(s) as STL Customize as you like (Beginner Customization Guide above or Features Guide below) Click Download (top right) When it asks for 3MF vs STL: Select STL! Download and Open Matching Filament Zero Base Print Profile On this page, select one of the base profiles that match your model choice (Net+, Tape+, Beam or Beam+) Click “open in Bambu studio” to download and open it. Delete the existing objects (Edit → Delete All) Set the Printer to match your Printer Save (optional): You can re-use this file and skip Step 2 in the future. Import your Custom STL into the optimized Filament Zero Print Profile Add in your custom STL (File → Import → STL - or just drag the file into Bambu Studio) IMPORTANT if your STL has more than one baseplate: Click the “Split to Objects” icon (with your STL selected) then press “A” to auto-arrange objects across all plates (see Multi Baseplate Print Prep below) NOW you can print with maximum efficiency. I wish this was easer. You should be able to just download the 3MF and have it work perfectly. I'll be petitioning MakerWorld to better support advanced 3MF print profiles in the Parametric Model Maker. Features Guide Sparse Gridfinity Bigger project? Bigger savings. Sparse mode removes inner geometry, creating 84x84mm cells wherever they fit — halving material and doubling print speed on top of everything above. For larger gridfinity layouts, and especially larger trays, this is all you need. Net+ in sparse mode approaches 20,000 standard squares per kilogram and nearly 500 squares per hour . But the sweet spot is Tape+ at 7,692/kg and 271/h: the extra rigidity is the right compromise for a sparse layout while keeping incredible efficiency. Run a few test prints and experiment with your layout. Model with Sparse Layout Type 6x6 print weight 6x6 print time (*) Tiles /kG Tiles /Hr Filament Zero Net+ Sparse flexible, interlocking 1.9g 4.6m 18,848 473 Filament Zero Tape+ Sparse X-Y-rigid, interlocking 4.7g 8.0m 7,692 271 Filament Zero Beam Sparse X-Y-Z-rigid 8.8g 15.4m 4,110 140 Filament Zero Beam+ Sparse X-Y-Z-rigid, interlocking 8.9g 17.2m 4036 126 3DMM Baseplates v1 X-Y-Z-rigid 29.8g 42.0m 1,208 51 Reduce your print times and filament even further with Sparse Gridfinity Drawer Spacers Nobody likes a gridfinity that slides around the drawer. And nobody likes printing separate spacers that pop out, drift, and rattle either. Print your spacers as part of your baseplate : add them to any of the four sides, in 1mm increments, for a snug fit that locks your whole grid in place. Add spacers to any side in MM increments Custom Shapes Drawers aren't always rectangles. Corners, notches, angled walls — real spaces have odd shapes, and your baseplate should fit them. Remove squares from the left and right of any row, in any configuration, to create nearly any shape you need. And if the shape configurator can't do it, split it in two: print two plates and join them with the interlock system. Create Custom Shapes by Removing Squares Multi Baseplate Generator Covering a whole drawer, shelf, or workbench? Skip the math. Instead of counting gridfinity squares, just enter your layout's width and depth in millimeters and Filament Zero generates exactly the baseplates you need. Pick your printer from the list and it automatically knows your build plate size — so usually it's just: pick your printer, pick your model, set your area, go. Fine-tuning options are there when you need them. Filament Zero already saves you printer time; this saves your time too, and if you're printing a lot of gridfinity, total time saved is what actually matters. Automatically generate all the plates you need for your area. Just specify the width and depth in MM, FZ takes care of the rest. Multi Baseplate Print Prep After you imported your customized, multi baseplate STL into the optimized print profile, it'll look like the screenshot below. There is an icon on the top with an “O” in it. That's the “split to objects” icon. Click it: Select “Split to Objects” Once you've split it into objects, press “A” and Bambu Slicer's auto-arrange will optimize your plates: Press “A” to auto arrange *: Times are based on the Bambu Slicer A1 “Model printing time” for 6x6 baseplates, 0,4mm nozzle.

SIMPLE . FLYING . FUN Motte RC is a compact two-channel RC biplane designed for relaxed flying on small fields. Smaller and more agile than Hummel RC , it trades a little speed for improved maneuverability and better stability in light wind. Its lightweight modular construction is durable, quick to print and requires little material, while the adjustable wing position makes CG and pitch tuning simple. The model has no movable control surfaces: altitude is controlled by total motor thrust, and turns are performed through differential thrust between the two wing-mounted motors. Motte RC is part of a growing series of simple 2-channel RC aircraft. Each model shares the same accessible control concept while offering a different configuration, appearance and flight character. Motte RC continues the ideas of WingStar , COMET , Wespe , SkyStar , DragonFly and Hummel RC in a compact, vintage-inspired and practical RC model made to fly often. Key Features Control: 2-channel differential thrust Motors: 2 × brushed motors Battery: 1S LiPo Adjustable wing position for CG and pitch tuning Recommended conditions: calm weather or light breeze Suitable for small outdoor fields Why Motte RC? Quick and material-efficient to print Simple modular assembly Easy, Beginners' friendly, two-channel control Replaceable and easy-to-reprint parts Mix and match selected parts from Hummel RC, WingStar, Wespe and COMET to create your own configurations More compatible parts and modular configurations are planned for future updates. 1 - Model Datasheet Wingspan: 346 mm Length: 293 mm Wing chord: 60 mm RC Transmitter and receiver: 2Channel 2.4G FX803 J3 (or equal), link here Battery: 3.7v, 220 mAh, Molex 51005 connector (or equal), link here Motors and Props: 2x716 Coreless motors with 2 props diam 46 mm (or equal), link here Model mass (with RC receiver, battery and motors): 50 g. 2 – Material, Settings, Printing Model design created and tested using Bambu PLA Basi c. Use this material for best results. Do NOT use PLA Matte, especially for the wing parts. Printed parts may deform after removal from the Plate due to internal material strains after cooling. Use recommended print settings. Note: The print profile for A1 mini use slightly higher material flow coefficient (1.03 instead of 0.98). For reliable printing: Clean the printing Plate before printing. After printing, remove the Plate and let it cool for 3-4 minutes Do not remove parts while the Plate is hot. 3 - Model Assembly The model consists of 18 parts, as shown in the figure. 1 – Nose, 2 – PCB Mount, 3 – A-Beam , 4 – B-Beam, 5 – Strut, 6 – Sting, 7 – Tail, 8 – Fin, 9 – Central Bracket, 10 – Dual-pin, 11 – Right Wing, 12 – Left Wing , 13 – Right Rib, 14 – Left Rib, 15 – Gear Strut (Right and Left), 16 – Wheel (2pcs), 17 – Pin (2pcs), 18 – BHCS Screw M2 x 4 mm (3 pcs). RC Receiver, Engines, props are not shown. The following assembly steps are shown without the electronic components installed. It is recommended to review them before installing the motors and electronics. Use cyanoacrylate glue where specifically indicated. Assemble the tail unit and fuselage as shown. Assemble the wing as shown in the figures. Use Dual-pin to fix wings. After installing and fixing the wing surfaces, install Wing Ribs (13, 14) on both sides. Assemble the landing gear struts as shown in the pictures below. Install landing gear struts in Central Bracket (9). Pay attention on proper positioning of right and left struts. Check correct positioning before application of glue. As final step, mount the fixing screw BHCS Screw M2 x 4 mm (18) in Central Bracket (9). Wing and landing gear assembly completed. To install the wing on the fuselage, pull the fuselage beam through predefined guide points on the wing Central Bracket, as shown in the picture. A slight pushing force may be gently applied if needed. 3.1 – Electronic Components Installation Install RC transmitter on PCB bracket (2). Finally, connect the motors to the receiver board as shown in the illustration. Before final assembly, make sure the motors rotate in opposite directions. For easier assembly and adjustment, the wires should be approximately 130-140 mm long. The wires are preferable to route through the rib. To install the motor in the rib, gently press it into place and slide it slightly forward until there is no gap. To prevent the motor from rotating during operation, secure it with a small piece of adhesive tape, as shown in the illustration. Install the ribs with the motors onto the wing as shown in the illustration. The motors must be positioned on the outer side of each rib. Install the assembled wing onto the fuselage beam, approximately 10 mm from the fuselage forward end. Then route the motor wires behind the lower fuselage beam on each side, then twist the wires together for several turns, as shown in the illustration. Only after routing the wires, install the PCB receiver bracket (2). Install the nose part (1) and secure it with screw (18). Install the battery and hold it in place with a suitable rubber band, as shown on picture. Position the wing so that the distance from the rear edge of the upper central bracket to the tail-boom joint is approximately 42 mm, as shown in the illustration. Fix finally the screw (18) of wing assembly. The model assembly is now complete. 3.2 – Balancing Pre-flight balancing not required when assembled as described above. CG positioned approximately 10 mm from the bottom wing leading edge. 4 - Model Flight Launch the model outdoors in calm weather or slight breeze conditions. Recommended wind speed: up to 5 km/h (≈1.4 m/s, ≈2.7 knots) . Always launch the model directly into the wind . Launch the model applying full throtle with a gentle horizontal push. If the model dives strongly, then: Move the wing slightly forward OR bend the elevator slightly upward If the model pitches up or stalls, first try reducing the flight speed. If flight speed reduction does not help, then: Move the wing slightly backward OR bend the elevator slightly downward Flight tip: For a ground takeoff, apply full throttle. After a takeoff run of about 10–12 meters , make a gentle turn in either direction. This slight bank helps the model lift off. Happy Flights and Smooth Landings!

Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould to cast freestanding ornaments with a snowman design. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, which should give a final ornament size of 8.5cm height with most casting slips. If you want it smaller/larger than 8.5cm, scale every piece of the print. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 375ml of plaster, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier. This version has an additional larger slot in the print with a removable insert to stop plaster from leaking during casting. Remove the insert once you're ready to demould the plaster, then the added flexibility will allow the print to pop right off!

description: This is a Universal Parametric OWB Holster designed around the Streamlight TLR-7 Series . The body of the light is where the retention is at, allowing you customize the rest of the holster to conform to the measurements of your gun. You can either build a holster than can run anything you own, provided the light is attached, or you can build a custom holster for each handgun. However you want to do it. The most requested changes outside of basic length and width measurements are 1) The option of Standard vs. Metric hardware, and 2) The ability to switch between TEK LOK and Safariland mounting patterns. Both of these options are now available. The metric can be customized using the “Nut Width” variable which defaults at 8.75mm, which is equal to #8-32. There are also minimums and maximums built into the options to protect the model itself. Such as, the minimum barrel length is 3.7". You can run a shorter gun in there as long as it can mount the light, but for the integrity of the holster, that was as short as I would let it go. For measuring instructions, you can view the following video where I also show testing of this holster. I've attached two different parametric files, a right hand and a left hand. I've also attached a ton of different holsters in my 3mf file(s) to choose from. These options will all vary from Left and Right hand versions, Teklok, Safariland mounting patterns, TLR7a or TLR7 Sub. I've also added print profiles specific to the Springfield Hellcat, the Glock 19 and the baby Staccato. To assemble, use #8-32 hardware, (unless you selected metric). Lengths will vary depending on what you are mounting the holster to, but generally, the mounting screws are ¾" and the tension screw is 1". The holster is designed for you to be able to press the appropriate nut into the recess, and be held there. You will need: 3x regular #8-32 nuts 1x nylock #8-32 nut. This is for the tension. 3x ¾" #8-32 screws, either hex, button head, whatever. This depends on what you are attaching to. 1x martini or button head 1" #8-32 screw. This is for the tension. To assemble, press the 3 regular nuts into the recesses inside the holster. You can then use the 3 screws to attach the holster to whatever. Be sure that the lengths are correct, so that the threads of the screws are not extending into the holster and inhibiting your gun or scratching it. Take the remaining nylock nut and martini screw. Press the nut into the hex recess of the tensioner and thread the screw in. It's best for you to place the unloaded handgun and light into the holster and tension until desired tightness is achieved. Print in PETG for best results in outdoor work. For assembly instructions, I've attached the following video. This will soon have an IWB EDC version. Thanks for all the support. Feel free to offer comments, critique, etc. Follow the youtube channel, instagram or follow me on X for updates and other nonsense.

I wanted to be able to permanently mount a monitor to my 19" 45U rack. I looked at some options and they were all fairly expensive. I didn't need it to move or articulate .. I just wanted a monitor I could use if I needed to connect directly to any of the servers in my rack. This design uses 4U for the mounting plate, but this is less space than is used by a typical monitor. I used a 4U size plate because it gave me appropriate thickness to mount the monitor and access to more mounting holes and a larger mounting surface area to ensure the mount was secure. I printed this using Siraya Tech's PPA-CF Core (mostly because I wanted to try it out). The mount is actually more sturdy than the aluminum in the rack - the rack bends before the mount does if I apply force. Any material that can handle the temperatures in your server closet will work given that small monitors < 24" are generally fairly light. I would suggest ABS or ASA at a minimum since some PETG formulations and most PLA formulations may deform under load at temperatures commonly found near a network rack.

description: Why this anchor exists: Every traveler knows the frustration: you arrive at the beach, set up your tent or lay down your towel, and the wind turns your stakes into useless plastic sticks. Sand, loose soil, and snow laugh at conventional stakes. They bend. They slip. They fail. I designed this anchor because I was tired of chasing my gear across the sand. The solution came from studying a classic mountaineering technique called a "deadman anchor" — a buried plate that uses the weight and friction of the ground itself to resist extraction. I engineered that principle into a compact, printable design that fits flat in your bag and deploys in under a minute. How it works (the physics): This is not a stake. This is a compression confinement anchor. Two discs (109.2 mm diameter) are separated by 115 mm along a cross-shaped central shaft. When buried and subjected to an upward pull, the lower disc compresses the sand between itself and the upper disc. The sand, trapped and compacted, generates lateral pressure against the surrounding ground, mobilizing its internal friction angle (φ). The result: the anchor must lift an entire confined cylinder of sand — over 1 liter in volume (1.08 L) — to be extracted. Standard stakes rely on surface friction along their shaft. In loose sand, that friction is nearly zero. This anchor converts a weak material into a solid block of resistance. Measured and calculated performance: Loose dry sand (children's sandbox): extraction force of 8–10 kg-f — already 5 to 15 times higher than a plastic beach stake in the same conditions. Compacted beach sand or moist earth: estimated extraction force of 20–30 kg-f, based on load capacity models with friction angles of 30–35°. Visual proof: when extracted from loose sand, the anchor pulls out a massive sand cylinder, demonstrating the confinement mechanism in action. A conventional stake in the same sandbox? Pulls out clean with almost zero resistance. Key features: Pack-and-deploy: assembles from flat-packed plates into a rigid cross-anchor structure. No tools required. 100% printable: no supports, no external hardware. Designed for consumer FDM printers (tested on Bambu Lab A1 Mini). Dual-disc bayonet lock: discs slide over the shaft, rotate 45°, and lock into teeth — secure, fast, and sand-tolerant. PETG recommended: for outdoor durability, UV resistance, and the flexibility needed during assembly. Scenarios: 🏖️ Beach: secure towels, sunshades, beach tents. ❄️ Snow camping: deadman anchor for tent guylines in powder. ⛺ Loose soil: anywhere conventional stakes fail. INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE Standard Setup: Dig: Make a vertical hole about 15 cm deep (remember: greater depth means greater pull-out resistance). Assemble the cross: Slide the two shafts together to form the cross-shaped structure. Place the lower confinement disc: Slide one disc over the shafts, pushing it down until it rests on the lower locking tabs . Rotate it 45° so the bayonet teeth lock it firmly in place. Bury and compact the base: Place the device into the hole and fill it with sand or snow up to the upper crossbars . Compact the material firmly with your hands to ensure proper confinement. Secure the upper disc: Place the second disc with the locking notches facing up, and rotate it 45° onto the upper crossbars to lock it. Finish filling: Cover the entire anchor, leaving only the tie-down holes visible on the surface for passing ropes through. Advanced Method (Deep Anchoring): For extreme wind conditions or deep snow, use the total burial method: Follow steps 1 through 5, but dig significantly deeper. Before finishing the fill, secure your ropes to the tie-down holes. Then cover the anchor completely and compact. The anchor will work at depth, providing maximum resistance. Usage tip: For tents, use 1 anchor per corner or tension point .

Parametrische Universal-Adapterplatte Diese vollständig anpassbare Adapterplatte verbindet zwei unterschiedliche Befestigungs- beziehungsweise Lochbilder miteinander. Sie eignet sich ideal, wenn vorhandene Bohrungen weiterverwendet werden sollen, das neue Bauteil jedoch andere Befestigungspunkte besitzt. So können beispielsweise Sensoren, Kameras, Displays, Elektronikmodule, Netzteile, Gehäuse, Halterungen oder kleine Geräte montiert werden, ohne neue Löcher in eine Wand, Maschine oder vorhandene Konstruktion bohren zu müssen. Zwei unabhängig einstellbare Lochbilder Die Adapterplatte besitzt zwei getrennt konfigurierbare Lochbilder: Lochbild A – vorhandene Befestigung Dieses Lochbild wird passend zu den bereits vorhandenen Bohrungen eingestellt, beispielsweise an einer Wand, einem Gehäuse, einer Maschine oder einer bestehenden Halterung. Lochbild B – neues Bauteil Das zweite Lochbild wird passend zu dem Bauteil eingestellt, das auf der Adapterplatte montiert werden soll. Beide Lochbilder können unabhängig voneinander angepasst, verschoben und gedreht werden. Dadurch sind auch versetzte oder unterschiedlich ausgerichtete Befestigungen möglich. Anpassbare Lochanordnung Für jedes Lochbild kann separat gewählt werden zwischen: deaktiviertem Lochbild einer einzelnen Bohrung zwei Bohrungen in einer Reihe einem rechteckigen Vierlochbild Die horizontalen und vertikalen Abstände lassen sich unabhängig einstellen. Eine Zweierreihe kann durch Drehen des Lochbildes auch vertikal oder diagonal ausgerichtet werden. Runde Bohrungen oder Langlöcher Jedes Lochbild kann wahlweise mit normalen runden Bohrungen oder Langlöchern erzeugt werden. Langlöcher bieten zusätzliches Montagespiel und sind besonders praktisch, wenn vorhandene Lochabstände nicht exakt bekannt sind oder das montierte Bauteil später noch ausgerichtet werden soll. Einstellbar sind unter anderem: Durchmesser der Bohrungen Gesamtlänge der Langlöcher Ausrichtung der Langlöcher Drehung des gesamten Lochbildes horizontale und vertikale Position Die Ausrichtung der Langlöcher kann unabhängig von der Drehung des Lochbildes verändert werden. Optionale Schraubensenkungen Für jedes der beiden Lochbilder können optional Senkungen aktiviert werden. Dadurch können geeignete Schraubenköpfe bündig oder nahezu bündig in der Oberseite der Platte sitzen. Die Senkungen werden nur auf der Oberseite erzeugt. Die Unterseite der Adapterplatte bleibt vollständig flach und kann direkt auf dem Druckbett platziert werden. Optionaler mittlerer Ausschnitt Zusätzlich kann ein mittlerer Ausschnitt aktiviert werden. Zur Auswahl stehen: kein Ausschnitt runder Ausschnitt rechteckiger Ausschnitt rechteckiger Ausschnitt mit abgerundeten Ecken Der Ausschnitt kann verschoben und bei rechteckiger Ausführung auch gedreht werden. Dadurch eignet sich die Adapterplatte ebenfalls für: Kabeldurchführungen Steckverbinder Lüftungsöffnungen hervorstehende Gehäuseteile Schalter oder Bedienelemente Kameralinsen und Sensorbereiche Automatische Plattengröße Bei aktivierter automatischer Größenanpassung werden Breite und Höhe als gewünschte Mindestabmessungen verwendet. Benötigen die Lochbilder, Langlöcher oder der mittlere Ausschnitt mehr Platz, wird die Platte automatisch vergrößert. Dabei werden auch die eingestellten Verschiebungen, Drehungen, Senkungen und Randabstände berücksichtigt. Alternativ kann die automatische Anpassung deaktiviert werden. In diesem Fall verwendet das Modell exakt die eingestellten Außenmaße und prüft, ob ausreichend Platz für alle Elemente vorhanden ist. Gestaltung der Grundplatte Die Adapterplatte besitzt: abgerundete Ecken eine umlaufende Fase an der oberen Außenkante eine vollständig flache Unterseite eine mittige Positionierung um den Modellursprung frei einstellbare Plattendicke frei einstellbaren Abstand zwischen Aussparungen und Außenkante Durch die gefaste Außenkontur erhält die Platte ein sauberes und technisch ansprechendes Erscheinungsbild. Typische Anwendungen Die Adapterplatte eignet sich unter anderem für: Sensor- und Kamerahalterungen Elektronikmodule und Platinengehäuse Displays und Bedienelemente Netzteile und Steuergeräte Maschinen- und Werkstattzubehör Wandhalterungen Lüfter und Belüftungskomponenten Modellbau und Robotik Fahrzeug- und Camperausbauten Reparaturen und Umbauten vorhandener Befestigungen Hinweise zum 3D-Druck Das Modell ist für einen unkomplizierten Druck ausgelegt. Die flache Unterseite wird direkt auf dem Druckbett positioniert, während Senkungen und Außenfase nach oben zeigen. In dieser Ausrichtung ist normalerweise kein Stützmaterial erforderlich. Für mechanisch belastete Anwendungen sollten eine ausreichende Anzahl an Wandlinien und ein für den Einsatzzweck geeignetes Filament verwendet werden. Überschneiden sich Bohrungen, Langlöcher oder der mittlere Ausschnitt, werden die Bereiche miteinander verbunden. Recommended Print Settings MAKE SURE YOUR PLATE IS VERY CLEAN! These prints have many small details in the first layer. If your plate is not clean, some of the details will not adhere and will affect the quality of the image. Material PETG is strongly recommended for outdoor use. Since fly boxes often sit in hot vehicles, sunlit boats, or wet wading packs, PETG provides superior heat resistance compared to standard PLA. While PLA will work, you will need to be cautious of heat to prevent warping. That being said, I have still included some PLA print profiles for you to use at your own discretion and because PLA will give a more color-accurate look. 🛠️ Hardware & Assembly Hinge Pins: To keep the amount of hardware needed at a minimum, this design simply uses a piece of filament as a hinge pin Fly Insert: Designed to fit slotted EVA foam trimmed to fit or the 3D-printed TPU fly grid insert. Magnet: The design stays shut with the use of two 20mm x 5mm x 2mm magnets glued in with your choice of glue (I have used superglue, E6000, and Loctite 406) Assembly tips: A tip for installing the magnets is to put two together and then Sharpie the outside of each magnet. This way you know which sides face each other when gluing them in. Use a small amount of glue. Too much will prevent the magnet from seating all the way. When using the TPU insert, I recommend gluing it in place. When gluing in the insert, for best results, start by scuffing both the inner box surface and the backside of the TPU with some sandpaper (80 to 180 grit preferred) and then apply a thin layer of glue over the majority of the surface on both pieces. Press the pieces together and then weigh down the TPU insert with some objects you have lying around until the glue is fully set. I recommend glues like Loctite 406 or Gorilla Clear Grip, but I'm sure many other options will work well enough. If you print one, please post a photo of your build and your favorite lid design! Update: July 28th, 2026 Added a mirrored verison of the 1001U lid for more customization with left or right side of Apache case placement ZK-1002T compatibility via inward facing mounts on the bump outs “Lid - No Amp” added. Use this with the ZK-1002T or for just a clean top lid. Selectable left or right wire cutouts as well Modular Electronics Housing for Apache 2800 Boombox Builds I designed the Apache Mod Box as an all-in-one place to house the amp, battery, wiring, and controls in an Apache 2800 boombox build. There are a few similar designs out there, but I wanted something that gave the builder more freedom with the layout. Instead of being stuck with the power button, charging port, and Voltmeter/USB Charger in one specific spot, this model lets you choose where you want them before you print. ZK-1002T Compatibility The ZK-1002T amp is provided compatibility via inward face of the box. There are 2 locations, 1 on each bump out of the box. Simply pick the object from the list and change it to a negative part. Once printed, remove the washer and nut from the amp knobs, slide them through the holes from the inside and reattach the washers and nuts. Use the “Lid - No Amp” for a clean finish on top! ZK-1001U Compatibility The included lid is designed to mount the ZK-1001U amplifier on top of the Mod Box while keeping the battery and wiring contained underneath. Because of the available clearance, you'll need a 5.5 × 2.1 mm right-angle DC adapter for the amp's power connection. A straight connector will not work properly with this setup. Assembly Hardware The Mod Box is assembled using M4 heat-set inserts and M4 × 12 mm screws . You’ll need: 6x M4 heat-set inserts 6x M4 × 12 mm flat head machine screws The inserts are installed into the box, and the lid is then secured with the M4 screws. This makes the lid easy to remove later if you need to get back into the box for wiring changes, battery replacement, or other upgrades. Tools Soldering Iron Heat Set Insert Tips Parts 5.5mm x 2.1mm Charge Port Jack 5.5mm x 2.1mm Right Angle Adapter Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger or USB-C Model 16mm 12v/24v Latching Power Button 24v 4Ah Battery or 7Ah Battery (same size) ZK-1001U Amp Internal Space Main Chamber: 227 mm long × 86 mm deep × 74 mm tall Bump Outs: 46mm wide x 111mm long Make sure your battery and other components fit within that space before printing. Voltmeter/USB Charger The model is designed around a standard 30 mm round Voltmeter/USB Charger with a 30.3 mm modeled opening . There are three possible mounting locations: Inside of the Apache case Outside of the Apache case Top of the Mod Box and accessible from inside the case So whether you want your USB ports accessible without opening the case or would rather keep everything inside, you can set it up either way. Charging Port The charging port is designed for a standard 12 mm round charging port with a 12.3 mm modeled opening . There are four possible mounting locations: Inside – left Inside – right Outside – left Outside – right This gives you the option to keep the charging connection inside the case or make it accessible from the outside. Power Button The Mod Box supports 16 mm, 19 mm, and 22 mm power buttons . Like the charging port, the power button has four possible mounting locations: Inside – left Inside – right Outside – left Outside – right The modeled openings are: Button Size Modeled Opening 16 mm 16.3 mm 19 mm 19.3 mm 22 mm 22.3 mm The power button and charging port do not have to be on the same side. You can keep your power button inside and charging port outside, put them on opposite sides of the Voltmeter/USB Charger, or set them up however works best for your build. Setting Up Your Mod Box The different cutouts are already built into the included 3MF, so you don't need to edit anything in CAD . In Bambu Studio, open the Objects tab and expand the Mod Box. You'll see the different cutout options labeled by size and location. Find the openings you want to use and change those objects to Negative Part . When the model is sliced, the negative objects will create the holes in the Mod Box. Leave any locations you aren't using alone. I highly recommend checking the sliced preview before starting the print. It's an easy way to make sure you've opened the right locations before committing to the full box. Important: Power Button Sizes The charging-port and power-button openings are nested together. Because of that, when you choose a larger power button, you also need to make all of the smaller openings at that same location negative . What You're Using Make These Negative 12 mm charging port 12 mm 16 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm 19 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm 22 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm + 22 mm For example, if you're using a 22 mm power button , make the 12 mm, 16 mm, 19 mm, and 22 mm objects at that location Negative Parts. Making only the 22 mm object negative will not create the complete opening. Thanks for checking out the Apache Mod Box! I put a lot of thought into making this as flexible and useful as possible for different Apache boombox builds. If you print one, I’d love to see how you set yours up. And if you have an idea for another amp lid, different port size, mounting option, or anything else that would make the Mod Box better, drop a comment or send a recommendation. I’m always open to improving the design and adding more options for future builds.

description: SPA Expert - Backpack Carabine Kit Target shooting is a great way to unwind and clear the mind and the UX SPA Expert is a cool little CO2 pistol as entry point into the hobby. It's affordable, semi-automatic, and works easily with CO2 capsules for endless fun plinking. Its low power makes it safe and the design allows for great modularity with add-on parts and customisation. It's the ideal option to anyone looking for outdoor fun. I'm a big fan of Umarex their products because they provide precision and fun at great value, and a great base for upgrading and tinkering. Products » Product universe » Classic » CO₂-powered » 2.4392 » SPA Expert » www.umarex.com This Carabine kit transforms this cool little pistol into a rigid compact takedown carabine. Having a stock improves accuracy and shootability significantly and gives it a nice touch of cyberpunk design. The forend integrates a silencer elevating the little pistol into a complete compact rifle that can be taken down and stashed everywhere. The entire kit is 3D printed and solid as a rock. It comes together with simple dowel parts and a snug fit providing a solid little rifle that can be printed for a fraction of the cost of the pistol. The foregrip has in integrated silencer that reduces noise considerably and the stock really reduces the jerk of the double action trigger. This is a great upgrade for any serious shooter that likes a compact plinking toy or a cool gift for a friend or kid getting into the hobby. With the options 3D printing provides you can customise color and options to your hearts content. Besides the stock and overall look the kit has a few subtle upgrades integrated in the design: Extended foregrip with integrated silencer Textured grips and cheekweld Open window for better CO2 heat transfer during shooting Compact package with the stock removed Grip only version: UX SPA Expert - Custom Grip - Free 3D Print Model - MakerWorld Pictured Red dot Sight: VictOptics SRD 1x18x20 Red Dot Assembly Slide the foregrip part over the picantinny rail and push it all the way to the back. Insert the two grip parts making sure the forend is all the way back, these engage in the botton picantinny rail securing it with the silencer against the barrel port. The hand parts are press fit, but you can use a drop of CA for extra security. Now combine the two stock parts with the printed dowels, use a drop of CA to fix the dowels in place. Alternate the layer orrientation of the dowels for optimal strength and rigidity. Now apply some CA on the dowels and surface, not too much, and pres on the other part to fit tightly. Apply some CA and place the cheekpiece over the stock using the integrated guide dowels and press to fit seamless. This whole three part construction is made to fit tight and have high rigidity when assembled correctly. You can now place the stock like the original grip and you have your own unique little CO2 carabine! Airguns are not toys, use with care and supervision!

description: This press plate set makes a quick and easy heart dish, bowl or plate out of clay. When making a deeper press, flip your piece upside down with the inner press plate still in place and set it on top of a glaze bottle or something to keep it raised until the clay has a chance to get more solid. If you’re making multiple deep plates at one time, print multiple copies of just the inner plate so you can continue making while your finished pieces rest! description: Looking for a custom adapter, fitting, reducer, or elbow? Look no further. AdapterGenerator is a fully parametric OpenSCAD generator for hollow adapters. Configure End A and End B independently using round or rectangular spigots and sockets, hose barbs, male or female threads, or bolted flanges, then connect them with a straight, offset, reducing, stepped, or bent transition. From vacuum hose adapters and duct transitions to threaded couplers, nozzles, reducers, and custom fittings, it's built for practical real-world connections. A shared transition system keeps the workflow simple, while independent end geometry, fit allowance, taper, bends, seals, wrench flats, and finishing controls let you tailor the result to the connection you need. Click Customize to open the generator. 🚀 Quick Start 1. Choose End A Select the first interface type and enter its size, length, and any interface-specific settings. 2. Choose End B Configure the second end independently. Mix sockets, spigots, hose barbs, threads, flanges, or rectangular fittings as needed. 3. Shape the Transition Set the transition length and optional offset. Use a length of 0 for an abrupt stepped connection. 4. Add a Bend Set the bend angle, radius, and rotation to create straight adapters or custom elbows. 5. Refine and Export Adjust fit, wall thickness, barbs, threads, O-ring grooves, flanges, and finishing details, then choose the desired output and quality. ⭐ Features Mix-and-Match Interfaces Connect round or rectangular sockets and spigots, hose barbs, threads, and flanges. Flexible Transitions Create reducers, enlargers, stepped adapters, and eccentric or offset connections. Custom Elbows Add bends up to 180° with adjustable centerline radius and rotation. Functional Details Add tapers, hose barbs, wrench flats, O-ring grooves, flange bolt patterns, chamfers, and socket lead-ins. Preview & Test Tools Use section views, test pieces, and Debug mode to inspect geometry and dimensions. ℹ️ Notes Some controls apply only to specific interfaces. Rectangular dimensions require rectangular ends, thread settings require threaded ends, and O-ring grooves support round sockets and flange faces. The generator validates many incompatible dimensions and clearances. Still inspect short transitions, large offsets, and tight bends in Section View or your slicer. Use Debug to diagnose geometry. For critical fits, print an End A Test or End B Test first and tune Fit Clearance for your printer and material. Use Print End to choose which end sits on the build plate. For additional guidance and troubleshooting, see the Frequently Asked Questions attached to this post. Feedback and examples of what you create are always welcome! 📜 Maker Scripts

description: 原创机器人企划 天堂边境奥比托斯 正在开展中！ 配色采用的是 彩多屋墨绿（PLA Basic）三慈棕色（PLA Basic） 眼部是 eSun哑光薄荷绿（PLA Matte） 轨道环及相关组件使用的是 彩多屋丝绸青铜（PLA Silk） 使用其他耗材可能会出现一定公差，部分打印悬垂会影响装配，需自行修整后装配即可，应该不是什么大问题。 打印方面： 本体均使用0.2层高 拳头照顾效果可使用0.16或更高精度 头部三块零件件需使用0.08或更高精度 打印头部有概率出现轻微拉丝，使用剪钳或者笔刀或者打火机简单处理即可 PLA Silk比较脆（部分零件图纸里面有放点备件），处理时请自行留意 材质限制，玩久了关节可能会松动，可使用丙烯哑光剂及其他进行加固 ！！！组装时请跟随说明书制作，部分零件未按顺序装配可能会影响后续拼装流程！！！ 后续更新均会在小红书及bilibili上公布，感兴趣的话可以移步关注！ 破路者（roadbreaker）作为先行开发配备的八台奥比托斯（orbitors）系列的强袭装甲（Assault Armor）之中的三号机。不同于开拓者及地狱行者的中近战攻击特化，破路者以可攻可守强火力立体机动堡垒为做开发目的，因此在初期制造阶段，身体部分零件有做区分于其他机体的改修。本机同样拥有三种模式切换能力，分别为： D（efense） Mode 防御模式 即常态站立模式 S（trike）Mode 突击模式 通过移动脚部骨架，使轨道环作为主移动道具，获得更高的突进力 O（verdrive）Mode 超速模式 四轮车形态，在移除背后的电池包下可变形为该模式，通过奥比托环自身储能爆发脱离战场，拥有突袭形态三倍的机动性，是对天使作战中用于自我保护的最终模式。 详情图中的主兵装 heaven bane及地台支架将在个人主页单独上传，可自行前往下载 相关套件禁止二次销售盈利，请尊重原作者，感谢大家支持与理解！

model_name: Bombastic Air 2 - Make your own desktop fan
description: Summer is here and its starting to get Hot! Turn your spare 120mm pc fans into tabletop fans to cool down. Here is the material list: (and 2 120mm pc fans with a thickness of 25mm, you can always make the model thicker or thinner if your pc fans arn't the right thickness) The M6 Nuts are for the added weight on the “base” model so that the fan does not topple over. I use 4 m4 DIN 935 nuts to act as threads on the base plate for the stand arms to screw into with m4x10mm screws. There are slots in the model that the nuts slide into (some force is needed) The thinner M4 DIN 439 nuts are used for the other threads, one needs to be placed inside the “adapter” model in the middle for the m4x10mm screws that connect them to the “stand” model. Then there are 4 slots inside the “Back” model that act as threads for the "adapter models to screw into with m4x10mm screws. The round hole at the bottom of the “Back” model is for the dc connector jack to slide out of and the square hole is for the spst rocker switch. the red wire is connected to one of the switch terminals and the other terminal is connected to the positive wires of the 120mm fans. Then all the Ground wires are connected together. Mush the wires into the middle area between the fans and put on the “Front” model on the “back” model. On the “back” model there are additional slots for the rest of the m4 DIN 439 nuts. Simply thread the m4x30mm screws through the front to the back and screw them together. There are optional holes in the base model in case you'd fasten it to a wall or something. Another optional addon is aa nonslip fabtic pad across the bottom of base stand to cover up the m6 nuts and what not. Happy Printing! Woops, a build plate area of atleast 255x255 x30 is needed to print this in the correct orientation. Printing at an angle messes up the messurments!
