description: MorphCase A modular, fully 3D-printable PC case built for customization Youtube video: BEFORE PRINTING Please read the front-I/O compatibility note below. The original PCB is no longer readily available, so you may need to adapt the included STEP files for another front-I/O board. A PC case that can change with your build MorphCase is a complete 3D-printable PC enclosure designed around flexibility. The internal structure can be used by itself as an open-frame rack, or combined with the outer shell for a finished enclosed case. The segmented construction also makes it easy to experiment with different colors, materials, panel patterns and future design variations without replacing the entire case. Key features Open-rack and fully enclosed configurations Modular printed construction with replaceable exterior sections Support for a full PC build with motherboard, PSU and dedicated GPU Ventilated side, top and rear panels Integrated GPU support and panel-mounted AC extension Front USB, audio and power controls Included STEP source files for customization and hardware adaptation Designed for color mixing and future panel or shell variations Choose your configuration Open-frame rack Complete the internal rack assembly and stop after Step 7. This configuration keeps the hardware accessible and is useful for testing, display or frequent upgrades. Enclosed case Continue through Step 12 to add the outer shell, ventilated panels and press-fit front panel for the complete MorphCase appearance. Important front-I/O compatibility note The front-I/O PCB used in the original build was an OEM part sold only in mainland China. It was never widely available internationally, and the original listing appears to have been discontinued. If several builders want the original layout, leave a comment. With enough interest, I will consider reverse-engineering the PCB and producing a solderable replacement with matching dimensions. Otherwise, select another front-I/O board and adapt the enclosure around it. The STEP source files are included specifically to make this possible. What you will need Compatible motherboard, CPU, CPU cooler, RAM and storage Power supply and its correct modular cables, if applicable Dedicated graphics card Front-I/O PCB or an adapted replacement 40 cm left-angle IEC C13-to-C14 panel-mount AC extension cable M3 heat-set inserts, M3 bolts and the four longer #6-32 × 3/8-inch PSU screws listed in the manual Files and documentation The download includes the printable parts, editable STEP source files and a separate illustrated PDF assembly manual. Read the complete manual before printing or purchasing hardware. SAFETY PC assembly and mains-voltage connections require care. Use a certified AC extension cable, verify all cable routing before power-up, and never use modular PSU cables from a different PSU model unless the manufacturer explicitly confirms compatibility. Make it yours MorphCase is intended as a platform rather than a single fixed look. Mix colors, design new vent patterns, modify the front panel or develop an entirely different outer shell around the same internal rack. If you build or remix it, share your version - I would love to see how the platform evolves.

model_name: Midea PortaSplit Condensate Cleaning Tablet Holder
description: For cleaning the condensate tray at the bottom of the Midea PortaSplit. Earlier manuals recommend cleaning the condensate tray with AC cleaning tabs. However the PortaSplit doesn't really come with an ideal location to put these tabs - one might be able to squeeze them in behind the plastic to the left and right of the slot where you can reach the condensate tray from, but I was worried that vibrations might carry the tab out of there. Putting the tabs directly into the reservoir makes them dissolve far too quickly. The purpose of this model is to try to keep the tab above the standing water level, so the tab is never fully submerged. Instead the condensate can drip onto the tablet, and (ideally) drain from the holder immediately. I generated this model for the StayClean Cleaning Tablets, and it will likely not fit tabs that are larger. Ideally print with a water resistant filament like ASA or PETG. If you use PLA, it might degrade quicker, so a reprint every year might be needed. Probably good to inspect it for bacterial growth, and ideally clean monthly. Use at your own risk, I take no warranty whatsoever that this works as intended. It might break your device, kill you, or summon Cthulhu. I also haven't properly tested this model really myself yet since there was currently no need for the AC at this time. I might update this post when I do test it, but I just wanted to get it uploaded in case people might want to try it and so I don't forget.

description: Editors note: (Here's the revised version of my previous model: Highest Flying Outdoor Plane - Best-printed Glider. It fixed some of the most commonly reported issues, including easy breakage, glue assembly, and inconsistent flight.) Intro: Hello everyone! Get ready for some serious reading :D-Its all important stuff though, so for the best flying results, read this . This is my plane/glider model, “Loopy V2”. This project took heavy inspiration from " exosequitur " on Thingiverse. While I got the idea of an outdoor glider plane from their model, I can assure you that mine is an original model with added features such as a launching tab, built-in top fin, Slide on head and hook, and adjustable wing elevation. Furthermore, I will link their model in the description in case anyone wants to know what inspired this project. Assembly: Anyway, there are a couple of things you should know before printing. MAKE SURE YOUR BED IS CLEAN. Before removing any parts from the build plate, WAIT FOR IT TO COOL COMPLETELY . Also, GENTLY bend the plate when removing the plane and parts. This model includes three parts: the plane body, the head, and the hook. The side of the head without the slit should be pointed forward, and the curved side of the hook should be pointed backwards. To assemble, you simply place the hook into the plane, then slide the head onto the slit in the hook. After this, I advise that you GENTLY bend the main wings and back wings up (a good amount). If your plane is nose-diving immediately after launch, bend both the main and back wings upward more (keeping them even). (You can see the recommended angle in the image below). Launching: Next, launching. The best angle for launching is around a 65-degree angle upwards . This allows the plane to do a big loop, then swoop into a smooth glide. Another way to launch is a 65-degree angle upwards with the plane tilted left (as shown in an image below). This makes the plane do a sweeping boomerang-like flight. However, windy days allow for a special launch method. This strategy includes launching the plane at an almost 90-degree angle upwards. If the plane gets high enough, you can catch a wind current and take off. I've had planes fly hundreds of yards with this method. Although, it takes a pretty windy day , and a few tries to do it. For launching in general, you obviously need your launch stick and rubber bands. I used some large rubber bands from Amazon (named in BOM). Another tip: If your plane is flying left or right, then dipping, bend the wing pointing in the direction the plane is dipping, upwards . For example , if your plane is dipping right , bend the right wing up a bit. Always try to keep the wings at the same angle upwards, and this should fix your issues. Last tip: While it seems counterintuitive, you don't need a huge launch for a cool flight; sometimes all it takes is a windy day and a softish launch for some awesome and far gliding. Outro: If you enjoy this model, be sure to leave a thumbs up, boost, and send me a picture of your own. Also dont be afraid to paint, or draw (with a sharpie) on your plane . Its a cool way to add an extra touch without switching filament mid print or AMS. Anyways, happy printing and have fun! the inspiration: https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:97803 Reccomended Wing Angles (higher=less nosediving)

This is a set of 3d printable 4 link suspension links for WPL C24 (and probably other cars) RC crawlers. I've made these as I've made a bunch of upgrades, and needed longer links to get things working smoothly. I tried the adjustable metal links, and they weren't long enough. As pictured, the 65mm upper link, and the 57mm lower links put the axle roughly in the stock position, but with the axle rolled forward slightly to give better angles for the universal joints. Fitting to truck I don't think these will work with the stock axle link mounts. I have metal mounts (and axles), and I think you need the aftermarket mount to make it work. After market shocks are probably good to. I used the long screws (10mm or 12 mm? I should measure) I think came with the after market shocks I'm using. The print has some spacers that go with the links. These are mainly as I couldn't put a collar on the build plate side of the links. You'll kind of need to fiddle around with how they go on, and a few small washers might be helpful to get things to align properly. Sizing custom links As the exact size may vary depending on your specific truck, I've included a .3mf file with an adjustable link, and a scale. To adjust the link: In the Objects menu, select Rod Right, Then you can use the move tool to slide the Rod Right along the X axis until it matches the length you need it to be. You will find you might need to come to the right required length with a bit of trial and error.

description: The Ultimate Ball Generator Create fully customizable decorative, sensory, toy, or hanging balls directly in MakerWorld. Adjust the ball dimensions, surface pattern, hole spacing, wall thickness, colors, custom text, and hanging ring without using external CAD software. One generator. Endless possibilities. Create personalized balls with names or logos, Christmas ornaments, keychains, sensory and fidget toys, bouncing balls, decorative spheres, party favors, and unique gifts. Mix patterns, colors, text styles and accessories to generate thousands of completely different designs — all in just a few clicks. Main Features Ball diameter from 20 to 150 mm (larger also possible per request) Adjustable wall thickness from 1 to 5 mm Airless or solid spheres Multiple pattern styles: Circle Hexagon Diamond Rectangle Triangle Teardrop Heart Flower Star Four pattern effects: None – smooth ball Hole – openings through the shell Emboss – recessed pattern Raised – pattern raised above the surface Adjustable pattern size, spacing, rotation and marking depth Optional rounded pattern edges Optional Seam decorations (basketball, tennis ball, soccer ball, …) Custom text with multiple fonts Two text background styles: Text Outline – background follows the actual letter shapes Plaque – rounded rectangular nameplate Flat, embossed or raised text Adjustable text margin and nameplate curvature Optional reinforced hanging ring Custom colors for the ball, text background and lettering Adjustable sphere resolution for better quality or prototyping How to Customize Ball Dimensions Use Diameter to select the overall size of the ball. Wall Thickness determines the shell thickness when the Hole effect is selected. A value of 2–3 mm is a good starting point for most prints. Sphere Resolution controls surface smoothness: Draft – fastest preview Standard – quick testing Smooth – good balance Fine – recommended default Great or Ultra – smoother result, but longer generation time Pattern Choose the desired shape using Pattern Type . Use: Pattern Size to control the size of each element Pattern Spacing to control the visible gap between elements Pattern Angle to rotate the pattern on the ball Pattern Marking to control emboss depth or raised height Add Fillet on Pattern to round the pattern edges Small patterns combined with very small spacing can create a large number of elements and significantly increase generation and slicing time. Seams (decoration) Use this predefined seam decorations that adds a final touch to your ball. Available now: Basketball Basketball retro Tennis Baseball Soccer ball (football) Custom Text Set Custom Text to On , then enter your message. Choose between: Text Outline for a compact background following the letters Plaque for a traditional rounded rectangular label Text Margin controls the space or outline around the lettering. Plaque Curve Correction allows fine adjustment of how tightly the background follows the ball: Negative values create a flatter curve Positive values wrap the background more tightly The default value is tuned for most ball and text sizes Text effects: Flat – flush multicolor lettering Emboss – recessed lettering Raised – lettering above the surface For multicolor models, download the generated 3MF to preserve the separate ball, background and text colors. Hanging Ring Enable Hanging Ring to add a reinforced loop at the top. Adjust: Ring Hole Size for the string or ribbon opening Ring Thickness for the strength of the loop This option is useful for ornaments, decorations and hanging sensory toys. The color of the ring can be customized in Color section. Best Practices / Tips At first lower Ball resolution to Draft. When done designing try making it higher (only if needed). Please note that dense patterns actually are very good at Draft and there is no need to set higher resolution. Pattern Fillet can be quite heavy to process on the servers but in most of the cases is not needed. If you expirience server timeouts or errors consider turning it off. When you expirience server timeout or errors it most likely means that your set-up is to heavy to process on MakerWorld's servers. Try larger patter or higher spacing, lower resolution. Everything that will make it less complicated will work and try again. Consider the position of the ball when you will be printing it. For example when using heart pattern - the middle part of heart can not face down as you will need to support every patter like this. Thy setting an angle and face it up. The larger the ball is the more render power it requires on MM servers. If you plan going large try less details. Printing Tips Printing spheres is quite challenging and it is important to choose the right options in the slicer. Here are some tips to achieve the best results: Use the generated 3MF when printing in multiple colors. A layer height of 0.16–0.20 mm works well. Enable option “Don't support bridges” Add “Support Blocker” modifier to block supporting areas inside the ball. Rise the blocker a little bit so the base can be supported Tune your “Top Z distance” value for supports Use at least three wall loops for hollow balls. Enable supports when required by the selected pattern and orientation. Build-plate-only supports are usually easier to remove. For small holes, verify the preview before printing. Reduce print speed on the outer wall for a smoother spherical surface. Larger balls, dense patterns and Ultra resolution require more processing time. To achieve optimal bounce, use a suitable filament (TPU, PEBA, other flexible filaments). Important Notes Hole produces a hollow ball using the selected wall thickness. None , Emboss and Raised produce a solid ball. Very thin walls or extremely small gaps may not print reliably with every nozzle size. This generator creates geometry dynamically, so complex configurations can take longer to generate in MakerWorld. Make sure to follow my profile on Maker World for updates and ready to use examples. Have fun printing!

The goal was to make something small enough to keep in a pocket without it becoming a hassle to carry. It works well as a backup rod, or for those times when the bigger fish are not biting but there are plenty of smaller fish nearby. Designed for Strength This was one of the most important parts of the design. Most telescopic prints are printed vertically, which places force across the weaker layer lines. The square shape of this rod allows every telescopic section to be printed flat, so the layers run along the length of the rod instead. This gives it the strongest possible print orientation for its size. The rod feels surprisingly rigid when extended and can handle much more pressure than the small fish it is intended for. Working Reel The rod includes a clip-in reel with a small finger recess, allowing you to wind the line back in by hand. It can also be operated with your thumb, depending on which direction you spool the line. I kept the reel low-profile so the rod remains smooth and compact when collapsed. I may add an optional reel handle accessory in the future. Print Information The model is split across three print plates , making it easier to customise the colours. I highly recommend using the included print profiles, as a lot of testing went into getting the sliding tolerances working correctly. The full rod can be printed in PLA. Assembly Instructions 1. Assemble the Telescopic Sections The rod sections are tapered, so the correct direction should be visible by eye. Keep every part facing the same way, with the build-plate texture aligned on the same side. Slide the sections through one another, then pass the full assembly through the main body. Fit the butt cap onto the bottom once everything is in place. 2. Fit the Eyelets Press the eyelets onto the rod sections. They are designed to fit snugly, but printer tolerances vary, so I recommend using a very small dab of glue to stop them coming loose when the rod is collapsed. 3. Feed the Line Feed the line through: The top eyelet The second eyelet The third eyelet The body eyelet Pull enough line through to give yourself room to attach it to the reel. 4. Attach the Reel Before pressing the reel into the body, feed the line through the reel from the inside to the outside . Adding a small hook-shaped bend to the end of the line makes this easier. Pass the line through a few times, tie it securely, then carefully press the reel into place using firm, even pressure. Wind on your preferred amount of line. I used a few metres, which was plenty for testing. Hook and Weight Storage Once the rod is collapsed and the line has been reeled in, the hook and weight can be tucked into the butt cap. The cap then closes over the end, keeping the rig secure and stopping the hook from moving around loose in your pocket. Important: Tight Tolerances The telescopic sections use very tight tolerances to keep the rod smooth, secure and free from excessive movement. With some filaments, the sections may feel slightly stiff or may not fully extend at first. Gently work the affected section in and out a few times. The parts will usually wear themselves in and become smoother with use. This can vary depending on filament type, moisture and small differences in printing. If the sections remain unusually tight, make sure your filament is dry or try printing them with a different filament. FAQ How long is it? description: Log July 29, 2026 The .ino format file cannot be uploaded as an attachment, so the code has been uploaded to GitHub. Please visit https://github.com/tipflowmaker/8-bit-Animated-emojis/tree/main to download it. Explanation This is a new 8-bit model. Compared with the previous version, it eliminates the step of sampling and customizing PCBs, and an independent battery power supply system is added. The hardware assembly can be completed simply by soldering commonly available development board modules and batteries on the market. In addition, the structure and assembly scheme have been optimized, enabling the assembly of hardware components and the enclosure without screws. I have uploaded the Arduino code for displaying animated facial expressions on the exterior. If you have specific requirements, you can also program and develop customized new firmware on your own. My 3D printed model has been verified with the A1 Mini. Given the variations between different 3D printers, I have also uploaded the STP files of the 3D model. You can adjust the tolerance gaps of the model to achieve a better assembly fit. Bill of Materials 1 × ESP32C3 Super Mini Development Board 1 × 0.96-inch SSD1306 I2C OLED Display Module 1 × TP4056 Charging Module 1 × TTP223 Touch Sensor Module 1 × 702025 Specification Battery Assorted Connecting Wires Wiring Reference ESP32C3 Super Mini OLED Moudle TP 4056 TTP 223 Bater 5V OUT+ GND GND OUT- GND 3V3 VCC VCC GPIO 4 I/O GPIO 8 SDA GPIO 9 SCL B + + B- _ Notes The welding direction of the TTP 223 touch sensor is shown in the figure. The touch surface on the other side must be flat so that it can be assembled into the housing. In addition, since no external mechanical switch is equipped for the hardware section, the switching function is implemented via the software of the ESP32-C3. After flashing the Arduino program I uploaded, power-off can be achieved by pressing and holding the TTP223 touch panel for 5 seconds, putting the ESP32 into deep sleep mode. After powering off, pressing and holding the panel for 2 seconds turns the device back on. The sleep mode drastically cuts down battery power consumption. However, the LED power indicator on the ESP32-C3 Mini development board generates substantial leakage current that drains the battery. Therefore, this LED can be damaged using a soldering iron or tweezers to reduce standby power loss. Finally After you finish the hardware soldering work, refer to the attached document for the detailed assembly steps of the casing. Finally, if you like this project, feel free to leave your comments and likes, or give me a free boost.

description: Time to take your Insta360 Luna cinematography to the next level! This sturdy camera rig helps you get low angle shots, sweeping pans and other cinematic shots with more comfort and control. The camera rig has been filed tested with a real Luna Ultra camera and has even been durability tested to make sure it keeps your camera safe. The print is separated into these parts: 1. The Main Handle: The main handle is sized for comfort even with larger hands and also contains the mount point for the Luna detachable screen. The screen connects to this mount point in the same way that it connects to the Luna gimbal body. To disconnect the screen, simply use the same red side buttons that you would normally use to detach the screen from the Luna gimbal body. (Note: please be careful removing supports from the mounting clips) 2. Gimbal Mount Arm: This is the piece that you will mount the main Luna Gimbal body onto. There are (3) ways to mount the Luna Body: (Recommended As Pictured) You can use the Official Luna ¼" Thread Handle along with a standard ¼" Camera thread screw to mount the handle to the Gimbal Mount Arm using the bottom hole and then attached the Luna to the Thread Handle (which comes with every Luna). This is the recommended mounting option for keeping the camera secure while also enabling you to easily detach the Luna from the rig. You can insert the Luna body directly into the slot at the end of the Gimbal Mount Arm then use (2) velcro straps (pictured as red straps in the product renderings) through the holes and around the Luna body to provide 2 layers of support to keep the Luna in place. You can optionally use a combination of options (a) & (b) to provide added stability for action heavy shots by mounting the Luna on the threaded handle with camera screw through bottom and also attaching the (2) velcro straps around the Luna body. 3. The Key: Once you find the desired angle of the Gimbal Mount Arm in relation to the Main Handle, you must insert the Key into the horizontal hole in the Rig joint connection point in order to lock in the angle. The Key has been sized to slide in snuggly to prevent wobble. Keep in mind, the Key must ALWAYS BE INSERTED HORIZONTALLY regardless of the Gimbal arm rotation angle. 4. The Lock: The lock fits into a slot at the end of the Key and holds the key in place while also adding an extra layer of stability. In practice, all of these parts work together to provide a quick and easy usability experience. Rather than messing around with twisting knobs and bolts, you simple remove the key, set the desired angle, put the key and lock back in place and continue filming.

description: 缩小到一米四尺寸的大疆EV50航模。 大疆EV50是大疆近期（2026年七月）发布的一款垂起固定翼无人机，采用了8+3动力布局，我这款是尺寸缩小到1.4米的缩比航模简化为4+1动力配置，空机大约1.1kg(PETG)建议起飞重量≤2.5kg. 说是缩比EV50但其实翼型用的NACA4412并没有和实机一样用那种超厚的看起来像超临界翼型的方案，并且稍微加大了一些机翼弦长以确保刚好的飞行性能。得益于参考机型巨大的机身尺寸，座头鲸同样也获得了巨大的机身空间，即便是6S2P电池放进去也显得非常宽敞，尽管并不建议用难么大的电池。而为什么要做一米四这个尺寸，很大的原因是为了给打印一整架飞机的耗材量刚好能控制在一卷以内或者多出来也不会太多，另外就是考虑到P1S大打印行程，这个巨大的机身确实是太巨大了。 由于参考资料仅仅是DJI官网的几个图片和一段视频所以也有少量额外的比例失真。 这次我开源了整机基础版的STP实体文件，大家可以根据自己的喜好二次编辑，并且可以直接使用Bambu Studio右上角的整体试图参考装配 490*10的碳管一根，主翼梁 500*8的碳管两根 460*2 400*2 120*2 320*1 140*2 这是3毫米碳棒 机臂是两根12*450的碳管 升力电机座可以直接用这种CNC的 如图 尾推电机座孔位和朗宇2814或者2810是一样的 当然其他电机的孔位也是这个，比如我手头刚好有一个兴耀华2820 当然我建议是2814电机就足够了 升力电机建议使用2801或者3110之类能带9到10寸桨的电机，不建议使用四合一电调，散热不好容易宕机，虽然丑一点我还是推荐用4个分体电调。 舵机需要六个，银燕ES08或者PTK7452的尺寸都是可以的 区域的电设诸如飞控之类看自己预算和喜好了，后舱盖的GPS舱可以容纳280尺寸的GPS模块。 因为现在的飞行报备流程太麻烦，所以暂时我也没打算装机试飞，先打出来看看，也只能期待条件比较方便的模友尝试一下了。

description: I have ADHD, and it sounds dumb, but keeping track of what shot I'm on feels like the worst kind of mental math. description: Modular Baseball Pickup Tube *ASSEMBLY AT BOTTOM* This modular baseball pickup tube lets you collect baseballs quickly without repeatedly bending down. Simply press the bottom of the tool over a baseball. The ball pushes past the eight movable flaps and enters the tube, while the flaps return to their starting position to prevent the ball from falling back out. The entire design uses built-in threaded connections , so every section twists directly together. No separate screws, bolts, or connectors are needed. Modular Design Each storage capsule holds approximately four baseballs . You can add more capsule sections to increase the total capacity or use fewer sections for a shorter, lighter collector. Because every part twists together, the tool is easy to: Assemble Disassemble Transport Customize Repair Expand The bottom flap assembly only needs to be printed once. Additional threaded capsule sections can then be added above it as needed, and the handle twists onto the top. How It Works The bottom contains eight one-way flaps . These flaps can move upward when the tool is pressed over a baseball, allowing the ball to enter the tube. Built-in stops prevent the flaps from moving below their original position, which keeps the collected baseballs trapped inside. Assembly Assemble the eight flaps inside the bottom flap holder. (MORE ABOUT THIS AT THE BOTTOM.) Twist the bottom section and flap holder together using the built-in threads. Twist one storage capsule onto the bottom assembly. Add additional capsules by twisting each section together. Twist the handle onto the top capsule. No separate hardware is required for the main assembly. The threads are built directly into the printed parts. Capacity Each capsule holds about four baseballs Add more capsules for greater capacity Remove capsules for a shorter and more portable setup This design is useful for baseball practice, batting drills, coaching, field cleanup, and anyone who wants a simple way to collect balls without constantly bending over. description: Its a (semi-overengineered?) guitar pedal replica / pick holder / fidget / desk toy thing. The compartment has slots for 9 guitar picks. The 3 knobs turn from 7 o'clock to 5 o'clock. The pedal has a printed spring so you can push it like a real one. (Though not super far, I'm still trying to figure out how to make springs. If someone wants to remix it with a better spring, cool.) Everything prints in pieces so you don't need an AMS. (There are two knob plates, one is solid black if you don't have an AMS and the other one does have flush down gray on it, so there is almost no AMS wastage if you want dual color knobs.) Zero supports. You will want super glue for most of the features. Prints in only a few hours. Some assembly notes: The six little dots fit in super easy. I used a dot of glue on each of them. The hardest part was getting them off the plate without losing them. The three knobs snap in and then free rotate while captive. You are going to want to push them rather hard straight down. You will probably use more force than you might be comfortable with, but it will work without breaking. I designed this to have dual color knobs. They only rotate the same distance as the real thing, therefore you want to make sure the knob is at somewhere between 7 and 5 before you snap them down. It's easy to tell if you are using two colors, if you are using only single colors, look inside the knobs and you will see where the cutout is and is not. You have a pretty wide margin of error. The two little black bolts are the hinges for the lid. They fit snug through the lid and looser into the base. Still I recommend a bit of glue near the head, so it firmly attaches to the lid while letting the deeper part rotate freely. The spring is asymmetrical. It matches the contour of the rim of the base.

Although its protection and firepower were impressive, the Maus was very slow, difficult to transport, and required enormous amounts of fuel, making it impractical for battlefield use. Only two Maus prototypes were built before the war ended, and neither saw combat. The project was cancelled because Germany faced shortages of resources and changing military priorities. Crews praised its reliability and low profile, which made it harder for enemy forces to spot. Although it was not as heavily armed or armoured as some German tanks, its mobility allowed it to outmanoeuvre opponents and support Allied advances across France, Belgium, and the Netherlands. The Cromwell remained in service after the war and influenced the design of the improved Comet tank. description: I wanted a companion cube cover for the Steam Machine that didn't require a bunch of magnets, screws and other BOM parts to put together. Here is a simple model sliced and designed for printing multi-color with an AMS! Designed with airflow in mind! I designed this to line up with the existing Steam Machine vents and air intake as best as possible given that we are putting a cover over-top of the entire device. The cover does not completely seal the device to the surface it is placed on, there are cutouts on the front and sides to aid in airflow to the bottom of the device (it sits on it's standoffs as designed) Back of the Steam Machine is left completely open for optimal airflow, cable routing, etc. I haven't noticed any issues with temps after installing mine, but you can also remove the faceplate to the steam machine before installing the cover to increase airflow Print Settings and Instructions: Either print it by the plate and assemble with 3D printed dowels (recommend some CA glue or similar) or as a single large print. There is a “Test Fitting” plate so you can make sure everything will fit before committing to the whole build. Supports are needed for at least the front faceplate, I'd recommend using them throughout for the dowel holes. Recommend 3 walls, 10% infill (gyroid or w/e you prefer) If the dowels don't fit you can size them down slightly A couple extra snap dowels are added, in case of breakage during install. Print extra's if you need. Test print should fit flush with the surface and around the Steam Machine, there should be no force required. USB and Power buttons, light bar should be lined up. Assembly Instructions: (if you did not print the All-In-One) You can use the snap dowel pins for glue-less assembly. Front face installs last. Otherwise Tools recommended - clamps wide enough to accommodate the cube, Super glue (CA Glue). If you do not have clamps you can do each side 1 at a time, just make sure it sets as square as possible. Install all faces in one session: Glue dowels into top face Apply glue to left and right faces and attach to top Install and glue any remaining dowels for the front face Glue and place front face Clamp together and let everything set Future Work: Button insert - right now you can use your pinky finger or lift the cover if you need to use the power button. SD Card slot, I had this in during the design phase, but I doubt people are hot-swapping SD cards in this thing, and it was more aesthetically pleasing to have one without the extra hole. (I'm not sure you could easily get it out anyway even if there was a hole, but if folks want it I can certainly add it back!) Snap Dowels for glue-less assembly - COMPLETE Changelog: Revision 1 (R1): 7/27/26 Shrunk dowel size by 0.2mm in length - if dowels are too long for a flush fit, you can shrink them more if needed. Updated some painting around edges Revision 2 (R2): 7/28/26 Added snap-fit dowels to aid assembly

description: Fishing Dehooker Designed for Safe and Controlled Hook Removal. This compact fishing dehooker has been designed to make hook removal safer, easier and more controlled while protecting both the hook point and your hands. Every detail has been carefully designed with three goals in mind: functionality, ergonomics and printability . The internal hook channel guides and protects the hook during removal, while the ergonomic fuzzy grip provides a secure and comfortable hold, even with wet hands. Features ✔ Protected hook channel ✔ Optimized hook guidance ✔ Ergonomic fuzzy grip ✔ Reinforced lanyard eyelet ✔ Lightweight and durable ✔ Optimized print profile included Design Highlights Protected Hook The internal channel is carefully shaped to keep the hook point and part of the shank protected inside the tool during hook removal, improving safety and reducing the risk of accidental snagging. Optimized Hook Channel The hook channel follows the natural profile of common fishing hooks, guiding the hook smoothly during extraction while maintaining excellent control, especially with small and medium-sized hooks. Lanyard Ready The reinforced eyelet allows the dehooker to be attached to retractable zingers, lanyards or key rings, keeping it always within easy reach while fishing. Printing Notes For the best results, please use the included print profile. The dehooker is intentionally printed suspended above the build plate , exactly as configured in the supplied print profile. This is a deliberate design choice rather than simply a printing preference. Printing the model in this orientation provides several important advantages: A uniform surface finish around the entire circumference of the handle, including the fuzzy grip texture. description: Say goodbye to a wet back and butt with this Tesla air conditioning kit for ventilated seat covers. (Without cover not tested) I bought ventilated seat covers for my 2022 Model 3, which was great—they keep you dry—but your back and butt still get hot when you get into a car that’s been sitting in the sun for 9 hours, even if it’s been pre-conditioned. So I designed a system that lets the rear AC to circulate cool air across your back and seat through an aftermarket ventilated seat cover—you can easily find these online; they’re the same models everywhere. The cover really helps distribute the cool airflow—the feeling is truly revolutionary. I’m not sure if this works well without the seat cover. I think you’d feel the plastic in your body since there isn’t the thickness of the cover to cushion it, but you can give it a try by You can cut in Bambu Studio the diffuser extensions to match your body, and driving position. Or simply don't fit the diffuser extensions, at least you will feel the AC at the bottom of your back for sure. But the seat cover creates a sort of tunnel that allows air to flow under your body without you blocking the airflow, all that with 10x fans, that's what makes the difference. Compatible with Model 3 and Model Y through 2023 (until the seat design changes). It may be compatible with the new Model 3 and Model Y, but I haven't been able to test it. By the way, if you're sensitive to the cold, you can turn on the heater in the winter in addition to the standard heated seats. Warning : Please note that is a DIY project and each driver have different driving/seat position so you may modify some pieces. Maybe you can use TPU to make flexible extension so that it would be more compatible without any modifications. You can try to heat the parts with heat gun to give it the form you want. The diffuser was designed for my seat adjustment; the angle of the seatback might restrict the diffuser. I'm providing a 2D drawing of the diffuser's profile so you can check if it would fit your setup. Otherwise, perhaps when installing the heater, you could adapt it to your setup—since it's a complex part, I haven't created any other versions. It's recommended to print it in heat resistant material like ABS, ASA, (maybe PETG but my car get 74°C at max), you can just try in PLA if you have the cabin overheat protection (that's how I made my first prototype to see if it worth it and damn it worth it !) Warping can be a bit annoying but doesn't prevent the assembly. I strongly recommend to print at 50% to avoid support at 45°. 60° overhang angle print good and I prefer to be safe and print slowly Assembly : First, You need to unclip the two elastic straps under the seat, at the back, that hold the small piece of leather cover in place. (white piece on my rear photo) Insert the main diffuser in the seat by the front to the rear, clip the diffuser extensions Insert 3x M6 nuts (or only 2) in the rear plenum, connect the rear plenum on the main diffuser with at least 2 screws to lock it Connect the 2x parts of the "Rear AC diffuser 2x Ø50 mm" by gluing them or using 4x plastic screw Put some sticky foam all around the part who goes in the Tesla vent, it make sure the part fits securely in the car, it prevent from moving. Be sure to make foam opening for the flaps like on photos I recommend to put foam around the flat surface to prevent from air leaks, it's a bit of a DIY I know, but it's worth it. Connect Ø50 mm air hoses with zip ties or collar to the plenum and to the the rear AC cover. If you have a ventilated seat cover then try to put the diffuser extensions (for butt and back) in the seat cover opening to really force the air to go in the seat cover, like sealing. For those who test without cover, feel free to share your felling :)

description: Dayton Audio Reference Series 2.1 - Speakers & Sub Based on the Dayton Audio Reference collection, a 2.1 speaker system running the RS100-8 4" full range driver, the RSS210HO-8 8" subwoofer and SPA300-D 300 Watt plate amplifier. The left and right speaker need to be run from a dedicated amplifier, with lowpass/subwoofer output that can pass to the subwoofers dedicated amplifier. The main left and right speaker are slot ported and are in 2 pieces to allow for easy removal of supports. The subwoofer is a sealed enclosure with heavy bracing and with the plate amplifier sealed in it's own box. The full range drivers are 30W @ 8ohms so very easy to drive. Although the plate amplifier is 300W @ 4ohms and the subwoofer is 300W @ 8ohms, the plate amplifier still drives the subwoofer very well and gets very loud. I run the speakers as my daily's from my Fosi ZA3 and ZH3 Stack (see my other models for the Z Stack housing!) and it sounds GREAT! Each enclosure is printed at 30% infill to prevent resonance. The main left and right speakers have a selection of feet, from 5 degree and 10 degree feet and stands, these all share the same fitting dimensions and can easily be swapped out. Required parts: 2x Dayton Audio RS100-8 4" driver 1x Dayton Audio RSS210HO-8 8" subwoofer 1x Dayton Audio SPA300-D plate amplifier 2x Dayton Audio BPA-38G binding post (pair) 1m speaker cable Spade connectors 32x CNC Kitchen M4x8.1 threaded inserts - 10x per speaker, 22x for subwoofer M4 screws - 6x black dome head per speaker, 18x black dome head for subwoofer and plate amp, 4x countersunk per set of feet CA Glue Adhesive Rubber feet (optional - helps stop the speakers slipping or vibrating on hard surfaces) Printing: I used Bambu PLA Basic for the enclosures and Bambu PLA Matte for the feet. I have found this to be perfectly strong enough with 30% infill and 4 wall loops. This may be overkill but the enclosures have come out strong and to my ear sound great. The subwoofer enclosure was obviously an extremely long and filament consuming print, at 2.8Kg and 2 days, 12 hours. The speaker enclosures come in at 1.2Kg and 24 hours each (for both enclosure and rear panel). The print profiles are my recommended settings and orientation. I printed each enclosure face down on the Smooth PEI plate. I ended up making the main speakers 2 piece as after several attempts at an fully enclosed version and needing to use strong supports, I found I could not extract the supports via the small speaker opening. No such issues with the subwoofer as obviously the much larger speaker opening. Assembly: Left and Right speakers Remove all print supports and make sure all faces are clean and clear of any lumps or bumps. Especially the interface with the speaker rubber gasket and the rear panel V groove. Press in the threaded inserts to the base for the feet and front baffle for the speaker. Careful not to press too hard as the threaded inserts and heat can cause the rear of the front panel to melt through. Press in the binding posts to the rear panel before attaching the panel to the main enclosure. I found with some other filaments (e.g. Sunlu) the binding post holes ended up slightly smaller and needed a lot of force to press in. Bambu PLA did not seem to have this issue. If in doubt try a bit of heat on the binding post to press it in, the same as a threaded insert. DO NOT try and pull the posts in by stressing the inside bolts, they are soft metal and the threads will strip. Apply a thin layer of CA glue to the V groove in the back of the enclosure and carefully press into place the rear panel. The panel should be a tight fit but end up flush with the rear of the enclosure. DO NOT apply too much glue or it will just leak into the enclosure and make a mess. Clamp (or apply weight) and let the glue dry. Add the fixings/nuts to the inside of the binding posts and attach a suitable length of speaker cable (approx 6 inches) using spade or the circular terminals that came with the posts. Add spade connectors to the other end of the cable to fit onto the speaker. Attach the cable to the speaker and lower the speaker into plate, carefully as the speaker terminals may need to be maneuvered around the edge of the opening. Screw the speakers into place. Screw the feet to the enclosure. Subwoofer Remove all print supports and make sure all faces are clean and clear of any lumps or bumps. Especially the interface with the speaker rubber gasket and plate amplifier. Also check that the small hole that passes the speaker cable from the amp to the main enclosure is free from any sharp edges. Press in the threaded inserts to the base for the feet, front baffle for the speaker and plate amplifier. Careful not to press too hard as the threaded inserts and heat can cause the rear of the front panel to melt through. Peel enough protective/anti-vibration foam covering from the speaker cable that is soldered to the plate amplifier to reach where the subwoofer speaker terminals will be located. If in doubt peel more rather than less, as trying to remove more after starting to pull the cable through the hole is very tricky. Carefully feed the plate amplifier speaker cable through the small hole from the plate amplifier enclosure into the main speaker enclosure. Try not to pull too much speaker cable through as it could vibrate against the enclosure if there is too much slack. Screw the plate amplifier to the enclosure. Strip approx 10mm of the end of the speaker cable. Start to lower the subwoofer into the enclosure and insert the speaker cable into the spring loaded terminals. Another pair of hands is helpful with this part. Screw the subwoofer into place. Screw the feet to the enclosure. Operation IMPORTANT - Depending on your location, the plate amplifier can be set to 110V or 240V. YOU MUST SET THE VOLTAGE SELECTOR AND INSTALL THE CORRECT FUSE FOR YOUR SUPPLY VOLTAGE. If you don't do this you could start blowing fuses, tripping breakers, or worse. Read the plate amplifier instructions on how to set the various switches and dials. Likewise check your amplifier specification and instructions before connecting anything and powering it on just to make sure everything is correctly set up! Attach the left and right speakers to your amplifier with speaker cable. Attach the plate amplifier to your amplifier lowpass/subwoofer out with an RCA/phono cable/Y-cable (per Dayton and your amplifier vendor instructions). Set the subwoofer plate amplifier volume to low and power on the plate amplifier, gradually adjust (per the Dayton instructions) to suit your listening requirements.

description: Create a custom-fit enclosure for almost any small electronics project directly in MakerWorld’s Parametric Model Maker or OpenSCAD. Enter the dimensions of your PCB, choose the lid style, position the required connector openings, and generate a ready-to-print project box sized specifically for your hardware. The model supports Raspberry Pi boards, ESP32 projects, Arduino-compatible boards, sensor modules, custom PCBs, battery-powered devices, and many other electronics projects. Unlike a fixed enclosure, this generator lets you adjust the case around your board instead of designing your project around an existing box. Main Features Enclosure dimensions generated from PCB measurements Adjustable clearance around and above the board Separate printable base and lid Screw-fastened, snap-fit, or friction-fit lid options Up to eight independently configurable connector openings Openings can be placed on any side of the enclosure Adjustable port width, height, position, and corner radius Four configurable PCB mounting posts Adjustable mounting-hole spacing and pattern offset Slotted or honeycomb lid ventilation Optional embossed or recessed lid label Optional wall-mounting tabs Rounded enclosure corners Adjustable wall, floor, and lid thickness PCB and component-volume preview for checking fit Print-plate layout for producing the base and lid together Small tolerance test part for checking lid fit before printing the complete case Supported Projects The generator can be used for projects such as: Raspberry Pi Zero and similar single-board computers ESP32, ESP8266, and RP2040 projects Arduino and compatible development boards Custom PCBs Sensor and monitoring devices Home automation controllers LED controllers Battery-powered electronics USB adapters and interface boards Small power supplies Prototype electronics Wall-mounted control modules Configuring the Enclosure Begin by entering the dimensions of your PCB: PCB length PCB width PCB thickness Maximum component height If the board includes mounting holes, enable the PCB posts and enter the mounting-hole spacing. The complete mounting pattern can also be shifted to support boards whose holes are not centred. Connector openings are configured individually. Each opening has controls for: Enabled or disabled Enclosure side Horizontal position Vertical position Width Height Corner radius This allows the enclosure generator to support USB, HDMI, power, Ethernet, switches, buttons, displays, ribbon cables, SD cards, and other connectors. Lid Options Friction-Fit Lid The lid is held in place by a fitted internal skirt. This is a good choice for enclosures that need occasional access and do not require tools. Snap-Fit Lid Flexible clips retain the lid without screws. This is useful for compact consumer-style enclosures, although fit may depend on material choice and printer calibration. Screw-Fastened Lid The lid is secured using screws positioned near the enclosure corners. This is the most secure option for permanent installations, wall-mounted projects, and enclosures that may be handled frequently. Ventilation The lid can be produced with: No ventilation Parallel ventilation slots Honeycomb ventilation Vent dimensions and density can be adjusted to suit the amount of airflow required. Ventilation is recommended for processors, voltage regulators, power supplies, LED controllers, and other components that generate heat. Labels An optional label can be added to the lid as either: Raised text Recessed text This can be used for project names, device identifiers, voltage labels, room names, network roles, or assembly markings. Wall Mounting Optional mounting tabs can be added to the enclosure for installation on a wall, panel, cabinet, workbench, or other flat surface. The tab dimensions and mounting-hole diameter can be adjusted for the fasteners being used. Recommended Workflow Measure the PCB and its tallest components. Enter the PCB dimensions and clearances. Configure the mounting-hole pattern. Add openings for every required connector. Render the assembled preview. Confirm that the PCB and component preview do not intersect the case. Print the tolerance test. Adjust the lid clearance if required. Generate and print the base and lid. Always measure the actual board and cables when possible. Manufacturer drawings describe the PCB and connector locations, but some cable plugs have oversized moulded housings that require additional clearance. Printing Recommendations Suggested starting settings: Layer height: 0.20 mm Walls: 3 or more Top and bottom layers: 4 or more Infill: 15–25% Supports: normally not required Base orientation: open side facing upward Lid orientation: outside surface on the build plate PLA is suitable for most indoor electronics projects. PETG is recommended for warmer environments, wall-mounted installations, and parts that require more durable snap features. For PETG or printers with tighter tolerances, slightly increase the lid-fit clearance before printing the full enclosure. Screw and Post Notes The PCB mounting-post holes are intended as printable pilot holes. Final screw fit depends on the printer, material, extrusion width, and type of screw being used. For critical assemblies, print a small test or drill the holes to the required finished diameter. Do not overtighten screws against a PCB. Nylon washers or small printed spacers may be useful for boards with exposed traces near the mounting holes. Important Limitations This generator uses rectangular, rounded connector openings on the enclosure walls. It does not currently generate: Arbitrary SVG-shaped wall cutouts Lid-mounted rectangular connector cutouts Automatic connector detection from PCB files Waterproof seals Integrated hinges Cable glands DIN-rail clips These features may be added in future versions. MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker The model is organized with simple exposed controls intended to work well in MakerWorld’s Parametric Model Maker. All connector file paths and complex data structures have been avoided so that the model can be customized without editing the source code. For advanced customization, the OpenSCAD source can also be downloaded and modified locally. Share Your Presets This generator can produce a large range of project-specific enclosures. Consider sharing your successful settings and print profiles for popular boards so other makers can quickly generate compatible cases. Please include the exact board revision when sharing a preset, as connector and mounting-hole positions can differ between versions.

Here is my version of a DIY Loadcell handbrake. I see some bought handbrakes and diy brakes put the lever farther away from the hand and some placing the loadcell at an angle, needing additional parts for leverage. I wanted it to be a simple direct connection with the lever closest to me since I put it next to my wheelbase. The cost is around $25 depending on if you have somethings stuff already. The most expensive part is the loadcell that I found for $16. Printed parts 1 - Lever - 6 walls and 10% gyroid infill and it has held up well. 2 - Base - 6 walls and 10% gyroid infill and it has held up well. 3 - Lever Spacers - 4 walls and 10% gyroid infill. 4 - 8mm pin - 6 walls 5 - Arduino box - 3 walls 6 - Bushings - TPU - 4 walls and 10% infill 7 - 5mm rod guides (if you use springs larger than the spring I used then the rod can move around and touch the spring while in movement, I added example rod centering spacers (16mm and 20mm) to keep the rod centered. I used PLA plus filament except for the bushings that are TPU. If you are unsure, or you shift like the hulk or are using a filament at is not that strong you can increase the walls to 8, 10, 12 or just print at 100% infill. The bushings I printed with TPU, 4 walls 15% grid infill. You can play with this to change the feel of the last stage of the pull. BOM (purchased parts) 1 - 200kg Loadcell (Qty 1) . It's needs to be this one or have the same the dimensions and hole patterns as this one due to the center hole for the spring guide rod/screw. NA151 60kg 100kg 200kg Commitment To 15Days To Arrive, New ($16) 2 - M5 x 100mm screw (Spring guide rod) (Qty 1) - This is what I had lying around and the length worked out fine adjusting the TPU bushings size to make it fit together. If you use a longer or shorter screw you will need to adjust the bushings accordingly. 3 - 5mm Rod end ball joint - Right Thread SI5 5mm (Qty 1) 5mm6mm8mm10mm12mm Rod End Male/Female SA SI T/K POSA8 PHSA8 Ball Joint Metric Threaded Rod End Bearing - AliExpress 13 4 - M4 screw 25mm or longer (and M4 Nut) (Qty 1) - To connect Rod end to the lever. 5 - Springs (Qty 1)- I used a 40mm x 12mm x 10mm Red spring that I had lying around. You can change the spring to whatever you have available or play with different spring setups. You can use to two smaller springs with different strengths. Wider springs, softer, stiffer, wider bushings and print different TPU bushings (elastomers). You will need to adjust the lengths of the bushings accordingly as you change the length. 6 - Washers (Qty 4) - I used 5mm x 12mm since I had them. If you use wider (larger diameter springs then use wider washers/bushings to match). 7 - M6 x 45mm screws (full thread) (Qty 2) - to bolt the loadcell to the base. They can also be 35mm but 45mm is best to pass through the sensor completely. 8 - Arduino pro micro - New Pro Micro for arduino ATmega32U4 Module with 2 row pin header For Leonardo in stock . best quality - AliExpress 502 9 - HX711 board - I would use this one. 1-10pcs HX711 Weighing Sensor 24-bit A/D Conversion Adapter Load Cell Amplifier Board Weight Sensors - AliExpress 502 There are different hx711 board versions. I recommend this one. It is larger, so it is easier to work with also with the HX711 you need to change read frequency (rate) from 10hz to 80hzx (10hz is too slow to read the data we need). This particular purple board version has an area on the back you just slice the connection between two pads with a razor and it changes it to 80hz. 10 - M8 x 45mm screw and nut (Qty 1) (optional) - You can either print the 8mm pin I made for the lever or use a M8x45mm screw. The 3d pin has worked fine. Print the base as it is oriented in in the file, on the side face. That is to maximize the strength due the layer lines. Printing it standing up will make it weak and prone to break due to layer lines. Here is the Arduino code to upload: #include #include // HX711 pins #define LOADCELL_DOUT_PIN 3 #define LOADCELL_SCK_PIN 2 HX711 scale; // Change this after calibration - - I left this as is. float calibration_factor = -9000.0; // Adjustable max force (kg) to reach 100% float maxForce = 120.0; // You can change this but would leave it at 120. If set to 200 it requires a lot of force to reach max pull. // Non-linear curve strength (1.0 = linear, 2.0 = strong curve) - You can play with this to change the “feel” of the end range of pull. float curve = 1.8; // HID Joystick object Joystick_ Joystick(JOYSTICK_DEFAULT_REPORT_ID, JOYSTICK_TYPE_GAMEPAD, 0, 0, false, false, true, // Z-axis only false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false); void setup() { Serial.begin(9600); scale.begin(LOADCELL_DOUT_PIN, LOADCELL_SCK_PIN); scale.set_scale(calibration_factor); scale.tare(); Joystick.begin(); } void loop() { if (scale.is_ready()) { float weight = scale.get_units(5); if (weight < 0) weight = 0; // Limit to maxForce if (weight > maxForce) weight = maxForce; // Normalize 0–1 float normalized = weight / maxForce; // Apply non-linear curve float curved = pow(normalized, curve); // Convert to HID 0–1023 int joyValue = curved * 1023.0; if (joyValue < 0) joyValue = 0; if (joyValue > 1023) joyValue = 1023; Joystick.setZAxis(joyValue); Serial.print("Raw kg: "); Serial.print(weight); Serial.print(" | Normalized: "); Serial.print(normalized); Serial.print(" | Curved: "); Serial.print(curved); Serial.print(" | HID: "); Serial.println(joyValue); } delay(5); } Assembly: Insert loadcell from the bottom upwards into the base (it will be a snug fit). Make sure the arrow on the loadcell is pointing towards the rear. I made the hole placement randomly with no meaningful spacing for a particular rig. I just drilled new holes into the plate. Place the lever base on the area want it and bolt it down. I recommend using all 3 holes in the front since that is where it receives the most force. Then place the two M6x45mm screws to secure the load cell to the base. They can be M6x35mm minimum. I like 45mm so they enter the other end of the base for added distribution of force/support. Place a spacer, insert the pin, then the lever, push the pin, then place the other spacer and push the pin through. I made the spacers a tight fit very tight to keep the lever from wiggling. You could print the spacers 0.5 shorter to make it easier. insert with the 3d printed M8 pin or M8 screw. Place the 4mm M4 rod end into the lever and secure it with the M4 x 40mm screw and nut. Take the M5x100 screw and place: washer > spring > washer > bushing > washer. Then insert that into the into the loadcell in the direction of the arrow. Then on the other end place a washer > bushing > washer and screw it into the rod end that's in the lever already. Program the Arduino (I will not cover this as there is a ton of info/videos on this) Just make sure your Arduino IDE Software you add the library for : 1 - joystick.h 2 - hx711.h Arduino + HX711 wiring The hx711 5 pins that are color coded go to the same colors on the loadcell sensor wire. The loadcell sensor silver/clear wire goes the yellow (for ground/noise) hx711 - VCC to Pro micro pin 2 hx711 - CLk to Pro micro pin 3 hx711 - GND to Pro micro pin GND hx711 - DAT to Pro micro pin 3 (goes to pin 3 or others on this side at the loadcell is a digital not analog). Cut between the two pads marked as RATE on the rear of the HX711 to convert it to 80hz Take the soldered boards insert them into the box/housing. Mault, a MTG card scanner/sorter. I built a machine that scans Magic cards with a webcam, identifies them with an AI model, and sorts them into bins with an Arduino + servos. Posting the whole thing here in case anyone wants to build their own or mess with the design. How it works: A feeder servo pulls a card into view of a webcam, it gets cropped and identified automatically, then you set up whatever sorting rules you want (color, rarity, price, set, whatever) in a small web app. The Arduino handles the actual routing, trapdoor/paddle/pusher servos push the card into the right bin. What's here: - 3D files for the enclosure and modules (Fusion 360 source + a ready-to-print .3mf) - Arduino sketch, wiring diagrams, BOM - The web app source (handles the AI identification, bin config, calibration, etc.) - A build guide (Currently being worked on so it may change) BOM at a glance: Arduino Uno R4 Minima, a PCA9685 servo driver, a handful of SG90 servos, an IR sensor for feed detection. It's all open source, with the full code on GitHub: https://github.com/dishwasher-detergent/mault . Print it, change it, use a different card game rule set, whatever. If you build one or improve on the design I'd really like to see it, and if you run into issues or want to fix something, PRs/issues are open. description: Tesla Model Y A-Pillar Gutter (washer fluid deflector) Why I made this At highway speed a lot of the windshield washer fluid gets pushed around the side of the windshield and runs down the driver's side window. You end up cleaning the windshield and dirtying the side glass in the same action. With the window open, some of it comes in. This gutter mounts on the A-pillar and catches that flow before it wraps around the corner, directing it up over the roof instead. Design I kept it as small and low profile as I could while still catching the fluid, since I didn't want a visible accessory stuck to the car. It isn't very noticeable unless you're looking for it. The profile is thin enough to flex, so it conforms to the curve of the A-pillar when you press it down instead of needing to match the contour exactly. I designed and tested this on a Model Y. The Model 3 pillar geometry is close enough that it should fit, but I haven't tried it. If you do, let me know how it goes. Print settings Material: PCTG-CF Anneal it before mounting I used PCTG-CF for the heat stability. A car exterior sitting in direct sun gets well above air temperature, and a part that softens will lose its shape on the first hot day, taking the VHB bond with it. PCTG-CF holds up better than PETG in that environment, and the carbon fill helps it keep its shape. Annealing I annealed it in the printer rather than an oven: Take the part off the build plate after printing. Tape it back down to the plate with blue painter's tape. This holds it flat while it's soft and stops it curling. Heat the chamber to 65C and the plate to 80C. Leave it for 60 minutes. Let everything cool down before removing it. This needs an enclosed printer to hold chamber temperature. Without one, an oven at a similar temperature is the usual alternative, but I haven't tested that myself. Mounting It attaches with VHB tape. Clean the mounting area on the A-pillar with isopropyl alcohol and let it dry fully. Wax or road film left on the paint will cause the tape to release later. Apply the VHB to the part first, then position it on the car. Press firmly along the whole length. VHB needs pressure to bond properly. Do this in warm conditions if you can, as VHB adheres poorly in the cold. Wait a day or two before washing the car or driving in heavy rain. The bond continues gaining strength over the first 24 to 72 hours. To remove it later, work a length of fishing line behind the part to cut through the tape without damaging the paint. If you print one Post a make. I'd like to hear from anyone running it on a Model 3, and from anyone in a hot climate on how it holds up over a summer.

model_name: Trotec PAC 2020 E – Dual Hose Adapter
description: Overview This project converts the Trotec PAC 2020 E from a single-hose to a dual-hose portable air conditioner. The original unit uses conditioned indoor air to cool the condenser and exhausts this air outside. This creates a slight negative pressure inside the room, causing warm outside air to enter through doors, windows and other leaks. With this modification the condenser is supplied with fresh outdoor air , while the hot exhaust air is still discharged outdoors. This greatly reduces the negative pressure inside the room and improves the overall cooling efficiency. Features ✅ Dual-hose conversion for the Trotec PAC 2020 E ✅ Designed for 16 mm twin-wall polycarbonate (multiwall) sheets ✅ Secure hose connection with integrated retaining bead (hose won't slip off) ✅ Tool-free installation into the air conditioner ✅ Tight fit without additional adapters ✅ Perfect for removable summer window inserts Required Parts In addition to the printed parts you will need: 16 mm twin-wall polycarbonate sheet 150 mm aluminium flexible duct (inside diameter) for the fresh air intake Original Trotec exhaust hose Fly screen (recommended) Suitable adhesive for bonding the inner and outer window rings The hose connector is specifically designed for 150 mm inner diameter aluminium ducting . The integrated retaining bead keeps the hose securely attached during operation without requiring hose clamps. Window Insert The window insert is designed for a 16 mm polycarbonate twin-wall sheet . Simply cut two circular openings into the sheet and install the printed adapters. The insert can easily be removed after the summer season without modifying the window. Hose Connection The hose connectors include an integrated retaining bead . This prevents the flexible air hoses from slipping off during operation while still allowing easy installation without hose clamps. Outdoor Air Intake Installing a fly screen on the outside air intake is highly recommended. This prevents insects, leaves and larger debris from entering the air conditioner while having almost no impact on airflow. Assembly Print all parts. Cut two openings into the 16 mm polycarbonate twin-wall sheet . Use the inner ring as a template to mark the cutout. Cut the openings as accurately as possible to ensure a snug fit. Place the fresh air intake below the exhaust opening. Position the exhaust opening above the fresh air intake. Place the outer window ring on the outside of the polycarbonate sheet. Lay the fly screen over the outer ring. Apply adhesive to the inner retaining ring. Press the inner ring into the outer ring, clamping the fly screen securely between the outer ring and the polycarbonate sheet. Allow the adhesive to cure completely. Connect the original Trotec exhaust hose and the 150 mm aluminium intake duct . Important For the best cooling performance, always install the exhaust opening above the fresh air intake . Since warm air naturally rises, placing the exhaust above the intake minimizes the risk of recirculating hot exhaust air. Material Recommendation I printed all parts in ASA because it offers: excellent heat resistance UV resistance high mechanical strength good dimensional stability PETG should also work well if the parts are not exposed to direct sunlight for long periods. Print Settings Layer Height: 0.30 mm Nozzle: 0.6 mm 3-4 Walls 20–30 % Gyroid Infill Material: ASA (recommended) Supports ✅ Trotec Adapter: No supports required ✅ Outer Window Ring: No supports required ⚠️ Inner Window Ring: Supports required Only the inner ring contains overhangs that require support material. The remaining parts have been designed to print support-free. Results After installing the dual-hose conversion I measured the following performance: Outdoor temperature: ~30 °C Supply air temperature: ~12 °C Exhaust air temperature: ~40 °C One children's room cooled from 25 °C to below 20 °C With both bedroom doors open, the complete upper floor stabilized at approximately 23 °C , even in full sunshine. These results were measured using Home Assistant temperature sensors and represent real-world performance in my home. Notes This model was designed specifically for the Trotec PAC 2020 E . It may fit other models with a similar rear housing, but this has not been tested. If you build one, I'd love to see your make! A split version of the Trotec adapter is included for printers with a 256 × 256 mm build volume (e.g. Bambu Lab P1, X1 and A1 series). Simply bond the three printed parts together before installation.

description: Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig A Mechanical Z-Axis Stabilization Platform for Insta360 The Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig is a compact, scientifically designed mechanical stabilization system developed specifically around the Insta360 Luna Ultra . It reduces vertical impacts, vibration, and sudden motion before those disturbances reach the camera’s gimbal and imaging system. Unlike rigid mounts, which transfer nearly all movement directly into the camera, this design places the Luna Ultra on a suspended carriage supported by an adjustable spring and oil-damped shock absorber. The mechanical suspension manages larger physical disturbances, while the Luna Ultra’s internal gimbal and electronic stabilization correct the remaining fine motion. The rig is designed primarily around the Luna Ultra’s geometry, controls, gimbal clearance, and remote-operation capabilities. Its modular mounting interface can also be adapted for other compatible Insta360 cameras. Design Objective The project was developed to create a practical, 3D-printable Z-axis isolation system that could be used across multiple filming environments without restricting the operation of the Luna Ultra. The main design requirements were: Reduce vertically transmitted shock and vibration Preserve unrestricted gimbal movement Maintain access to controls, ports, screen, microphones, and cooling areas Support handheld, tripod, bicycle, pole, suction-cup, and vehicle-mounted use Use readily available hardware Remain easy to print, assemble, maintain, and customise Avoid specialised machining The result is a lightweight mechanical isolation platform that works with the Luna Ultra rather than replacing its existing stabilization system. How the System Works? The Luna Ultra is mounted on a vertically suspended carriage rather than being rigidly connected to the lower mounting structure. The carriage is guided by a bearing-supported linkage and controlled by an adjustable spring and hydraulic oil damper. When the lower mount experiences a vertical disturbance, such as a footstep, road impact, bicycle vibration, or sudden vehicle movement, the lower structure moves first. The suspended camera carriage is allowed to move relative to the frame, reducing the acceleration transmitted directly to the camera. The suspension behaves approximately as a spring–mass–damper system: where: m is the suspended mass of the Luna Ultra and camera carriage k is the effective spring stiffness c is the hydraulic damping coefficient F(t) is the disturbance entering through the handle or mount x is the relative displacement of the suspended carriage The coil spring supports the camera mass and absorbs impact energy during compression. The oil damper controls the velocity of the motion and dissipates energy during compression and rebound. This prevents the repeated bouncing commonly associated with spring-only stabilizers. The mechanical suspension therefore removes a portion of the larger vertical disturbance before it reaches the Luna Ultra. The camera’s gimbal and electronic stabilization then correct the lower-amplitude residual motion. Testing & Validation A preliminary performance assessment was conducted using the Insta360 Luna Ultra payload, approximately 233–235 g, together with the adjustable piggyback oil-damped suspension used in the design. The assessment compares the expected vibration transmitted through a conventional rigid mount with the Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig during walking, running, cycling, vehicle mounting, and rough-terrain use. The values below are simulated engineering estimates intended to represent realistic prototype performance rather than instrumented physical test results. The suspension was tuned to keep the camera near the centre of its available travel, preserving compression and rebound capacity while reducing vertical shock transmission. The bearing-guided linkage and hydraulic damping provide the greatest improvement during higher-frequency vibration, such as gravel cycling and vehicle use, while still reducing the repetitive vertical motion associated with walking and running. The design also maintains clearance around the Luna Ultra’s gimbal, ports, controls, detachable display, and camera body throughout the simulated motion range. * Future physical validation should compare the rig against a rigid mount using accelerometers, suspension-displacement tracking, high-speed video, and frame-by-frame footage analysis. Testing should also verify fastener retention, bearing wear, structural fatigue, gimbal clearance, and material performance. The current prototype uses PLA with TPU grip components, while PETG or ABS is recommended for functional real-world testing and repeated dynamic use. The shock absorber provides three primary functions: Supporting the suspended camera mass Controlling compression under impact Controlling rebound as the carriage returns to its neutral position The threaded adjustment collar allows the spring preload to be changed according to the installed camera mass and the desired suspension response. A softer setup can improve sensitivity to walking and smaller vibrations, while a firmer setup may be more appropriate for bicycle, off-road, or vehicle-mounted use. The suspension should be adjusted so the Luna Ultra carriage rests near the middle of its available travel. This provides sufficient movement in both compression and rebound and reduces the risk of bottoming out or reaching full extension. The shock absorber is connected to the printed suspension structure using two M2 × 16 mm screws , one at each mounting point. Hybrid Manufacturing Approach The rig employs a hybrid manufacturing approach , combining custom 3D-printed structural components with commercially available precision mechanical hardware. Rather than attempting to manufacture every component through additive manufacturing, each element is produced using the process best suited to its mechanical function. The primary structural components, including the main frame, suspension carriage, linkage arms, camera interface, bearing housings, and universal mounting platform, are 3D printed. Precision motion and high-load interfaces are achieved using commercially available metal hardware, including an adjustable oil-damped shock absorber, sealed ball bearings, steel fasteners, and standard mechanical hardware. This combination provides the flexibility of additive manufacturing while maintaining the durability, precision, and reliability of conventional mechanical components. For the prototype presented in this project, the majority of the structural components are printed in PLA , while the handle grip and contact surfaces are printed in TPU to improve ergonomics, provide a more secure grip, and reduce high-frequency vibrations transmitted to the user. For long-term functional use, however, PETG, ABS, or ASA are strongly recommended for the structural components due to their superior impact resistance, fatigue performance, temperature stability, and outdoor durability. These materials are better suited for repeated dynamic loading and demanding environments such as automotive, cycling, and outdoor filming. TPU should continue to be used for the grip sections where flexibility, comfort, and vibration damping are beneficial. This hybrid approach offers several engineering advantages: Lightweight yet rigid printed structure Precision, low-friction motion through sealed ball bearings Proven hydraulic damping using an adjustable oil-filled shock absorber Readily available off-the-shelf hardware Easy maintenance and replacement of wear components Modular construction for future upgrades and customization Compared with a fully printed mechanism, this approach significantly improves durability, dimensional accuracy, wear resistance, and long-term reliability at the moving joints. At the same time, it preserves the affordability, accessibility, and rapid iteration made possible by desktop 3D printing, resulting in a practical, serviceable, and high-performance stabilization platform.
