Quarter-Turn Compression Latch A compact and robust 3D-printable quarter-turn latch for enclosures, cabinet doors, and DIY projects. The mechanism consists of only four printed parts and operates with a simple 90° rotation between the open and closed positions. The handle naturally rests in the downward position , allowing gravity to keep the latch closed. This makes it well suited for applications exposed to vibration, such as camper cabinets, workshop furniture, or portable equipment. The tapered latch arm provides a slight compression effect when closing, allowing doors or panels to be pulled tightly against the frame if required. Installation & Assembly The latch is designed for a simple installation using only three drilled holes and common hardware. Preparing the Door Drill the main center hole to 20 mm using a step drill. Drill two 3.5 mm clearance holes vertically aligned with the center hole, as shown in the model preview (use 2 parts as a guide for the holes). The mounting holes should be clearance holes only. The screws should not engage the door material. Instead, they thread into the printed retaining part, clamping the complete assembly securely to the door. Installing the Latch Insert the outer body through the 20 mm hole from the outside. Press-fit the inner carrier onto the outer body from the inside. Secure both parts using the two short mounting screws . Place the latch arm onto the shaft. Snap the handle through the carrier and latch until fully seated. Install the long center screw , which secures the handle while allowing smooth 90° rotation. No adhesive is required. Although the parts can be glued together, using screws is strongly recommended. The mechanical connection provides a much stronger assembly and significantly improves rigidity across the layer lines of the printed parts. If required, the center section of the model can be stretched or elongated in your slicer to accommodate thicker doors without affecting the locking mechanism. Recommended Hardware The original design was developed using common flat-head SPAX wood screws , although equivalent metric machine screws work equally well. Short Clamping Screws Original design: Quantity: 2 Length: 8 mm Flat countersunk head Approximately 7.5 mm head diameter Equivalent machine screw: M3 × 8 mm DIN 7991 / ISO 10642 Countersunk Socket Head Screw These screws clamp the outer body and inner carrier together through the door. Center Retaining Screw Original design: Quantity: 1 Length: 20 mm Countersunk head Equivalent machine screw: M3 × 20 mm DIN 7991 / ISO 10642 Countersunk Socket Head Screw The center screw retains the handle and latch assembly while allowing free rotation. If the latch is modified for thicker or thinner panels, simply adjust the screw lengths accordingly. Key Features Four printed parts Simple 90° quarter-turn operation Gravity-assisted closed position Tapered latch for optional compression Press-fit assembly Three-screw construction No springs required No glue required Easily adaptable for different door thicknesses Designed for reliable operation under vibration Technical Specifications Specification Value Rotation 90° Printed Parts 4 Main Bore 20 mm Mounting Holes 2 × 3.5 mm clearance Designed Panel Thickness 2.5 mm acrylic (default) Door Thickness Adjustable by extending the center section in the slicer Original Mounting Screws 2 × M3 × 8 mm countersunk (or trimmed SPAX) Original Retaining Screw 1 × M3 × 20 mm countersunk (or SPAX) Applications Acrylic enclosures 3D printer enclosures Camper cabinets Workshop cabinets Storage compartments Electronics enclosures Access panels DIY furniture Utility doors Why This Exists This latch was originally designed as part of my custom Ender 3 enclosure project. The goal was to create a simple, reliable, and inexpensive latch that could be printed without supports, assembled with common hardware, and withstand everyday use. After extensive testing, the design proved to be strong, easy to assemble, and highly reliable. Its gravity-assisted closing action helps prevent accidental opening due to vibration, while the tapered latch provides slight compression without requiring springs or additional hardware. Since then, the design has been reused for workshop cabinets, acrylic enclosures, camper furniture, and other DIY projects where a compact and dependable quarter-turn latch is needed. The design is intentionally simple, easy to modify for different material thicknesses, and inexpensive to build. If there is enough interest, I may also release the complete Ender 3 enclosure project that inspired this latch. Assembly in pictures: Drill main hole Insert outer body and use as guide for the clearance holes Resulting hole layout press-fit and align outer body and inner carrier screw together with 2 shorter screws Add latch into inner carrier Press-fit handle onto latch Screw latch and handle together with longer screw

A take-off platform that lifts your quad above wet grass, packs flat, and needs no hardware. Four identical tiles clip into a Ø240 mm deck on four ground stakes. The hex lattice is 57% open under the prop disc, so the wash blows straight through instead of bouncing back off the deck and pushing the quad around on lift-off. Built for a 3" (LionBee-size). Scales to 5" by changing one number in the source. Why Grass fields eat props and lenses. Flat pads sit in the wet; angled cradles are for launch control off a table. This one stands on stakes, so the quad starts ~88 mm up, clear of the vegetation, and the deck drains and dries. Specs - Deck: Ø240 mm, 3 mm plate, hex cells 17 mm across flats - Open area: 57% under the prop disc, 50% overall - Height: ~88 mm on one leg segment, ~168 mm on two stacked - Perimeter lip 6 mm keeps the quad from sliding off - Raised centre target to aim at when you set down - ~250 g PETG for the complete pad Assembly No screws, no glue, no tools. Rotate each tile 90° and drop it in: the half-lap tongue slides under the neighbour's pocket and a Ø4 mm peg drops into its hole. Legs push up through the posts from below. Friction fit should be snug, the deck shouldn't fall off if you lift the pad by one leg, but it should pull apart by hand. Too tight: two strokes with a file on the tenon. Too loose: one wrap of electrical tape. Printing - PETG or ASA. PLA softens in a hot car and goes brittle in UV. - 0.20 mm layers, 3 walls, 15% gyroid - No supports — every overhang is 45° or better - Two tiles per plate; legs and spikes fill the gaps - Brim on the legs and spikes - Print one tile and one leg first and check the tenon fit before committing

description: I know the configurator can be a bit tricky; if the guide isn’t clear enough, please do feel free to message me. I’m currently putting together some more comprehensive example profiles featuring all the patterns and various options TESSERA — Modular Parametric Wall Tiles (28 pattern engines) Turn your wall into a generative artwork. TESSERA is a fully parametric system of decorative 3D-printed wall tiles: pick a pattern engine, pick a seed, and build a wall where every tile is unique — yet every joint matches perfectly. No two TESSERA walls in the world need to look the same. Yours won't. 🆕 What's new in v3.0 (since v2.0) Six new pattern engines — now 28 in total. Hicks hexagon 🔶 — the iconic hotel-carpet hexagon lattice: open interlocking rings with solid center dots, shipped as a tri-color tile (base + bands + red cores as separate meshes). Contributed by a community member and ported verbatim. Scallop interlace — tangent half-circle ribbons woven into a fish-scale net; flat or domed 3D relief. Hex height field & Overlapping hexagons — honeycombs where every cell rises to a different height, forming a random landscape (with clumping into plateaus, multiple passes, and a full coverage bed). Vertex cubes — cubes standing on their point, the directional-scale look. Vertex cubes — sinuosal decoration with similar S pattern. ✂️ Trim to fit — real walls are never a whole number of tiles. Now you can cut any tile down to fill the leftover strip: you give the size to keep and the edge to cut, and — crucially — the tile keeps its world window, so the pattern stays aligned to the wall even on non-repeating designs. Connector sockets keep their positions (dropped only if the cut slices them); keyholes, shelf and hook recentre on the trimmed tile automatically. More robust everywhere. Switching to a sculpted or 3D-relief engine with an edge chamfer left over no longer errors — those engines simply ignore chamfer and modulation now. Trimmed tiles never fail either: a filler strip too small for a socket or keyhole just comes out without them. 🆕 What's new in v2.0 Relief modulation — the headline feature. Every 2D pattern can now be sculpted in height while keeping its exact design: the top of the relief follows a 3D field of your choice — waves (egg-crate), radial splash (one giant drop centered anywhere on the wall), organic (seed-driven noise), ridges , stepped terraces (contour bands crossing the design) or random plateaus (a block grid where every cell gets its own height — align the grid to the pattern cell and each element rises to its own level). A height floor keeps the design always readable, and a minimum-width guard drops unprintably thin slivers to the level below automatically. Three new sculpted engines (22 total): Crosswave (interfering sine waves — domes and saddles), Droplet (a water drop frozen mid-splash, rings fading with distance) and Topo (organic noise quantized into flat terraces — a contour-line terrain model, gorgeous with one filament color per level). Functional tiles, upgraded : the hook tile now takes 1 to 3 evenly spaced prongs (hook_count), and shelf/hook add-ons ship as a separate third object in their own color — assign three filaments, or print just the add-on in PETG for extra strength. Customizer polish : parameter groups reorganized in the order you actually use them (Pattern and Dimensions right after Part, backlight options at the bottom); curve resolution is now an exposed parameter (curve_res — the Quality section is no longer empty!); and sculpt_res moved next to it as the smoothness control for all sculpted engines, now up to 160. ✨ Why it's different Most tile models repeat one identical piece. TESSERA doesn't: the pattern lives on an infinite virtual canvas , and each tile is just a window on it. Give every tile its position (tile_x, tile_y), keep the same seed, and the design flows across the joints — curves, mazes and dunes continue from one tile to the next as if the wall were printed in one piece. Bonus: if a tile ever breaks, reprint it. Same seed, same position, identical tile. Write your seed on the back of the wall! 🧩 28 pattern engines, 5 families Global random field — every tile unique, always matching: Truchet arcs, Diagonal maze, True labyrinth, Voronoi web, Bubbles Global deterministic field — one continuous lattice across the wall: Hexagon honeycomb, Tri-weave, Isometric cubes, Diamond plate, Flowing waves, Fish scales/Seigaiha, Celtic plait, S-wave flames, Hicks hexagon, Scallop interlace Per-tile motif — identical tiles, infinite repetition: Concentric ripples, Sunflower, Star lattice, Girih strapwork, Basket weave Sculpted heightmap — continuous 3D surfaces, plaster-panel style: Silk, Dunes, Crosswave, Droplet, Topo 3D relief engines — true raised geometry: Vertex cubes, Hex height field, Overlapping hexagons Two engines deserve a special mention. The True labyrinth is a genuine perfect maze (binary-tree algorithm): every corridor connects, no dead zones, and it continues across tiles — yes, you can solve your wall with a finger. 🌀 And the Sunflower is pure mathematics made visible: seeds placed at the golden angle (360°/φ²), exactly like a real sunflower — and its arms style draws the spiral arms themselves. The arm count is a Fibonacci number by theorem (8/13/21/34 — nothing else produces clean spirals). Switch 21 → 34 and watch the next term of the sequence appear on your wall. 🌻 🔧 The system Two tile formats : square 1×1 and wide 2:1 , freely mixed — sockets share the same pitch, so brick-style running bond layouts just work ✂️ Trim to fit : cut edge tiles to any size for imperfect walls, pattern stays aligned Relief modulation 🌊: sculpt the height of any 2D pattern with waves, splashes, noise, terraces or random plateaus — same design, new depth Backlight mode 💡: switch to cutout and the tile becomes a pierced light panel with a smart support web (no floating pieces, with any engine). The included LED spacer frame mounts on the wall, hosts the strip, and the tile snaps into its front rebate Hidden bowtie connectors join tiles from the back — clean joints, nothing visible from the front Blind keyhole pockets (0/1/2 per tile) hang the wall on ordinary screws, invisible from the front Multi-color by design : base plate and relief are separate meshes, and functional add-ons are a third — use your AMS, or simply add a filament change at the base layer on any single-nozzle printer (on sculpted tiles this paints gorgeous topographic contour lines) Functional tiles : a shelf tile with ribbed ledge and a hook tile with a 45° lip — same footprint, same connectors, they click into any TESSERA wall Calibration part included: dial in the connector fit for your printer before committing to full tiles NxN preview (2×2 to 5×5): see your exact wall before printing a single gram 🖨️ Printing Everything prints flat, no supports require . Tiles: base on the plate, 2 walls, 10–15% infill. Connectors: 4+ walls or 100% infill. PLA is perfect; PETG for humid rooms. Layer 0.16–0.20 mm (adaptive/0.12 mm recommended for the sculpted engines). 📖 A full illustrated PDF guide is attached — quick start, seamless-tiling explanation, per-engine reference, parameter tables, mounting steps and FAQ. ⚠️ For shelf/hook tiles: set keyholes = 2, put at least one screw in a stud or proper anchor, and load-test gradually. Connectors align tiles — they don't carry shelves. 🚀 Quick start Print the calibration part, tune conn_clearance Play with preview until you love a pattern + seed Export one tile per wall position (same seed, different tile_x/tile_y) Print, connect, hang. Done. Show me your walls in the comments — pattern + seed, so others can remix your design! ❤️ Designed by Xeyos Design. Fully parametric — hit Customize and make it yours. NOTE. The uploaded profile contains just a few examples to illustrate some good print settings, but TESSERA offers a huge number of combinations – find the one you like best.

description: Ultimate Onion Slicer Update 23/07/2026 : une V2 est désormais disponible ! Elle apporte plusieurs améliorations de conception : structure plus robuste, meilleure durabilité, temps d’impression réduit et emboîtement optimisé entre les deux parties du modèle, nettoyage des supports en quelques secondes. Deux tailles sont proposées : 100 % pour les petits à moyens oignons et 120 % pour les moyens à grands oignons, disponible pour la A1 mini également. Je vous recommande vivement la V2 . Ce modèle est un outil d’aide à la découpe conçu pour maintenir fermement les oignons (peut être utilisé pour les pommes ou d'autres aliment de le même taille/forme), pendant la préparation, tout en garantissant une coupe plus sûre, stable et régulière. Les dents du modèle sont dotées de picots permettant le maintient des oignons en place sans glissement. Les espacements réguliers entre les les dents servent de guide de coupe, permettant de réaliser des tranches ou lamelles homogènes et de taille identique, pour une découpe plus précise et constante. Une poignée ergonomique intégrée améliore la prise en main et le contrôle de l’ensemble pendant l’utilisation. L’outil permet également de sécuriser la découpe, en particulier pour les enfants ou les utilisateurs peu à l’aise avec les couteaux, en réduisant le contact direct avec l’aliment et en limitant les risques de glissade ou de blessure. PS : Je l'ai imprimé en PLA mais je vous recommande d'utiliser du PLA-FS (Food Safe). Je l'ai testé sur des oignon de taille normal. Démonstration : Couper un oignon en deux. Poser une moitié sur la partie inférieure 'Poignet" du slicer dans le sens de la découpe. Placez la partie supérieure (« dents ») au-dessus, en respectant le sens d’assemblage, puis exercez une légère pression jusqu’à entendre un « clic », afin que les deux parties s’emboîtent et maintiennent fermement l’oignon. Utiliser un couteau de cuisine de taille normal ( entre 1 et 2mm d'épaisseur max) pour trancher l'oignon. Retirez la partie supérieure à dents en tirant sur l'un des deux côtés, puis récupérez vos lamelles d'oignon. Et voilà !

Parametric Stackable Soda-Can Dispenser Keep your fridge or pantry organized with this fully customizable, stackable can dispenser. Cans load from the back and roll forward on a gently tilted floor, so a fresh one is always waiting at the front lip. Features 🥤 Auto-feeding tilted tray — load at the back, grab from the front 🧱 Stackable — build a wall of dispensers as tall as you like 🍯 Honeycomb side walls for a light, rigid, great-looking print 🔩 Snap-together assembly — no glue, no screws 🦵 Snap-on legs that hold the base unit at the perfect dispensing angle 🖨️ Auto bed-splitting — large models are tiled into printable pieces that clip back together with Multiboard-style dual-clip keys Fully parametric — tune it to your cans and printer right in the customizer: can height & diameter, tray depth, tilt angle, wall thickness, honeycomb size, number of stacked units, legs, and more. Assembly: Print the wall, floor, and leg parts, then join the tiles with Multiboard dual-clip bowtie keys (printed separately). Snap the legs onto the bottom unit and stack additional units on top. The attached profile is for six EU 0.33l cans. I've printed it with PETG and its sturdy enough to handle four fully loaded levels of cans. 🛠️ How to Use This is a fully parametric model — open it in the MakerWorld customizer (or OpenSCAD) and dial it in to your cans and printer. ⚠️ Important: The model opens in stacked mode so you can preview a full stack. Quick start Set your can size — can_diameter and can_height . Set space_depth (how deep the tray is — it rounds down to a whole number of cans). Adjust angle if cans don't roll freely (higher = steeper). Switch mode to print , set part_select , and export STLs. description: 萌系黑龙/夜煞桌面摆件与屏幕挂件（3D 打印款）完整说明 一、项目主要特点 双形态互动设计： 巧妙的重心与姿态设计，使其既能像趴在屏幕边缘的“监工”一样稳稳挂在显示器上，也能作为独立的立体公仔稳固地站立在平坦的桌面上，兼顾实用与趣味。 超精细仿生鳞片： 尽管是 Q 版造型，但模型体表布满了极其精细的微缩龙鳞与皮革般的肌理纹路，极大地提升了手办的精致度与高级感。 分件灵动大眼： 标志性的超大眼睛极其适合分件打印（或多色 AMS 打印）。黑白分明的灵动大眼不仅是整个模型的灵魂，也大大降低了手残党的涂装门槛。 萌系治愈比例： 采用大头小身子、短手短脚的经典 Q 版拟人化比例，配合充满好奇的无辜神态，能瞬间融化打工人的心。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 适用场景 电脑桌面 Setup： 绝佳的显示器屏幕挂件或机箱内部装饰，为冰冷的数码办公空间增添一丝奇幻与温馨。 车载治愈萌物： 配合无痕胶固定在车载中控台或屏幕上方，陪伴你的每一次出行。 潮玩盲盒展示： 独立站立姿态极其适合摆放在展示柜中，与其他动漫手办或盲盒完美契合。 适配人群 奇幻动画/萌宠爱好者： 对《驯龙高手》等奇幻 IP 中忠诚、可爱的龙形生物毫无抵抗力的玩家。 办公桌“软装”达人： 喜欢用各种治愈系小物件打造个性化工位、缓解工作压力的上班族。 3D 打印手办玩家： 追求高精度皮肤质感表现，喜欢给模型进行眼部点睛涂装的手工爱好者。 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 为了完美还原极其细密的皮肤鳞片，确保这只小黑龙拥有高级的手办质感，建议参考以下切片参数： 层高（Layer Height）： 强烈建议使用 0.12mm - 0.16mm。头顶与背部等平缓的圆弧区域建议开启“动态层高（Adaptive Layers）”，以彻底消除顶部的等高线台阶。 墙数量 / 外轮廓（Walls / Perimeters）： 3 层。多层外墙能让表面的微小鳞片起伏更加立体扎实。 填充率（Infill）： 10% - 15%。推荐使用 聚 Gyroid（陀螺仪） 填充。若打算将其主要作为屏幕挂件，较低的填充率能减轻整体重量，使其挂在屏幕上时重心更稳。 打印速度： 外部可见区域（Outer Wall）建议降速控制在 40-60 mm/s，慢速不仅能大幅提升哑光耗材的表面光泽一致性，还能确保每一片微小的鳞片细节不糊、不拉丝。 四、补充打印 & 组装建议 尺寸缩放参考： 屏幕挂件款（80–100mm）： 专门为显示器定制的最佳尺寸，不挡视线，小巧灵动。 (注：缩放前请先使用卡尺测量您显示器边框的厚度，确保缩放后龙爪与身体的间隙能够刚好卡住您的屏幕边缘) 。 桌面标准款（120–150mm）： 适合作为独立的手办摆件放在鼠标垫旁或书架上，体表的鳞片细节表现力最强。 超大镇宅款（180mm以上）： 适合拥有大尺寸打印机的玩家，极致放大后的鳞片犹如真实的爬行动物皮肤般震撼。 耗材与色彩推荐： 强烈建议使用哑光黑（Matte Black） 或带有极细微闪粉的 星空黑（Galaxy Black）耗材打印主体，能完美过滤掉廉价的塑料反光，复刻出深邃的高级皮革质感。 眼睛涂装/点睛小贴士： 如果是单色打印，眼睛部分可以用丙烯马克笔（白色打底，黑色画瞳孔）轻松涂装。强烈建议在纯黑的瞳孔边缘点上一抹白色的“高光”，这能让整只小龙瞬间注入灵魂，眼神变得极其清澈灵动。 屏幕安全固定技巧： 虽然模型设计有卡住屏幕的物理结构，但为了防止不小心触碰导致其掉落摔坏，建议在挂上屏幕时，在龙的腹部或前爪内侧贴一小粒蓝丁胶（Blu-Tack）或透明无痕纳米胶，既稳固又绝对不会损伤显示器屏幕。

Esta es mi interpretación de cómo pudo haber sido realmente el Caballo de Troya. Al modelarlo, intenté considerar aspectos que suelen pasarse por alto: la resistencia estructural necesaria para soportar su propio peso y el de los guerreros que ocultaba, así como una postura sólida y convincente. También imaginé que, al presentarse como una ofrenda o tributo, su apariencia debía transmitir solemnidad y respeto, más que la de una simple estructura de madera. Otro aspecto importante fue pensar en los recursos disponibles de la época. Asumí que fue construido principalmente por guerreros, con conocimientos prácticos, y no por artesanos especializados. Por eso busqué un diseño robusto, funcional y factible de construir con las herramientas y materiales que probablemente tenían a su alcance. Esta no pretende ser una reconstrucción histórica definitiva, sino una interpretación basada en criterios estructurales, funcionales e históricos.

description: This compact gravity-dispensing water dish is sized for jumping spiders and other small terrarium inhabitants. I was inspired by this model , but designed this version from scratch with a more natural rocky look and a fully printable water tank instead of requiring a separate vial. The removable 10 ml tank automatically replenishes the dish, while the anti-drowning gyroid infill provides secure footing and minimizes exposed open water. The tank includes a built-in air channel that allows water to dispense properly. A small triangle on top points toward the outlet cutout, making it easy to orient the tank during installation. Features Removable 10 ml water tank (fully printable) Gravity-fed water replenishment Anti-drowning gyroid infill Natural rocky aesthetic Compact size for small terrariums Cutouts sized for 8 x 2 mm magnets Dedicated tank profiles for transparent PETG and regular PLA Filling and Installing the Tank The water dish must be completely removed from the terrarium for refilling. Fill the tank with water. Hold the water dish upside down. Orient the tank with its outlet cutout pointing toward the back. The triangle on top indicates the direction of the cutout. Insert the tank, then flip the complete water dish into its normal upright position. Some water should begin flowing into the dish. Add a little more water directly to the dish until it reaches the top of the gyroid infill. This helps establish the flow from the tank. Rotate the tank so the outlet cutout points toward the front. Use a paper towel to briefly dab away any water standing above the gyroid. Use short dabs so the paper towel doesn't begin drawing water from the tank. Return the complete water dish to the terrarium. Printing Please use one of the included print profiles without rebuilding the setup manually in the slicer. The gyroid section, tank opening, and magnet cutouts are created using mesh modifiers and negative parts, so the original object settings need to remain intact. The gyroid infill percentage is carefully tuned for proper water flow from the tank. Do not change the gyroid infill percentage , as doing so may cause the dish to dispense too much or too little water. The water tank includes separate profiles for: Transparent PETG: Prints very slowly with the cooling fan disabled to improve transparency and watertightness. Regular PLA: Uses vase mode to produce a watertight tank and doesn't require the slower transparent PETG settings. For either tank profile, retain the included adaptive layer height and vase mode settings . Changing these settings may prevent the tank from printing correctly or holding water reliably. Magnet Sizing The included magnet cutouts are sized for 8 x 2 mm magnets . Because the holes are negative parts in the slicer, they can be resized before printing if you're using different magnets. You must fix the magnets in place using superglue.

description: Tired of not finding a practical system to make your own roller blinds? This is a complete, robust, and 100% DIY system designed for MakerWorld! This project allows you to create a custom roller blind at a very low cost. It uses a standard 22.5mm cylindrical wooden rod (readily available in any DIY or hardware store) and a smooth cord-pull mechanism. Key Highlights: Cost-Effective & Custom: Make it exactly to the dimensions of your windows without paying a premium. Versatile Mounting: Supports can be screwed directly into either the ceiling or the wall. Easy Maintenance: The clever slider design allows you to easily unhook and remove the brackets to wash the fabric. Smooth Operation: Features a 4-roller system acting as mechanical bearings for a frictionless roll. Bill of Materials (Printed Parts) 2x End Caps (to glue onto the ends of the wooden rod) 4x Rollers (mechanical wheels for smooth rotation) 1x Left Bracket 1x Right Bracket 2x Base Mounts (The sliding brackets to screw into the wall/ceiling) Hardware Required (Non-Printed) 1x Cylindrical wooden rod (22.5mm diameter). 1x Fabric curtain (cut and hemmed to your window size). 2x Screws and wall anchors (adapted to your wall or ceiling material). 1x Cord (approximately twice the total length of your curtain). Tools: Wood glue (to secure the end caps) and, to attach the fabric to the wood I personnally used staples but feel free to propose any alternative ! Step-by-Step Assembly Guide Prepare the fabric: Cut your fabric to your window's width and length, then hem the edges. Glue the 3D-printed end caps to both ends of the wooden rod. Attach the fabric to the wooden rod using staple for example Assemble the brackets (put the 4 rollers into their designated place, they are purposely loose but any proposal to improve that part is highly welcomed !) Mount the little rail to the wall / ceiling using a screw. Do a test to ensure they are properly placed with regard to the wooden rod length with their caps: Measure the exact distance needed, then screw the two Base Mounts into your wall or ceiling. Slide the left and right brackets onto them. Set up the cord: Wind the cord around the wheel (to ensure the cord doesn't slide around the cap I had to make 3 turns around the caps) of the dedicated end cap. Place the wooden rod assembly into the bracket rollers. Test the pull mechanism!

description: # 🌿 Plumeria Frangipani Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. The collapsible geometry has been individually tuned for each bowl diameter (85 mm, 105 mm, and 120 mm). Scaling the models up or down is not recommended , as it may negatively affect the collapsing performance. Assembly Guide Collapse the TPU bowl The collapsible mechanism may feel stiff the first few times it's used. Starting from the bottom, fold one section at a time until it snaps into the collapsed position. After a few cycles, leave in the collapsed position for a few hours so the TPU builds memory. It will be much smoother after this. Install the bowl into the rim With the bowl collapsed, press a small section of the TPU lip into the rim first. Continue working your way around the rim, pressing the TPU into place until it is fully seated. The fit is intentionally snug, so moderate pressure may be required. Parametric Pill Columns Tray Generator (Modular Design) Create high-quality custom trays for organization, gifts, or home decor in the modern "pill columns" style. This project was developed to offer maximum flexibility: simply adjust the dimensions, and the script seamlessly recalculates the vertical column distribution around the perimeter, maintaining a flawless geometry designed for support-free 3D printing. Perfect for both personal use and the production of unique, exclusive pieces. --- DETAILED PARAMETER MANUAL --- 1. Basic Settings - Tray Shape: - Oval: Generates a classic stadium-shaped tray (straight sides with semi-circular ends). Perfect for keys, perfumes, or glasses. - Rectangular: Generates a rectangular tray with customizable rounded corners. Great for organizing boxes, drawers, or office items. - Tray Length and Width: The absolute maximum exterior bounds of the tray (measured in millimeters). The script uses these dimensions as constraints and automatically scales the column count to fit exactly inside these bounds. Note: Width must be less than or equal to Length. - Column Height: The total height of the boundary columns from the base to the top (mm). This determines how deep the tray cavity is. - Base Thickness: The height of the tray's bottom floor (mm). A value of 3mm is recommended to ensure structural rigidity, prevent warping during printing, and allow safe depth for bottom engravings without breaching the interior floor. 2. Pill Columns Style Settings - Column Radius: Half of the column's thickness (mm). A smaller radius (e.g., 3.3mm) yields many small, delicate columns, while a larger radius (e.g., 8mm or 10mm) results in fewer, chunkier pillars. - Lateral Overlap: Controls how deep adjacent columns merge into each other (expressed as a percentage: e.g., 0.15 = 15%). - Lower values (0.0 to 0.10): Columns barely touch, creating deep, sharp V-valleys on the outside (warning: values close to 0 make the print structurally weak). - Ideal values (0.15 to 0.25): Columns merge perfectly to form a strong, watertight, cohesive outer wall with a smooth, pleasing texture. - Higher values (0.30+): Columns interpenetrate deeply, flattening the outer texture. - Top Style: - Round: Finishes the top of each column with a smooth, spherical dome. This gives a very soft, organic look. - Flat: Cuts the columns flat at the top. Recommended if you want a clean, modern, architectural look. - Top Bevel Radius: Only active when Top Style is set to Flat (mm). It rounds off the sharp top edge of the flat pillars. A bevel of 1.0mm is recommended to eliminate sharp corners, make the top feel premium to the touch, and prevent print delamination. - Inner Wall Style: - Wavy: The inner wall mimics the wavy, scalloped shape of the columns. This looks highly organic and consistent but forms internal valleys that can catch dust or soap. - Smooth: A clean, flat inner wall is sliced directly into the columns. This creates a flat interior face, making it extremely easy to wipe clean and ensuring objects placed inside sit flat against the wall without catching. 3. Column Cross-Section Shape - Column Cross Section: - Round: Classic circular pillars. - Oval: Eliptical pillars. This allows you to squeeze or stretch the columns. - Oval Aspect Ratio: Only active when Column Cross Section is set to Oval. It scales the column's width along the perimeter path while keeping its radial thickness constant. - Values > 1.0 (e.g., 1.35): Stretches the columns along the perimeter, making the columns look wider and flatter horizontally. - Value = 1.0: Standard circular columns. - Values < 1.0 (e.g., 0.80): Squishes the columns, making them thinner along the perimeter and deeper radially. 4. Advanced and Customization Settings - Corner Radius: Only active when Tray Shape is set to Rectangular (mm). Controls the rounding radius of the tray's outer corners. Must be larger than the Column Radius. - Enable Top Text and Top Text Height: Adds raised (embossed) 3D text (such as a name or brand name) to the center of the tray's interior floor. You can configure the font size and height (typically 1.0mm is ideal). - Enable Bottom Logo and Engraving Depth: Engraves (debosses) a signature text, brand name, or website handle (e.g., @brand) into the bottom face of the tray base. The engraving uses standard text fonts. The depth is automatically limited to prevent piercing the base. Since it is engraved inwards, it does not affect the tray's stability on flat tables. - Display Mode: - Full: Renders the complete model ready for STL export. - Base Only / Border Only: Isolates parts to inspect details. - Cross Section: Cuts the model in half longitudinal to inspect wall thickness, internal clearances, and engraving depths before printing. RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal for the vertical curves of the spheres) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Recommended for filling small fusions) - Infill: 10% Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Supports: No supports needed! - Fuzzy Skin (Optional for premium finish): Contour, Thickness: 0.3mm, Point distance: 0.8mm 💡 Pro Tip: Enable Variable/Adaptive Layer Height in your slicer.

description: All Linked 2‑Line Customizable Name Plate Generator This is a fully parametric two‑line name plate generator built from the script you provided and matched to the uploaded model. It produces clean, linked lettering with unified background layers, an optional underline capsule, and optional vertical support sticks for cake‑topper or display use. The generator is optimized for easy customization , multi‑color layering , and reliable printability. This model prints without supports, all geometry is designed to be support‑free. Ironing is recommended on the top text layer to achieve a smooth, premium finish. 🔧What this model does Generates two independent text lines with linked/connected letterforms and automatic background expansions. Produces background layers (thick offset shapes) behind each line so the text reads strongly at a distance. Optionally adds an underline capsule sized automatically from the combined text bounds. Optionally adds vertical support sticks (legs) with rounded bottoms for insertion or display. Exports as layered geometry so each color layer can be separated for AMS or manual filament swaps. 🛠️What you can customize Line 1 and Line 2 text (any word, name, or phrase). Fonts for each line (script, display, serif, etc.). Letter heights and XY scaling for precise visual balance. Inter‑letter spacing and line spacing to tune how the two lines link. Background depth and background padding (background_font_thickness / offset). Underline : enable/disable, thickness, gap, extra length, X offset, and background depth. Support sticks : enable/disable, stick length, thickness, spacing, and background padding. Colors for each element: line 1, line 2, underline, and unified background color. 🧱 Parametric structure and behavior Text is rendered as 2D outlines, offset for borders, then linear_extrude is used to create stacked layers. The generator auto‑calculates combined bounds for both lines to size the underline and align background shapes. Support sticks are generated with a flat top and rounded bottom using hull logic for smooth, printable legs. All translations and scales are computed from textmetrics so the model remains centered and stable at any size. 🖨️Printing tips Support‑free : geometry is designed to print cleanly without supports. Manual swap: pause at the background depth or base height to change filament cleanly. Stick safety: if using as a cake topper, round the stick bottoms and test insertion depth before serving. 🎨 Color Swap (Manual Multicolor) If you don’t have an AMS, this model prints perfectly with manual filament swaps. description: # 🌿 Alocasia Scalprum Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. model_name: Letrero de Nombre Cursivo con Corazón
description: ¡Hola! 👋 Este letrero personalizado te permite escribir cualquier nombre (¡o hasta dos nombres juntos! 💑) en una preciosa tipografía cursiva, con la opción de añadir un corazón y unas colas decorativas que le dan un toque súper especial y romántico. Perfecto para regalar, decorar una estantería o sorprender a alguien especial 🎁✨ 🔤 ¿Cómo escribo el nombre? Solo tienes que escribir el texto en el parámetro texto . Puedes usar mayúsculas y minúsculas sin problema para las letras normales 😊 ⚠️ Importante: las colas decorativas (inicio, final y el corazón) solo funcionan con letras en minúscula . Si escribes una letra en mayúscula donde debería ir una cola, esa letra se quedará "normal", sin la colita. Así que, si quieres el efecto completo, ¡escribe el nombre todo en minúscula! (ej: "aurora" en vez de "Aurora") 💕 ¿Cómo pongo el corazón entre dos nombres? ¡Súper fácil! Solo escribe los dos nombres separados por un espacio , por ejemplo: "oscar giu". El sistema detecta automáticamente el espacio y coloca ahí el corazón, uniendo las dos palabras de forma preciosa 🥰 No hace falta escribir ningún símbolo especial, ¡el espacio ya hace toda la magia! 🪢 ¿Qué son las colas de inicio y final? Son dos pequeños adornos decorativos (una especie de rúbrica caligráfica) que se añaden antes de la primera letra y después de la última letra de todo el texto, dándole un acabado mucho más elegante y "hecho a mano" ✍️ activar_adorno_inicio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola antes de la primera letra activar_adorno_final ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola después de la última letra activar_corazon_espacio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva el corazón en el espacio entre nombres Recuerda: estas 3 opciones solo se aplican si la letra correspondiente (primera, última, o la de antes del espacio) es minúscula 🔡 ⚙️ Todos los parámetros que puedes personalizar 📏 Tamaño ancho_deseado_letrero — el ancho total del letrero en mm; las letras se ajustan solas para que el texto entero mida justo esto, sea cual sea el nombre 📐 ✏️ Texto texto — el nombre o los nombres que quieres grabar (recuerda: minúsculas para el efecto completo de colas) 🖋️ grosor_texto — el grosor (altura en Z) del relieve de las letras, en mm 🔼 💕 Adornos especiales activar_adorno_inicio — cola decorativa al principio del texto activar_adorno_final — cola decorativa al final del texto activar_corazon_espacio — corazón automático en el espacio entre dos nombres 🧱 Base contorno_base — grosor del borde/marco sólido alrededor de las letras, en mm grosor_base — grosor de la base, en mm (con un valor alto, ej. 50mm, el letrero se sostiene solo de pie sin necesitar agujeros de montaje) 🧍 🕳️ Parches Tapahuecos (por si alguna letra deja huecos sueltos, como en la "o" o la "a") activar_parche_izquierdo / activar_parche_derecho / activar_parche_centro — activa cada parche donde lo necesites parche_izq_x / _y, parche_der_x / _y, parche_cen_x / _y — posición de cada parche (mm) radio_parche_izq / _der / _cen — tamaño (radio) de cada parche, en mm 🎨 Colores color_base — color del cuerpo/base del letrero color_texto — color del relieve de las letras (colores disponibles: Rojo, Amarillo, Rosa, Verde, Azul, Naranja, Morado, Negro, Blanco, Gris) ¡Espero que te encante el resultado! 💖 Si tienes dudas al generar tu nombre personalizado, no dudes en preguntar 😊🖨️ Hi! 👋 This personalized sign lets you write any name (or even two names together! 💑) in a beautiful cursive font, with the option to add a heart and decorative tails for a super special and romantic touch. Perfect for a gift, decorating a shelf, or surprising someone special 🎁✨ 🔤 How do I write the name? Just type the text in the text field. You can use uppercase and lowercase letters without any problem 😊 ⚠️ Important: the decorative tails (start, end, and heart) only work with lowercase letters. If you type a capital letter where a tail should be, that letter will remain "normal," without the tail. So, if you want the full effect, write the name all in lowercase! (e.g., "aurora" instead of "Aurora") 💕 How do I add the heart between two names? Super easy! Just type the two names separated by a space, for example: "oscar giu". The system automatically detects the space and places the heart there, beautifully joining the two words 🥰 No need to type any special symbols, the space does all the magic! 🪢 What are the start and end tails? These are two small decorative flourishes (a kind of calligraphic signature) that are added before the first and last letters of the text, giving it a much more elegant and "handmade" finish ✍️ activate_flourish_beginning ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish before the first letter activate_flourish_end ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish after the last letter activate_heart_space ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the heart in the space between names Remember: these 3 options only apply if the corresponding letter (first, last, or the one before the space) is lowercase 🔡 ⚙️ All the parameters you can customize 📏 Size desired_flag_width — the total width of the flag in mm; The letters automatically adjust so the entire text measures exactly this, whatever the name 📐 ✏️ Text text — the name or names you want engraved (remember: lowercase for the full tail effect) 🖋️ text_thickness — the thickness (Z-height) of the letter relief, in mm 🔼 💕 Special Embellishments activate_embellishment_start — decorative tail at the beginning of the text activate_embellishment_end — decorative tail at the end of the text activate_heart_space — automatic heart in the space between two names 🧱 Base base_outline — thickness of the solid border/frame around the letters, in mm base_thickness — thickness of the base, in mm (with a high value, e.g., 50mm, the sign stands on its own without needing mounting holes) 🧍 🕳️ Patches Filler letters (in case any letters leave gaps, like in the "o" or the "a") activate_left_patch / activate_right_patch / activate_center_patch — activate each patch where you need it left_patch_x / _y, right_patch_x / _y, center_patch_x / _y — position of each patch (mm) left_patch_radius / right_patch_radius / _center_patch — size (radius) of each patch, in mm 🎨 Colors base_color — color of the body/base of the sign text_color — color of the letter relief (Available colors: Red, Yellow, Pink, Green, Blue, Orange, Purple, Black, White, Gray) I hope you love the result! 💖 If you have any questions while creating your personalized name, don't hesitate to ask 😊🖨️

description: Silence Trio | See No Hear No Speak No Evil Tre gesti semplici. Tre silenzi diversi. Una sola frase. Nascono nel Giappone del 1600, scolpite sul santuario di Nikkō, e da quattro secoli continuano a dire la stessa cosa senza aprire bocca. Mizaru, quella che si copre gli occhi Non è cecità. È la scelta di non nutrire lo sguardo con ciò che avvelena. Chi guarda troppo il male finisce per somigliargli. Kikazaru, quella che si copre le orecchie Non è sordità. È il rifiuto del rumore che divide: la voce che insinua, la mezza frase riportata, il pettegolezzo che sembra innocuo. Iwazaru, quella che si copre la bocca Non è mutismo. È la parola trattenuta un istante in più, il tempo esatto che serve a capire se aiuta o se fa solo danno. Insieme Da sole sono tre statuette. Insieme sono una frase. description: Modular kit for securely adapting your portable AC to an open tilt-window and adding an intake hose for better cooling efficiency. Holds the window firmly in place while sealing off the opening and providing excellent airflow for both the intake & exhaust vents. For complete sealing, I recommend cutting foam pieces to fill the open space above and below the opened window. The kit includes a 255x230mm to 150mm intake hose adapter for portable AC units, a modular plate with two 150mm vents and adjustable brackets to fit the majority of tilt-windows as shown in the cover image. Printing : Print this in PETG or ABS . The exhaust vent will get too hot for PLA. The file is structured as follows: The kit is made up of multiple 250mm segments and a smaller 105mm segment. In my case, the window was 85.5cm in height, so I needed both adapter segments ( plates 3 and 4 ), as well as the top segment with mounts ( plate 5 ) and the short 105mm fill plate ( plate 7 ), which adds up to 855mm. Perfect fit, almost like I designed it specifically for that window or something :) In your case, measure the height of your window. Then print the plates according to your needs. You can add a blank 250mm segment by printing plate 6, or a blank 105mm segment by printing plate 7. It is likely that you'll need to modify at least one piece to achieve a perfect fit, if you wish to have zero gap. Whether you do that with a hacksaw or by simply shortening the piece in the slicer is up to you. Assembly: Assembly is fairly simple, refer to this image. The only supplies required are some M8x20 Screws, nuts and washers to secure the mounting brackets . The locking pieces to secure the segments together are meant to fit tightly, don't hesitate to tap them into place lightly with a hammer. You can assemble the segments in different orders than shown here, just be sure to have a set of mounting brackets somewhere near the top and another somewhere near the bottom. Test fit everything and then tighten the screws. The brackets can be both slid back and forth within their mounting slots, as well as tilted to fit as tightly as possible. Make sure to place the exhaust vent ABOVE the intake vent! The intake will otherwise ingest hot air directly from the exhaust! While this design should fit most european-style tilt windows as shown in the cover image, there is no way I can guarantee it will fit yours exactly. The modular design and seperate brackets should however make it easy to adapt with minimal effort. Happy printing and enjoy!

description: 🩻Overview🩻 This high-precision 3D model is a faithful replica of the human knee joint, created through a rigorous anatomical and digital workflow. The skeletal structures were directly extracted and reconstructed from real CT scans to guarantee true-to-life bone morphology. The soft tissues—including ligaments, menisci, and articular cartilage—were then meticulously 3D modeled by hand, based on in-depth studies of MRI scans and anatomical literature. It serves as a premium medical-grade educational tool, perfect for students, orthopedic professionals, physical therapists, or 3D printing enthusiasts. Included Anatomical Structures The model features all critical bony and soft tissue structures necessary to understand the complex biomechanics of the knee: 🦴Skeletal Structure (CT Extracted): Femur, Tibia, Fibula, and Patella (kneecap), featuring accurate reproductions of condyles, epicondyles, and articular surfaces. 🔗Ligamentous Apparatus (MRI Modeled): Cruciate Ligaments (Anterior Cruciate Ligament - ACL & Posterior Cruciate Ligament - PCL). Collateral Ligaments (Medial Collateral Ligament - MCL & Lateral Collateral Ligament - LCL). Patellar System (including the patellar tendon/ligaments). 🦵Cartilage & Cushioning (MRI Modeled): Menisci (Medial and Lateral menisci). Articular Cartilage covering both the femoral and tibial contact surfaces. Intended Use Education & Didactics: An excellent tactile and visual aid for anatomy classrooms, medical schools, and healthcare training. Patient Communication: Ideal for orthopedic clinics and physiotherapy practices to visually explain injuries (e.g., ACL tears, meniscus damage, osteoarthritis) and surgical procedures to patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A great project to showcase your printer's capability with complex, high-detail organic geometries. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for PLA . No flexible filaments are required, making it easy and reliable to print on any standard 3D printer. Optimized for Single AMS (4 Colors): The model is structured to use exactly 4 colors, making it perfectly compatible with a single Bambu Lab AMS unit. To maximize visual contrast and educational value, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Femur, Tibia, Fibula, Patella) Red: Ligaments Blue: Menisci Beige: Articular Cartilage Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created other versions that are completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the collection here: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Versions with Themes I currently plan on making more variations of this model with specific themes. An outdoor activity-themed version that could have a surfboard, skateboard, or fishing bobber or lure. A larger version that had a light using the led light kit. Interactive 2D map view - Resize, rotate, or drag your choice of shape on a 2D map view. Selective water body removal - You may or may not want to print some of the fetched water bodies. This tool lets you exclude water body segments from being generated. Extension tiles - A single GPX is a single tile by default. You can extend the tiles by adding new tiles in the Interactive 2D Map View. Jigsaw puzzle - Generate up to a 20×20 jigsaw terrain puzzle with full control over the jigsaw shape parameters and randomness. Pro upgrades go directly toward the server capacity that makes higher limits possible. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Reports indicate potential anomalies, including vertical shafts and structured, geometric patterns reaching deep into the bedrock beneath the major pyramids. While these findings have sparked intense debate among archaeologists regarding their nature and origin, they offer a tantalizing glimpse into what may still be hidden beneath our feet. Inspired by these findings, I have designed a model of the subterranean structures that some researchers believe may be part of this deep network, featuring complex pillars with coiled sections and block-like bases. Este proyecto convierte cualquier persiana en una persiana motorizada inteligente controlable desde botones físicos o desde tu celular con la app Blynk IoT . Un ESP32 recibe las órdenes (subir, bajar, stop, auto) y las manda a un motor DC a través de un driver TB6612FNG que protege el microcontrolador de la corriente del motor. El sistema recuerda cuánto tiempo tarda en abrir o cerrar del todo, respeta un límite máximo de apertura para que la persiana no se enrede, y guarda toda esa configuración en la memoria del ESP32 aunque se apague la luz. description: Overview This soccer kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to always be centered in the exact same position. It is a soccer-themed version of the models you can find in the collection here: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures All of the parts in all of the models in the collection are compatible with each other. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. Except for the ball, no parts require supports or an AMS. Two versions of the ball are available. One that requires an AMS or dual nozzle and one that requires the hexagons to be pressed or glued into place. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates with both types of balls in the profile and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three or fourteen pieces: the base, the print-in-place linkages, and the ball that requires AMS or the ball that does not and the eleven pentagons. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All of these parts are completely compatible with the other models in this collection. https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. If the no-AMS ball is printed, the pentagon pieces need to be placed in place (they will likely require some glue). Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Other Versions with Themes This is a soccer-themed version of the models you can find in the collection here: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures I currently plan on making more variations of this model with other specific themes. These may include but not be limited to: A space theme with the ball being a planet or the moon. A version themed around a different sport such as baseball, tennis, golf, volleyball, or American football. A moving object-themed version that could be a motorcycle, racecar, airplane, or rocket. An outdoor activity-themed version that could have a surfboard, skateboard, or fishing bobber or lure. A larger version that had a light using the led light kit. There are many possible versions that I could create. Let me know which ones you want to see, and let me know of any other ideas that you have. description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. A question for the more curious viewer: Why does the biceps tendon anchor to the scapula instead of attaching directly to the humerus? Let me know in the comments!

Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

description: The project This life-size 3D model is a realistic human hand skeleton. It was created starting from a real CT scan to keep the true shape of the bones. After cleaning up the scan, custom joints were added directly into the design. The result is a highly accurate model that prints in one single piece and moves just like a real hand. ⚙️ Print-in-Place Kinematics & Anatomy Unlike standard static models or complex multi-part assemblies, this hand is designed to be printed as a single, continuous piece: Zero Assembly Required: The complex mechanical joints are built directly into the geometry. Once the print is finished, the fingers and thumb are immediately ready to flex, extend, and move. Bio-realistic Movement: The internal joint constraints were specifically calibrated to respect the natural limits and range of motion found in a real human hand. Medical-Grade Accuracy: Features true-to-life representations of the carpal bones, metacarpals, and phalanges, preserving the organic textures and shapes of the original scan. 🎓 Perfect For: Clinical & Academic Study: A fantastic, hands-on visual aid for medical students, physical therapists, and anatomy teachers. Biomechanical Demonstration: Easily explains how the skeletal framework behaves during grasping, finger articulation, and thumb opposition. 3D Printing Showcase: An incredibly impressive project to demonstrate your printer's dimensional accuracy, bridging capabilities, and print-in-place tolerances. Artistic Reference: A great physical tool for artists and animators studying lifelike hand poses. 💡 Print Guidelines Format: 100% Print-in-Place. Material: Optimized for standard PLA. Rigid materials work perfectly to demonstrate the skeletal kinematics—no TPU or flexible filament is needed. Scale: Pre-scaled to match the proportions of an average adult human hand (1:1 scale). Disclaimer: While highly accurate and derived from real medical data, this model is designed strictly for educational, demonstration, and hobbyist purposes. description: Help students pause, breathe, and reset with this tactile Wave Breathing Pause Card from 3DprintEDU. This 3D printable SEL tool gives children a calming finger tracing path to follow while practising mindful breathing, focus, and emotional regulation. Students begin at the raised O , then slowly trace along the wave paths as they breathe in and out. The included 3MF file contains both versions , so you can choose the style that works best for your students, classroom, or sensory space: Raised Path Version An embossed tactile wave path that students can feel clearly as they trace. The repeated wave pattern gives students a gentle rhythm to follow as they slow their breathing and refocus. Repeat the path a few times, moving calmly from wave to wave. The tactile design gives students a simple, hands on way to pause, regulate, and reset. For younger students, an adult can guide the rhythm by saying: Trace up, breathe in. Trace down, breathe out. Keep going slowly. description: New design in the “Can I lick it” series This model is part of my ongoing collection where I turn everyday curiosity into simple, fun labels. For this version, I created a color‑coded system based on the periodic table. Each element is placed into a category depending on how safe or unsafe it generally is to interact with. To make the categories more reliable, I compared the results of six different AI models . Each model classified all 118 elements independently, and I used the overlapping conclusions to decide which color each element should receive. The goal was not to be overly scientific, but to avoid obvious mistakes and keep the system consistent. The Excel file I used during the comparison is included in the upload. It’s written in Dutch, but the structure is simple enough to follow even without understanding the language. The design itself is clean and straightforward, matching the rest of the series. It’s meant to be fun, recognizable, and easy to print. Disclaimer: This project is meant for humor and curiosity only. Please don’t actually sniff, lick, or test any real elements or materials. description: Modular Articulated DNA Educational Model Let your students build, connect, and explore the DNA with this colourful modular model designed for hands-on learning. Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases, while the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone. This model is great for classrooms, STEM projects, biology demonstrations, or anyone who wants a fun physical way to understand nucleotide pairing and DNA structure. I also plan on extending this model with a couple of more pieces for better demonstration of topics like Transcription and Translation . Feel free to leave a like and follow if you'd like to stay updated. Parts You can print as many of the individual parts as you like and connect them with each other! Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases and the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone: Cytosine Guanine Adenine Thymine Uracil Assembly & Colouring The backbone pieces can be clicked together with a little bit of force. It is recommended to use 5x2 (dxh) magnets for both the backbone pieces and nucleotides, to better hold them in place. Place the magnets into the slot (make sure you have them oriented all in the same way!) and use a paper clip, a scredriver, or something similar to push the magnet all the way into the slot. You can also remove the magnets if needed using a paper clip from the other side. Feel free to adjust the colouring of the pieces to your needs. My file uses the colours according to the Wikipedia nucleic acid image: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid#/media/File:Difference_DNA_RNA-EN.svg Versions There are two Versions of nucleotides: Standard Set (recommended!) nucleotides have no chamfer/fillet on the connection pin. This makes them harder to separate from their counterparts, but results in a more stable double strand. Rounded Nucleotide Set contains nucleotide pieces with a rounded down connection pin. This makes them easier to separate, e.g. when demonstrating something, but obviously also reduces the stability of the entire double strand in terms of base pairs disconnecting when you move the double strand around. If you have any suggestions, feel free to let me know!

My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of a spherical gear system, which is also called as ABENICS named after the inventor's name Abe. Brief Description A spherical gear system consists of one spherical gear and two cylindrical gears. Each cylindrical gear can rotate around its central axis, and that axis itself can swing around a second axis pointing toward the center of the sphere. By driving these two axes independently for each cylindrical gear — four axes in total — the system can control the orientation of the spherical gear across the full range of pitch, roll, and yaw. In a real application, the only limits on the motion range come from mechanical interference between the output coupler on the sphere and the surrounding structure, not from the gear geometry itself. The spherical gear is constructed by engraving a spur gear tooth profile around one axis of a sphere, then repeating the process around a perpendicular axis. The gif animation below illustrates this two-step process: first one rotation, then a second rotation about an axis 90 degrees away, yielding the characteristic cross-hatched spherical surface. The cylindrical gear is designed by rolling a basic spherical gear — engraved around only one axis — against a cylindrical blank. This process leaves one distinctive eye-shaped feature on the cylinder surface. Because of this, the cylindrical gear is also called a monopole gear. When you handle the printed model, you may notice that the spherical gear tends to stall at certain orientations. This happens when the monopole of the cylindrical gear aligns with a pole of the spherical gear. At this position, the spherical gear can not rotate in the direction of the cylindrical gear's central axis. To rotate the sphere in any intended direction, the secondary axis of the cylindrical gear must first be driven to make the main axis perpendicular to that direction. Only when the control software does this intelligently, the spherical gear can achieve motion in any arbitrary direction. To convince yourself that the spherical gear can indeed be moved in any direction from any orientation, try the following when it locks up: put your finger on the sphere and move it in small circles. Since the lock only resists one specific rotation at a time, pushing in various directions will gradually swing the cylindrical gear into an orientation where it can drive the sphere the way you want. Try this at different orientations of the sphere and you will find that free motion in any direction is always recoverable. The spherical gear system is a relatively new concept, first published in 2021, and is intended for robotic joints that achieve the same three rotational degrees of freedom as human joints. Reference Kazuki Abe; Kenjiro Tadakuma; Riichiro Tadakuma (October 2021). "ABENICS: Active Ball Joint Mechanism With Three-DoF Based on Spherical Gear Meshings" . IEEE Transactions on Robotics . 37 (5). Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly (1) The spherical gear is printed in two pieces to have easy and precision printing. Combine them with two dedicated pins. (2) The cylindrical gear is also printed in two pieces. Combine them with two dedicated pins. (3) Push the shaft into the cylindrical gear and secure the other knob with the retaining ring. (The gears are simplified in these pictures to make it easy to handle in the CAD.) (4) Mount the assembled cylindrical gear with shaft onto the bearing. (5) Put the sphere on the plate. (6) Put the cylindrical gear on the bearing. (7) Push the secondary shaft of the cylindrical gear into the bearing on the plate. It should snap fixed in the square hole on the bottom plate of the smaller bearing. Other examples You may also be interested in the models in my educational mechanical mechanism examples. Find them in this collection: https://makerworld.com/collections/15048577-my-educational-mechanism-models Happy printing! I learned a lot about technical detail of designing gear tooth profiles from Haguruma-No-Hanashi website . I’m truly grateful for that.
