Its posture is hunched forward, yet more controlled than the feral crouch of an ordinary Ghast. The Gravecaller stands with its legs spread widely across the base, one foot slightly advanced and the other braced behind, giving it a stable ritual stance. The torso twists subtly toward the outstretched arm, creating a strong diagonal line through the body and making the pose feel active without relying on magical effects. Its head is hairless and corpse-like, with a high, angular skull, pointed ears, deeply sunken eyes, and a mouth stretched open in a guttural command. The jaw is filled with irregular teeth and prominent fangs, while the cheeks are gaunt and drawn tightly against the bone. Several long, string-like tendons or decayed strips of flesh hang from the lower jaw and chin, giving the face a grotesque, ceremonial appearance. These strands should be grouped into thick, connected forms rather than sculpted as individual fragile threads. The left hand grips a tall grave-calling staff planted firmly into the base. The shaft is made from dark, weathered wood or bone-bound timber and is reinforced with wrapped cords, metal bands, and crude ritual bindings. At the top sits a large skull framed by smaller bones and curved supports, creating a dramatic focal point. Every decorative element is physically attached to the staff structure, and the lower end connects directly to the ground for added stability. The staff should appear ancient and macabre, but not overly delicate or overloaded with tiny ornaments. The opposite arm reaches forward with the palm open and the fingers curled, as if the Gravecaller is directing nearby undead toward its prey. The hand is oversized and clawed, with long but thickened nails. Its gesture is commanding rather than mindless, separating this creature from the more animalistic Ghast. The arm remains slightly bent at the elbow to reduce overhang and improve printing strength. The Gravecaller wears a collection of decayed ritual garments and scavenged grave ornaments. A torn mantle hangs from one shoulder and falls behind the upper arm in broad, connected folds. Around the waist is a heavy belt decorated with a central skull, bone plates, and several large talismans. Ragged cloth panels descend between and beside the legs, forming a dark ceremonial skirt. The fabric is heavily damaged, with irregular pointed edges, but all hanging pieces connect to one another or to the legs to avoid unsupported sections. Its exposed skin is stretched tightly over the ribs, shoulders, arms, and legs. Scars, open wounds, hardened growths, and areas of rough necrotic tissue cover the body. The chest remains visibly hollow and starved, while the thighs and shoulders retain enough muscle to suggest the unnatural strength of a Ghast. The fingers and toes end in hooked claws, and both feet are planted securely against the base. The color palette is dominated by desaturated green-grey, pale corpse flesh, and bruised blue. Dark purple and blackened red can be used around wounds, eyes, and the mouth. The garments suit faded violet, charcoal, dirty burgundy, or mouldy black, while the bone ornaments provide pale focal points. The staff works well in dark brown wood, aged ivory, tarnished bronze, and old blood tones. The round tabletop base represents a desecrated burial site. Several skulls, large bone fragments, cracked earth, and grave debris are embedded around the creature’s feet. The staff is planted among these remains, visually connecting the Gravecaller to the dead it commands. The terrain stays low and compact, ensuring that the model’s silhouette remains clear and that no scenery becomes fragile or distracting. A voice beneath the soil. A command the dead obey. The grave answers back. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghast Gravecaller design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from the standard Ghast through ritual gear and commanding posture. Tall, gaunt undead anatomy with long limbs and visible ribs. Wide, stable stance suited to a necromantic battlefield leader. Grotesque head with pointed ears, sunken eyes, fangs, and hanging jaw tendons. Large grave-calling staff planted directly into the base. Staff topped with an integrated skull and securely attached bone decorations. One clawed hand extended in a commanding summoner-like gesture. Heavy ritual belt with skull ornamentation and large bone talismans. Torn shoulder mantle and layered ceremonial cloth panels. All fabric sections attached to the body or neighbouring garments for print safety. Thickened claws, tendons, staff details, and bone elements for dependable printing. Both feet firmly connected to the round base. Desecrated graveyard terrain with skulls, bones, and cracked earth. No floating spirits, magical energy, smoke, aura effects, or separate components. Strong asymmetrical silhouette suitable for encounter leaders and display collections. Designed for resin printing while remaining achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a muted green-grey, pale blue-grey, or dead flesh basecoat. Shade the recesses with dark purple, black-green, or brown washes, concentrating around the ribs, face, joints, and damaged tissue. Rebuild raised areas with pale grey, ivory, or desaturated green highlights. Add bruising with thin purple, burgundy, and blue glazes around the shoulders, knees, wounds, and mouth. Paint the ritual garments in faded violet, dark burgundy, charcoal, or mouldy brown. Apply a black or dark purple wash, followed by dusty grey or muted lavender edge highlights. Bone ornaments and skulls can be based in dark beige, washed with sepia, and highlighted through bone to pale ivory. For the staff, use dark brown or grey-brown wood with lighter streaks along the grain. Metal bands can be painted in tarnished bronze or blackened iron, with small green or orange corrosion accents. The skull topper should receive stronger highlights than the surrounding bones to make it the visual centre of the miniature. Finish the base with dark soil, grey stones, aged bone, and restrained dead grass tones. Selective gloss inside the mouth, around fresh wounds, or on the eyes can contrast effectively with the matte corpse skin and dusty clothing. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Ghoul Lacedon Miniature – Drowned Hunter of the Deep This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Ghoul Lacedon is presented as an aquatic undead predator shaped by long exposure to black water, flooded crypts, and lightless coastal depths. It retains the ravenous anatomy of a Ghoul, but its body has become broader, heavier, and more adapted for movement beneath the surface. Webbed claws, fin-like growths, water-swollen flesh, and a low amphibious stance immediately distinguish it from the land-dwelling Ghoul while preserving the same corpse-born hunger. The creature has a powerful, hunched humanoid frame with broad shoulders, a thick upper back, and long arms that nearly reach the ground. Its torso is gaunt around the ribs and abdomen, but the shoulders, forearms, thighs, and calves remain dense with unnatural muscle. This contrast creates the impression of a drowned corpse that has become a specialised underwater hunter rather than a weakened cadaver. The spine curves sharply forward, lowering the head between the shoulders and giving the miniature a compact, predatory silhouette. Its head is large, bald, and distinctly aquatic. A broad mouth opens into a savage snarl, exposing irregular needle-like teeth and prominent fangs suited to tearing flesh. The jaw is heavy and slightly extended, while the lips are peeled back around the teeth. Deep-set eyes sit beneath a pronounced brow, giving the creature a hostile, animalistic expression. The nose is flattened and partially decayed, with wide openings that suggest an amphibious or drowned physiology. The cheeks and neck are deeply ridged, and the sides of the head may feature short fin-like membranes or hardened gill structures. A series of thick, jagged fins runs from the back of the skull along the neck and upper spine. Additional fin ridges appear on the forearms and calves, giving the creature a strong aquatic identity without resembling a fish-person or sea demon. These structures are broad, layered, and firmly connected to the limbs, avoiding thin translucent membranes or fragile spikes. Smaller ridges may continue along the elbows and shoulders, reinforcing the flowing direction of the body. The Ghoul Lacedon is posed in a wide, low crouch as though it has just dragged itself from the water. One foot is planted on a raised section of rock near the front of the base, while the other braces farther behind. Both feet are large and fully webbed, with thick clawed toes gripping the terrain. The torso leans forward, and both arms are extended to either side in an aggressive balancing posture. One claw reaches toward its prey, while the opposite hand is drawn slightly back, ready to strike. The hands are oversized and amphibious, with webbing between the fingers and long hooked claws. The fingers remain thick and partially grouped to ensure dependable printing. The webbed membranes are sculpted as solid, shallow connections rather than delicate sheets. Similar webbing stretches between the toes, giving the feet a broad footprint and increasing the model’s physical contact with the base. Its corpse-like skin has a slick, waterlogged texture. Deep folds gather around the neck, joints, and abdomen, while cracks and tears expose darker tissue beneath. Barnacle-like growths, scarred patches, and hardened nodules may appear across the shoulders and limbs, but these should be large and simplified enough to remain readable after printing. Ragged remains of cloth hang around the waist, soaked against the hips and thighs. The garment consists of broad connected panels with torn edges, avoiding long unsupported strips. The ideal palette combines dark teal, drowned blue-grey, cold green, and desaturated turquoise. The belly, face, palms, and inner limbs may be lighter and more corpse-pale, while the back and fin ridges can be darker. Purple, black-red, and brown shading around wounds and joints enhances the drowned appearance. Teeth and claws provide strong contrast in stained ivory or yellowed bone. The round tabletop base represents a flooded ruin or rocky shoreline. Uneven stone, shallow sculpted water, broken masonry, shells, and a few low aquatic plants surround the creature’s feet. The water remains a textured part of the base rather than a transparent effect, with ripples sculpted directly around the planted limbs. All environmental elements remain low, solid, and physically connected. Born beneath black water. Hunger that never drowned. The deep sends it ashore. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghoul Lacedon design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from a standard Ghoul through aquatic anatomy and terrain. Broad, hunched silhouette with long arms and powerful swimming limbs. Large predatory head with recessed eyes, flattened nose, and fang-filled jaws. Thick fin-like ridges along the head, neck, spine, forearms, and calves. Webbed hands and feet with durable, integrated membranes. Oversized hooked claws suitable for both climbing and underwater hunting. Low amphibious crouch suggesting emergence from deep water. Both feet firmly planted with broad contact across the round base. Water-swollen corpse skin with scars, folds, wounds, and hardened growths. Ragged soaked garments securely connected to the hips and legs. Strong asymmetrical action pose with both arms spread for balance and attack. Thickened fingers, fins, claws, and joints for reliable miniature printing. Flooded ruin base with stone, ripples, shells, and compact aquatic details. No floating water, bubbles, spray, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported scenery. Designed for high-detail resin printing and achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. Excellent for underwater encounters, flooded crypts, coastal ruins, and undead groups. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a dark blue-grey, desaturated teal, or drowned green basecoat. Apply a deep navy, purple-black, or green-brown wash into the recesses around the ribs, joints, face, fins, and skin folds. Rebuild the raised areas with lighter turquoise-grey, pale green, or cold corpse-flesh tones. Use lighter, more desaturated colors across the chest, face, palms, and inner limbs to create a waterlogged appearance. Glaze the shoulders, elbows, knees, and wounds with muted purple, bruised blue, and blackened red. The fin ridges can be painted in darker teal or blue-black, followed by pale edge highlights to define their shape. Paint the mouth interior in dark burgundy or purple-red, with the teeth progressing from dirty beige to aged ivory. The claws can be finished in yellowed bone, dark horn, or pale grey. A small amount of gloss varnish on the skin, mouth, and webbing can create a convincing wet finish. The ragged garment works well in faded brown, black-green, or washed-out maroon. Paint the base in cold stone greys and muted coastal browns. Sculpted water can be layered with dark teal, medium blue-green, and pale blue-grey highlights along the ripples, followed by gloss varnish. Shells and stones offer small accents in beige, off-white, and muted orange-brown. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

Werdandi-Figur Diese Figur stellt Werdandi, die zweite der drei Nornen aus der nordischen Mythologie, dar (neben Urd und Skuld). Sie ist in einer anmutigen, stehenden Pose dargestellt und trägt ein langes, fließendes Gewand, das ihre Figur und Beine umhüllt, aber auch viel nackte Haut zeigt, besonders am Oberkörper und am rechten Bein. Ihr Haar ist kunstvoll hochgesteckt, mit einigen Strähnen, die ihr Gesicht umrahmen. Sie hält einen kleinen Krug oder eine Kanne in ihren Händen, die sie nach vorne hält. Ihre linke Hand stützt den Boden des Krugs, ihre rechte hält ihn am Hals. Wissenswertes zu Werdandi Werdandi ist in der nordischen Mythologie die mittlere der drei Nornen und repräsentiert "das, was wird" oder die Gegenwart. Ihr Name wird oft als "Werden" oder "die Werdende" übersetzt. Sie ist eine Schicksalsgöttin und webt zusammen mit ihren Schwestern am Schicksalsfaden der Menschen und Götter. Ihre Darstellung als Frau mit einem Krug könnte ihre Rolle beim Schöpfen aus dem Brunnen des Schicksals, Urðarbrunnr, symbolisieren. Vielseitigkeit der Figur Obwohl sie spezifisch als Werdandi entworfen wurde, kann diese Figur aufgrund ihres generischen Fantasy-Adligen- oder Göttinnen-Aussehens natürlich auch für viele andere Zwecke verwendet werden. Sie eignet sich hervorragend für Rollenspiele (wie D&D oder Pathfinder), Tabletop-Wargaming (zum Beispiel als Priesterin oder Adlige) oder einfach als Sammlerstück. Zweites Diorama-Element Diese Figur ist das zweite Element eines geplanten Dioramas, das eine Szene aus der nordischen Mythologie darstellen wird. Sie ergänzt die erste Figur, Skuld (die Kriegernorne), und bildet einen Kontrast zu ihr, indem sie die Gegenwart und die Sanftheit repräsentiert, während Skuld die Zukunft und den Kampf symbolisiert. Die Rüstung und die Pose von Werdandi sind so gestaltet, dass sie sich harmonisch in die geplante Umgebung einfügen und eine dynamische Szenerie mit ihrer Schwester ergeben.

description: Goblin Boss Miniature – Cunning Tyrant of the Tribe This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Goblin Boss is presented as the ruthless leader of a goblin warband: louder, crueler, and far more confident than the warriors that follow it. Unlike a common Goblin Warrior, the Boss relies on intimidation, tactical positioning, and overwhelming numbers. Its commanding pose, superior equipment, and trophy-laden attire immediately distinguish it from lesser goblins while remaining practical for high-quality 3D printing. The Goblin Boss has the compact, wiry proportions characteristic of goblins, standing low to the ground with a broad, balanced stance. Although physically much smaller than most humanoid opponents, the miniature should project confidence through posture rather than size. The torso leans slightly forward while the legs remain spread wide, giving the impression that the Boss is barking orders while remaining ready to spring into combat. Its head is oversized compared to its body, creating the classic goblin silhouette. The face is angular and deeply expressive, with a broad flattened nose, pronounced brow, wrinkled forehead, sharp cheekbones, and a wide mouth filled with crooked yellowed teeth. The lips are curled into an aggressive snarl, exposing several oversized canines. Narrow eyes glare toward an unseen enemy with a mixture of arrogance and malice. The ears are long, broad, and sharply pointed, projecting outward from both sides of the head and giving the miniature an instantly recognizable profile. The Goblin Boss wears noticeably better equipment than ordinary members of its tribe. A reinforced leather cuirass covers the chest, strengthened with overlapping iron plates, rivets, and crude metal edging. One shoulder carries a large scavenged pauldron while the opposite shoulder remains lightly protected, creating an asymmetrical appearance typical of goblin craftsmanship. Numerous leather straps cross the torso, securing pouches, knives, and trophies without becoming overly cluttered. A heavy belt supports layered leather skirt panels that protect the hips and upper thighs. Attached to the belt are a skull trophy, several crude charms, and small pouches for stolen valuables or battlefield supplies. Every accessory remains firmly attached to neighbouring equipment to ensure print durability. The Boss wears a tattered cloak draped from one shoulder. Rather than flowing dramatically, the cloak hangs in broad, thick folds close to the body, with torn lower edges suggesting long campaigns and rough treatment. The cloth connects naturally to the back and legs, preventing fragile unsupported sections. One arm extends fully forward with an accusing finger aimed directly at its next victim. This gesture is the defining feature of the miniature, immediately communicating command, leadership, and ruthless authority. The extended arm remains slightly bent, while the finger itself is thick enough for dependable miniature printing. The opposite hand grips a broad curved falchion or heavy goblin scimitar. The blade is chipped, uneven, and obviously scavenged rather than expertly forged. It has a thick spine, reinforced guard, and compact point, making it both visually intimidating and structurally durable. The weapon hangs low beside the body, ready to swing after the Boss has ordered its followers into battle. Leather bracers reinforce both forearms, while wrapped bindings protect the wrists and lower legs. The feet remain bare, ending in broad splayed toes that grip the uneven ground securely. Every limb remains close enough to the body to maintain excellent structural integrity. The Goblin Boss should appear experienced rather than heroic. Small scars, damaged armour, patched leather, dented metal plates, and repaired straps all reinforce the impression that this creature has survived countless raids through cunning rather than honour. Its equipment should feel stolen, repaired, and reused many times. A fitting colour palette begins with yellow-green or olive skin highlighted toward lighter green across the face, hands, and ears. Leather should range from dark brown to reddish tan, while armour works well in blackened iron, tarnished steel, or aged bronze. The cloak provides an excellent opportunity for dark crimson, faded brown, or charcoal cloth. The skull trophy and scattered bones offer natural pale bone contrast. The round tabletop base represents a rough woodland trail or abandoned campsite. Low rocks, exposed roots, scattered gravel, and sparse patches of moss surround the Boss's feet. The terrain remains compact and unobtrusive, ensuring the commanding pointing gesture and curved blade remain the primary visual focus. Lead through fear. Strike through numbers. Mercy wastes opportunities. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Goblin Boss based on the Monster Manual 2024 design. Instantly recognizable commanding pointing pose. Compact goblin proportions with an aggressive forward stance. Oversized goblin head featuring long pointed ears and snarling expression. Broad curved falchion held low in a practical combat position. Reinforced leather and scavenged metal armour unique among goblin ranks. Large asymmetrical shoulder guard for a stronger silhouette. Tattered shoulder cloak sculpted in thick connected folds. Skull trophy, pouches, and crude ornaments integrated into the belt. Bare goblin feet firmly planted on the round base. Thickened fingers, weapon, ears, and cloak edges for reliable printing. No floating accessories, magical effects, smoke, or background scenery. Compact woodland terrain with stones, roots, and scattered debris. Clearly distinguished from the Goblin Warrior, Minion, and Hexer. Suitable for goblin encounters, tribal leaders, ambushes, and dungeon adventures. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and carefully calibrated FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Start with olive-green or yellow-green skin, applying a brown-green wash into the facial wrinkles, fingers, ears, and muscles. Highlight raised areas using progressively lighter yellow-green and pale olive to emphasize the exaggerated goblin features. Paint the leather armour in varied browns, from dark mahogany to worn tan. Shade deeply around straps and stitching using dark brown washes before edge-highlighting with lighter leather tones. The cloak works especially well in faded crimson, charcoal, or dark brown, with dusty highlights across the raised folds. Use blackened iron or tarnished steel for the armour plates and sword. Apply orange-brown rust sparingly around rivets and damaged edges, followed by restrained silver highlights along the blade and armour corners. Paint the skull trophy in aged bone using sepia washes and ivory highlights. Finish the base with dark earth, grey stones, exposed roots, and muted green moss. A matte finish across skin, leather, and terrain contrasts nicely with satin metallic armour and subtle gloss on the eyes and teeth. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Small Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Guard Miniature – Vigilant Defender of the Realm This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Guard represents the disciplined soldiers that protect towns, castles, temples, and trade routes throughout countless fantasy settings. While individually less powerful than seasoned adventurers, Guards form the backbone of every civilized realm. Their equipment is practical, standardized, and built for reliability rather than heroics. The Guard stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a disciplined defensive stance. Both feet are planted firmly on uneven cobblestones, with the weight distributed evenly to create a stable and believable pose. Rather than charging forward or posing dramatically, the Guard stands ready to receive an approaching threat, conveying professionalism and restraint. The body is realistically proportioned beneath practical clothing and armor. The figure wears a quilted red gambeson that extends to mid-thigh, providing protection while allowing freedom of movement. Heavy folds in the fabric create strong sculptural depth, making the miniature rewarding to paint without introducing unnecessary complexity. A simple steel helmet protects the head. It features a rounded dome with a reinforced brow and subtle rivet detailing, remaining thick enough for reliable printing. description: Kuo-Toa Miniature – Fanatical Deepwater Spear Hunter This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. Dwelling in the darkest lakes, flooded caverns, and forgotten underwater ruins, the Kuo-Toa are unsettling amphibious humanoids whose unwavering religious fanaticism and unpredictable behavior make them some of the Underdark's most memorable inhabitants. This miniature faithfully recreates the classic Kuo-Toa warrior shown in the uploaded reference, depicting a cautious but battle-ready sentry armed with a long spear and prepared to defend its submerged domain. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a broad, defensive stance. Both large webbed feet are firmly planted in shallow marshy ground, with bent knees lowering the creature's center of gravity. The pose immediately conveys alertness rather than reckless aggression, suggesting a hunter patiently waiting for prey to venture too close before striking with its spear. The wide footing also provides excellent balance for printing and gameplay. The anatomy remains unmistakably piscine. The torso is lean and muscular without appearing overly heroic, reflecting a creature adapted for swimming and sudden bursts of movement. Long arms end in broad webbed hands capable of gripping weapons securely, while thick digitigrade legs terminate in wide amphibious feet with individually sculpted webbing between the toes. The proportions remain faithful to the Monster Manual depiction, giving the creature an awkward yet surprisingly capable physical presence. The head serves as the miniature's strongest focal point. Large bulging fish-like eyes protrude prominently from either side of the skull, immediately identifying the creature as a Kuo-Toa. The eyes stare forward with an unsettling, almost vacant intensity that perfectly captures the race's strange demeanor. A broad amphibious mouth stretches across the face, filled with rows of small pointed teeth visible between slightly parted lips. Fine gill slits and subtle folds around the jaw reinforce the aquatic anatomy without becoming overly delicate for printing. The creature's skin displays layered amphibious textures that transition naturally across the body. Smooth, damp-looking areas cover the chest and abdomen, while fine scales and rougher textures appear along the shoulders, limbs, back, and head. Slight ridges running across the spine hint at primitive dorsal fins without creating fragile protrusions. These varied textures provide painters with numerous opportunities for shading and highlighting. The Kuo-Toa carries a long double-ended spear held horizontally across its body with both hands. The thick wooden shaft is wrapped with coarse rope bindings near each grip, while both spearheads feature rugged forged metal points appropriate for a tribal civilization. The weapon remains close to the torso, ensuring excellent structural integrity while reinforcing the miniature's defensive posture. Its clothing remains simple and functional. A rough leather harness crosses the shoulders, supporting a short weathered cloak draped across the upper back. Around the waist hangs a layered cloth loincloth secured with braided rope, accompanied by small leather pouches suitable for carrying fishing tools, charms, or ritual objects. Rope wrappings around the wrists and ankles further emphasize the primitive craftsmanship associated with Kuo-Toa society. Every accessory remains securely attached to the figure, avoiding thin unsupported elements while maintaining visual authenticity. The scenic base follows the uploaded reference closely. Uneven rocky terrain surrounds a shallow pool of stagnant water beneath the creature's feet, suggesting the muddy shoreline of an underground lake or flooded cavern. Small stones emerge through patches of damp earth, while subtle puddles reinforce the amphibious environment without overwhelming the composition. The base remains clean and compact, complementing rather than distracting from the miniature itself. The recommended paint scheme reflects the classic coloration shown in the reference. The skin begins with muted blue-green tones, shaded with dark teal washes before gradually transitioning toward lighter turquoise highlights across the raised muscles and facial features. The underside of the jaw, abdomen, and palms may receive slightly lighter desaturated green or grey-blue tones to create natural contrast. The enormous eyes become instant focal points when painted with rich amber or golden-orange irises surrounding glossy black pupils. Teeth are painted in aged ivory with subtle sepia shading, while the spear combines weathered brown wood with dark iron spearheads. Leather equipment uses worn reddish-brown tones, and the damp base benefits from earthy browns, dark greys, green algae effects, and gloss varnish applied selectively to the water surface for a convincing wet appearance. Silent beneath black waters. Faith guides every spear. The depths are always watching. ✨ Key Features Faithful Kuo-Toa based on Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Classic fish-like humanoid anatomy with amphibious proportions. Large bulging eyes and distinctive aquatic facial features. Defensive two-handed spear pose with strong silhouette. Detailed scaled skin and organic amphibious textures. Primitive leather clothing and rope accessories. Marsh-themed scenic base with shallow water effects. No floating parts, magical effects, or fragile unsupported details. Excellent addition to Underdark encounters and aquatic monster collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before layering muted blue-green across the skin. Apply dark teal washes into the recesses before highlighting raised scales with lighter turquoise and pale green edge highlights. Use subtle satin varnish to create a naturally damp appearance. Paint the eyes with bright amber or orange surrounded by glossy black pupils for an unsettling expression. The leather harness and loincloth benefit from layered reddish-brown tones with light weathering, while the spear shaft can be painted weathered wood with dark iron spearheads. Finish the base using layered mud browns, cold grey rocks, green algae washes, and selective gloss varnish to create convincing shallow swamp water. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, particularly Underdark adventures, flooded caverns, subterranean lakes, aquatic encounters, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. On some models, these parts may disconnect or break more easily if handled roughly. Please handle the models with care. They are not intended for aggressive play, but rather as educational models, display pieces, or gentle collectible toys. Durability may vary from model to model. Some models are stronger and may be suitable for careful play, while others are more delicate and better suited for display on a shelf. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. Safety Notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing them too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a choking risk. If you adjust parts with heat, always proceed carefully and use heat gently. Support / Links: I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print it really motivates me to keep creating. description: Hobgoblin Captain Miniature – Iron Commander of the Crimson Legion This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Hobgoblin Captain is a veteran battlefield commander whose authority is earned through discipline, tactical brilliance, and personal martial prowess. Unlike ordinary Hobgoblin soldiers, a Captain leads from the front, directing formations while fighting alongside their troops. The Monster Manual 2024 depicts Hobgoblins as highly organized military societies, and this miniature faithfully reflects that philosophy. Based closely on the uploaded reference, the model presents a commanding officer issuing orders while remaining fully prepared to engage the enemy. The Hobgoblin Captain stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a confident command stance. His feet are planted wide apart across rocky ground, creating an exceptionally stable posture that communicates complete battlefield control. Rather than rushing into combat, he has paused at the critical moment to direct his troops, embodying leadership through action rather than spectacle. His physique is broader and more muscular than that of a standard Hobgoblin Warrior. Thick shoulders, a powerful chest, and strong forearms suggest years of campaigning while maintaining realistic proportions suitable for a disciplined military officer. The head follows the uploaded reference closely. The skin is a warm bronze-brown with subtle olive undertones characteristic of Hobgoblins in the Monster Manual 2024. A deeply furrowed brow, sharp cheekbones, and pronounced jawline give the face a hardened, uncompromising expression. His eyes remain intensely focused on the battlefield ahead, conveying tactical calculation rather than uncontrolled fury. Long pointed ears project outward from the sides of the head while remaining thick enough for reliable printing. His dark hair is gathered into a tightly bound warrior's topknot positioned high on the crown, reinforcing the clean military appearance expected of a commanding officer. The torso is enclosed within heavy layered plate armor worn over chainmail. Large angular pauldrons protect the shoulders while a reinforced breastplate dominates the chest with broad overlapping steel plates. The armor features restrained rivets and practical construction instead of elaborate ornamentation, emphasizing the Hobgoblin philosophy of military efficiency. A deep crimson officer's tabard hangs from beneath the breastplate, extending to mid-thigh in broad layered folds. The cloth provides a striking visual contrast against the dark steel armor while clearly distinguishing the Captain from ordinary soldiers. Behind him, a heavy crimson cloak flows naturally from the shoulders, draping behind the legs in broad supported folds. The cloak remains connected to both the shoulders and lower body to ensure durability without sacrificing movement. The Captain's left arm extends dramatically forward with the index finger pointing directly toward the enemy. This commanding gesture defines the entire miniature. Rather than appearing delicate, the fingers remain slightly thickened and naturally supported by the forearm's angle, ensuring excellent printability while preserving the unmistakable impression of issuing battlefield orders. His right hand firmly grips a practical longsword held low beside the body. The blade is broad, straight, and reinforced with a thick spine, ideal for tabletop durability. The sword hangs in a ready position rather than an exaggerated attack pose, reinforcing the Captain's role as a leader who fights only when necessary. At his waist hangs a second sheathed weapon secured by broad leather belts crossing the hips. Multiple pouches, buckles, and utility straps provide additional military realism while remaining closely integrated into the armor. Layered chainmail skirts emerge beneath the plate armor around the hips before transitioning into heavily armored greaves protecting the legs. Thick leather boots stand securely upon uneven rocky terrain, with both feet making full contact with the base. The round base depicts a rugged battlefield strewn with loose stones, compact earth, and scattered debris. A damaged crimson shield bearing the Hobgoblin legion's insignia lies discarded near the Captain's feet, exactly as shown in the uploaded reference. This broken shield subtly reinforces the ongoing battle while remaining fully integrated into the terrain without creating fragile elements. The recommended colour palette closely follows the uploaded miniature. The skin is painted warm bronze-brown with olive shading and lighter flesh highlights across the face and hands. The armor uses dark weathered steel shaded with black washes before receiving restrained silver edge highlights. The tabard and cloak are painted rich crimson fading into deep burgundy shadows. Leather belts and boots use dark walnut tones with lighter brown highlights. The discarded shield matches the tabard with a dark crimson face and black legion emblem. The rocky terrain combines muted earth browns, weathered greys, and sparse dry grass. Advance. Hold the line. Victory belongs to the disciplined. ✨ Key Features Faithful Hobgoblin Captain inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely based on the uploaded reference miniature. Dynamic command pose with extended pointing arm. Broad military plate armor over richly textured chainmail. Stern veteran facial expression with traditional warrior's topknot. Heavy crimson officer's cloak and tabard. Practical longsword held in disciplined ready position. Additional sheathed weapon and integrated military equipment. Wide stable stance emphasizing battlefield authority. Battlefield base featuring discarded legion shield, stones, and rubble. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, aura, or detached scenery. Strong readable silhouette immediately recognizable as a commanding officer. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and suitable for carefully tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying a warm bronze-brown basecoat to the skin. Shade the facial features with olive-brown washes before layering lighter flesh tones across the brow, nose, cheeks, and hands. Paint the armor using dark gunmetal followed by black washes to deepen every plate junction. Highlight the edges using restrained silver to create a battle-worn but well-maintained appearance. Chainmail benefits from controlled steel drybrushing to emphasize its texture. The crimson tabard and cloak should be layered from dark burgundy into rich red highlights along the folds and edges. Leather belts, boots, and scabbards work well in dark walnut highlighted with warm tan. Paint the discarded shield to match the Captain's colors, weathering its edges with scratches and exposed steel. Finish the rocky battlefield base using layered earth browns and cool greys with sparse tufts of dry grass. Apply a matte varnish to the cloth and terrain while allowing the armor and sword to retain a restrained metallic sheen befitting an experienced legion commander. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, military campaigns, organized Hobgoblin warbands, fortress assaults, and premium miniature collections.

description: Bring crusader stronghold architecture to your grimdark sci-fi battlefield with this detailed Black Templars Citadel Gatehouse terrain piece. This model is designed as a fortified gatehouse section inspired by the monumental fortress architecture of the Black Templars. The piece combines a massive arched gateway, gothic buttresses, elevated fighting platform, battle-damaged upper walls and prominent crusader iconography, creating a dramatic mix of fortress entrance, ruined strongpoint and tactical terrain. It works perfectly as cover, line-of-sight blocking terrain, objective scenery or a thematic centerpiece for grimdark sci-fi tabletops. With its tall silhouette and multi-level design, the model is especially well suited for defending chokepoints, forming the entrance to a larger fortress complex or acting as a commanding focal point on the battlefield. It fits naturally into crusader keeps, shattered citadels, shrine districts or war-torn imperial cities and adds both tactical value and strong Black Templars character to the table. All my models are real test prints, not just digital renders. I always try to find the best balance between print time, level of detail and filament usage, so the terrain looks impressive on the table without becoming unnecessarily difficult or wasteful to print. I also put a lot of effort into optimizing the files, removing print issues and making the models as user-friendly as possible. My goal is to offer terrain that prints cleanly, feels solid, and can be used straight from the printer or painted with simple drybrushing techniques. Designed with FDM printing in mind, the piece is suitable for PLA filament printing and looks great in simple grey material without any color changes. description: Lemure Swarm Miniature – Tide of Damned Souls This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lemure Swarm represents one of the most horrifying manifestations of infernal corruption—a heaving mass of countless damned souls fused together into a single crawling nightmare. Closely inspired by the uploaded reference and the Monster Manual 2024 depiction, this miniature emphasizes overwhelming organic horror rather than speed or aggression. The miniature is designed on a Large (50 mm) round tabletop base , allowing the sprawling mass of bodies to nearly fill the entire footprint. Instead of depicting individual Lemures standing separately, dozens of infernal bodies have merged into one towering mound of living flesh. The broad contact area gives the model exceptional structural stability while creating an unmistakable silhouette unlike any other fiend in the collection. The lower portion forms a thick pool of liquefied infernal flesh that spreads naturally across the base. From this grotesque foundation, countless humanoid forms emerge as though attempting to free themselves from eternal imprisonment. Bodies are only partially formed before dissolving back into the surrounding mass, creating a seamless transition between individual Lemures and the larger swarm. No figure appears completely separate; every soul remains permanently fused to the collective. Dominating the composition are numerous screaming faces positioned at different heights throughout the mound. Some stretch upward with mouths opened impossibly wide in silent agony, while others twist sideways or emerge only halfway from the flesh. Every expression conveys suffering rather than rage, reinforcing the tragic nature of these damned beings. The faces vary subtly in size and angle, preventing visual repetition while maintaining the impression of an endless sea of tortured souls. Multiple malformed arms reach outward from every direction. Some extend fully toward unseen victims with clawed fingers spread wide, while others appear only halfway formed before disappearing back into the flesh. Thick strands of melting tissue connect every limb directly to the central body, ensuring there are no fragile unsupported parts while enhancing the impression that the swarm itself is continuously shifting and reforming. The surface of the miniature is densely textured with stretched skin, flowing muscle fibers, sagging folds, puckered scars, exposed veins, and merging anatomical forms. Faces dissolve into shoulders, arms vanish into torsos, and bodies blend seamlessly together without clear boundaries. This continuous sculpt creates remarkable visual depth while remaining strong enough for reliable resin printing. Rather than standing upright, the swarm advances slowly as a creeping wall of flesh. The front of the miniature pushes forward with numerous crawling limbs dragging the mass across the ground, while the rear rises into a mound of intertwined bodies that gives the model impressive height despite having no fragile vertical structures. This low center of gravity makes the miniature exceptionally durable for gaming. The scenic base depicts corrupted infernal ground partially submerged beneath pools of viscous flesh. Weathered skulls, broken bones, scattered debris, and patches of cracked earth emerge from beneath the advancing tide, suggesting countless previous victims consumed by the swarm. Every scenic element is sculpted directly into the base to maximize durability and simplify printing. The recommended paint scheme closely follows the uploaded reference. The flesh should be painted using pale ivory, unhealthy pinks, bruised purples, raw crimson, and desaturated flesh tones blended together across the numerous bodies. Deep burgundy washes settle into every fold while lighter ivory highlights emphasize the stretched skin. The mouths benefit from dark crimson interiors with yellowed teeth and pale tongues, creating striking focal points across the model. Thin layers of gloss varnish on selected areas can simulate wet, freshly formed flesh without overwhelming the entire miniature. The infernal ground beneath is best painted using dark earth browns, blackened stone, scattered bone colors, and pools of coagulated crimson. No soul escapes. Every scream becomes another voice. Hell remembers everyone. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Large swarm composed of countless fused Lemures. Numerous screaming faces emerging organically from the mass. Multiple grasping arms integrated directly into the body. Rich sculpted textures featuring flowing flesh, scars, folds, and merging anatomy. Low, stable composition with exceptional structural integrity. Scenic infernal base with skulls, bones, and corrupted ground. No floating elements or unsupported anatomy. Outstanding centerpiece for infernal encounters, Lower Plane adventures, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime in grey or black before layering pale flesh tones across the entire swarm. Build variation using ivory, bruised pinks, muted purples, crimson glazes, and sepia washes to distinguish individual bodies without separating them visually. Highlight raised folds using pale ivory while keeping deep recesses saturated with burgundy and violet washes. Paint mouths with dark reds, gums in fleshy pinks, and teeth using aged bone colors. Finish selected areas with controlled gloss varnish to create the appearance of wet infernal flesh. The base works beautifully with blackened stone, dusty earth pigments, scattered skulls, and dark blood effects. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect for infernal invasions, abyssal battlefields, Lower Plane encounters, fiend-themed campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Gorgon Miniature – Iron-Hided Beast of Devastation This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Gorgon is one of the most iconic magical beasts in the Monster Manual 2024—a massive, iron-plated bull whose thunderous charge and petrifying breath have turned countless adventurers into stone. Despite its name, this creature bears no resemblance to the legendary medusa. Instead, it is a living engine of destruction, combining the immense power of a charging aurochs with the impenetrable hide of forged steel. This miniature is designed to faithfully capture that unmistakable appearance while remaining robust, highly printable, and instantly recognizable on the tabletop. The Gorgon stands on a Large (50 mm) round base , occupying nearly the entire footprint with its broad, muscular body. Every proportion emphasizes raw physical power. The chest is exceptionally deep, the shoulders tower above the hindquarters, and the neck is thick enough to appear capable of supporting enormous impacts. Unlike an ordinary bull, its anatomy is exaggerated to convey supernatural strength while still remaining believable. Its pose captures the moment immediately before a devastating charge. The head is lowered aggressively, one forehoof pawing at the ground while the opposite foreleg braces the creature's immense weight. The hind legs are spread widely to support the powerful forward momentum. Every hoof remains firmly attached to the base, providing excellent stability for both gaming and display. The head is broad and intimidating. Thick armored plates cover the forehead and cheeks, giving the skull the appearance of a forged war helm. The nostrils are large and deeply recessed, hinting at the deadly petrifying breath concealed within. The mouth is slightly open, exposing heavy grinding teeth rather than predatory fangs, while the expression remains fierce and relentless. The horns are among the Gorgon's defining features. A pair of massive horns curve forward from the sides of the skull before sweeping slightly inward toward their sharpened tips. The horns should appear thick, heavy, and solid, with subtle ridges showing years of growth. Their attachment to the skull is broad and reinforced, ensuring excellent print durability without sacrificing their imposing appearance. The creature's hide resembles overlapping plates of forged iron rather than natural skin. Large armored plates cover the shoulders, flanks, hips, and upper legs, overlapping like heavy medieval plate armor. Between these plates, deep seams reveal smaller interlocking sections that allow movement while maintaining protection. The sculpt should avoid excessive micro-detail, instead favoring bold, clearly defined armor segments that remain crisp after printing. Along the spine runs a row of heavy metallic ridges that continue onto the tail. These ridges gradually diminish toward the tip while maintaining a continuous armored profile. The tail itself is thick and muscular, ending in a broad armored tuft rather than long strands of hair. It curves naturally behind the body while remaining close enough to the base to avoid fragile unsupported geometry. The legs are immensely powerful, with thick muscles visible beneath the armored plating. Large iron-covered knees and reinforced joints further distinguish the Gorgon from an ordinary bovine. Each hoof appears broad, slightly worn, and deeply planted into the rocky terrain, reinforcing the sense that this creature is nearly impossible to stop once it begins moving. The recommended colour palette focuses on aged metal rather than organic flesh. Begin with a dark iron or gunmetal basecoat before applying black and brown washes into every recessed armor seam. Successive drybrush layers of steel and bright silver bring definition to the raised plates, while restrained rust effects around joints, rivets, and lower legs suggest centuries of wear without making the creature appear neglected. The horns work beautifully in dark charcoal transitioning to bone-colored tips, while the eyes can be painted in glowing amber, fiery orange, or bright red to provide a striking focal point. The round tabletop base depicts shattered rocky ground torn apart by repeated charges. Broken stone, cracked earth, scattered gravel, and sparse patches of dead grass emphasize the destructive force of the beast without distracting from its massive silhouette. The terrain remains low-profile, ensuring the Gorgon itself dominates the composition. Steel instead of flesh. A charge that shatters armies. One breath turns courage to stone. ✨ Key Features Faithful Gorgon based on the Monster Manual 2024 . Massive supernatural bull with unmistakable armored silhouette. Dynamic pre-charge pose conveying tremendous momentum. Broad armored head with recessed nostrils and heavy jaw. Large forward-curving horns sculpted for durability. Layered iron-plated hide with clearly defined armor segments. Continuous armored dorsal ridge extending onto the tail. Thick muscular legs with reinforced armored joints. Four firmly planted hooves for maximum tabletop stability. Heavy armored tail following a compact, print-friendly curve. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, or oversized scenery. Strong geometry optimized for resin and FDM printing. Excellent centerpiece monster for wilderness encounters, dungeons, and legendary hunts. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying a dark gunmetal basecoat across the entire body. Shade the recesses using black and dark brown washes to deepen the armor joints. Drybrush progressively lighter steel and silver across the raised plates to create the appearance of worn forged metal. Apply restrained orange-brown weathering around the lower legs, armor seams, and tail to simulate oxidation while preserving the creature's intimidating metallic finish. Paint the horns with dark charcoal blending smoothly into warm bone-colored tips. The eyes provide an excellent focal point when painted in glowing amber, fiery orange, or vivid red. Finish the rocky base with layered grey stone, dusty earth tones, and sparse dead vegetation. A matte finish on the terrain combined with a subtle satin sheen on the metallic armor creates an impressive visual contrast. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, including Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, and other fantasy miniature collections.

description: Winged Kobold Miniature – Dragonkin Aerial Ambusher This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. While ordinary kobolds rely on numbers and cunning traps, Winged Kobolds add an entirely new dimension to the battlefield. Blessed—or perhaps cursed—with leathery draconic wings, they dive from cavern ceilings, ruined towers, and dragon lairs to harass intruders from above before disappearing into darkness. This miniature faithfully follows the uploaded reference, portraying a Winged Kobold poised in a low, aggressive stance with its wings fully extended, spear in hand, ready to launch into combat. The miniature stands on a Small (25 mm) round tabletop base in a broad, crouched pose that immediately communicates speed and agility. Both clawed feet are firmly planted among scattered rocks, with deeply bent knees and a low center of gravity that suggests the creature has only just landed—or is moments away from taking flight. The pose creates an energetic silhouette while maintaining excellent structural integrity for printing. Its anatomy follows the classic draconic proportions of a kobold. The body is compact, lean, and wiry, built for speed rather than brute strength. Long forearms, digitigrade legs, and a flexible tail emphasize the creature's reptilian heritage. The tail emerges naturally from the lower back and curves around the rear of the base in a wide arc, remaining close to the ground to provide additional visual balance without creating unsupported overhangs. The head is unmistakably draconic, featuring an elongated snout filled with sharp triangular teeth displayed in an open snarl. Narrow reptilian eyes glare fiercely beneath ridged brows, while large pointed ears angle backward alongside small horn-like protrusions that rise from the crown. The facial expression conveys equal parts confidence, aggression, and mischievous cunning, perfectly fitting the unpredictable personality of Winged Kobolds. The creature's defining feature is its pair of fully extended dragon-like wings. Rather than feathered wings, these are leathery membranes stretched between sturdy finger bones, closely resembling those of small dragons. Each wing connects naturally to the shoulders with thick musculature before extending outward in a broad, symmetrical display. The membranes feature subtle wrinkles, stretched textures, and reinforced wing fingers that create dramatic visual appeal while remaining thick enough for dependable resin printing. Their wide span gives the miniature an instantly recognizable aerial silhouette without becoming excessively fragile. The right hand grips a crude short spear held low beside the body, ready for quick thrusting attacks during aerial dives or skirmishes. The spear has a thick wooden shaft bound with rope and fitted with a rugged forged metal spearhead that reflects improvised kobold craftsmanship. The left hand remains open with extended claws, reaching toward an approaching enemy as though preparing to grab hold or maintain balance during flight. The Winged Kobold wears only minimal equipment appropriate for its lightweight role. A simple stitched leather chest harness provides modest protection without restricting wing movement. Rough cloth wrappings cover the forearms and portions of the legs, while a worn loincloth hangs from a rope belt. A small pouch attached at the hip hints at tools, sling stones, or scavenged valuables collected during raids. Every accessory is kept compact and securely attached to avoid fragile components while reinforcing the creature's practical survivalist nature. The scales covering the body vary naturally in size. Larger armored plates protect the chest and shoulders, while smaller textured scales wrap around the limbs, neck, and tail. The leathery wings contrast beautifully with the harder scales, providing painters with multiple textures to explore. Thick clawed fingers and powerful talons complete the anatomy, reinforcing the Kobold's ability to climb cave walls and cling to rocky ledges. The scenic base closely follows the uploaded reference. Jagged stones and uneven rocky terrain suggest a dragon's cavern, mountain cliff, or ancient ruin. One larger rock formation beneath the extended wings helps visually anchor the model while maintaining a clean, uncluttered composition. Every scenic element remains integrated into the base, ensuring durability and easy tabletop use. The recommended paint scheme reflects the reference miniature. The scales are painted in rich reddish-brown tones with darker mahogany washes between the scales before warm orange highlights define the raised surfaces. The wing membranes transition toward darker brown with reddish undertones and lighter edge highlights to emphasize their leathery texture. Bone-colored horns, claws, and teeth provide natural contrast, while the leather harness uses muted browns and dusty tan cloth. The spear combines weathered wood with aged steel, and the eyes glow bright amber or yellow to give the miniature an alert, predatory appearance. Small wings. Fearless heart. Every shadow hides another dive. ✨ Key Features Faithful Winged Kobold based on the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Classic dragonkin anatomy with compact agile proportions. Large fully extended leathery dragon wings. Dynamic crouched landing pose with strong visual movement. description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Custom Fonts: You can use any font MakerWorld has installed , type it into font_name as "Family:style=Style". description: Windproof Heavy Duty Sand Pegs Stakes with 19mm HEX Designed For Extreme Beach Camping Stop watching your tent fly away in coastal gales. Built out of pure necessity, these heavy-duty screw-in sand pegs were designed to withstand the brutal realities of off-grid wild beach camping. When you are exposed to relentless 70–80 km/h winds , standard tent stakes just won't cut it. These aggressive, deep-threaded spiral anchors bite hard into loose ground to keep your shelter, tarp, or beach umbrella firmly rooted. Smart, Optimized 3D Print Design As a maker and avid camper, I designed these pegs from scratch to solve two major problems: weak ground holding and wasteful printing. The geometry has been carefully tuned for the 3D printing process: Zero Supports: Engineered to print completely support-free, saving post-processing time. Fast & Efficient: Optimized design drastically cuts down on print time and filament waste without sacrificing structural integrity or toughness. 3 Included Models & Sizes To ensure you have the perfect anchor for any beach topography, the package includes 3 distinct variations: 1x Medium Size: Great for compact packing, firmer damp sand, and standard setups. 1x XL Standard: Extended length for deep penetration into shifting, loose sand to provide massive pull resistance. 1x XL Wide-Thread: Features a significantly wider screw thread configuration. This is engineered specifically for extra strength and maximum surface area bite if you are dealing with ultra-fine, super dry, or powdery sand. 1x XXL Ultra Wide-Thread (19mm Hex): A beefed-up, heavy-duty version featuring our widest thread yet and a robust 19mm hex head for maximum torque and strength. (Note: Untested, feedback welcome!) Print Settings & Material Recommendations ⚠️ For Best Results: Print with high infill (minimum 40-50%) and at least 4-5 perimeters/walls to ensure maximum torsional strength when screwing them into the ground. ASA (Highly Recommended): If your stakes are going to sit in the blistering direct sun all day, ASA is the top choice . It offers excellent UV resistance and high thermal stability, ensuring the pegs won't soften, warp, or deform under intense beach heat. PETG (Budget/Alternative Option): PETG works perfectly fine with a simple trick! If you use PETG, dig a hole in the sand until you reach the damp, harder layer, screw the pegs in there, and then bury them back up with sand. As long as they are buried away from direct sunlight, PETG will stay cool enough to maintain its strength and hold your gear secure. Pro-Tip for Maximum Hold in Loose Sand: To get the absolute best anchorage on windy beaches, don't just screw them into the dry, powdery top layer. Dig a small hole until you reach the dense, wet sand underneath. Screw the anchor directly into that wet layer so the wide threads can lock into the compacted sand. If the sand is completely dry or you can't dig deep enough, pour a bottle of sea water over the area after screwing it in to tighten and pack the sand around the threads. Fill the hole back up and stomp it down! Update: New Model Added! (4. description: 🚨 NEW UPDATE: ERGONOMIC BASE 🚨 Following amazing community feedback, I've added a new Ergonomic Base design! It features a rounded finger groove at the bottom to stabilize your hand and prevent accidental slipping that could ruin your wet polish. Available in two Print Profiles: Ergonomic Base (Standard Height): 18mm clearance for comfortable fit. You definitely need magnetic gel polish (usually called 'cat eye'). Regular nail polish dries too fast in the air. Gel stays wet while you use the spinner to create the pattern. Once you get the perfect star/aura effect, immediately "freeze" the design by curing it under a UV/LED lamp. Bring the viral TikTok nail trend to your 3D printer! 💅✨ I designed this magnetic spinner from scratch after seeing the viral "Cat Eye" nail polish effect online. It features a manual spinning mechanism to create dynamic magnetic patterns on cat-eye gel polish. 🌟 FULLY TESTED & UPDATED! Thanks to amazing community feedback, this design is fully proven to work and now includes multiple print profiles to fit whatever magnets you have at home: Universal 5mm & 6mm Cylinder (Through-hole): Perfect for the long cylindrical magnets that usually come included with cat-eye polishes. The through-hole design allows magnets of any length to fit flawlessly. Standard Round Magnets: The original profile for two 9x1.5mm neodymium magnets. 💡 Pro-Tip for the best Cat-Eye Effect: Do not spin it too fast! Place your finger inside, hold the spinner close to the wet polish, and spin the top part slowly . This gives the magnetic particles enough time to react to the changing polarity, creating a beautiful star or aura pattern. Cure immediately after! Recommended Print Settings: Layer height: 0.2 mm Walls/Perimeters: 3 Infill: 15% (Gyroid) Supports: No supports needed! Print time & material: ~45 minutes / 18g of PLA. Death Box - “BREAK IN CASE OF DEATH” Ever wanted to leave a secret note, passwords, safe combos, or photos to a friend or loved one in case of your uneventful passing? Here is your chance! There is a gap inside this box where you can seal in a note or photo mid-print. The size of the gap is 140mm x 112mm x 3mm (5.5in x 4.4in x 0.12in) which is the perfect size to fit a folded up piece of letter-sized paper (folded twice). You can probably fit more than one page, but one page fits nicely. I set this print to pause at layer 730 which is about the top of the gap inside. Once paused, insert your note or picture into the print, make sure it is flush, or below the print layer, and resume printing. I added a 10mm brim as well since this is a tall and narrow print. There are two models in this design. One is a standard infill model that is quite difficult to break open. The other has a weak point in the middle where I set it to 0% infill which makes it a lot easier to snap in half with your hands. I put a cool fuzzy skin on the file (Voronoi, which makes it looks like stone) but you can turn that off or make any skin you want. Feel free to change the text as well!

description: This one was quite the task! I originally did my clicker bar using these transparent bead storage cases which worked perfectly fine while making the odd one at home but I ran into a bit of an issue when we took it to our events. The first was they were quite small in height meaning I couldn't put a lot of keycaps in them, it also caused overflow into the other containers when people were digging around for the colour they wanted so I had random letters mixed in with each other. 😩 They were also a pain to put out on display because they came with an attached lid so I had to keep them closed after people left or use double the space to keep them open. Not great when you're already busy enough building the actual clickers and limited on table space! That got me motivated to upgrade the display - I looked around for a while but couldn't find anything that really matched what I needed so I set myself to work. The main issues I needed to resolve were: It had to be modular so I can always add extras for new keycaps if needed. Had to be held together somehow during the events so it doesn't get pushed over easily by people but needs to be able to accommodate for different sized bins and layouts due to table restrictions. A slot to show the letters/symbols as people often got lost trying to find letters if keycaps were flipped upside down in the box, worse if letters got mixed around already. Ideally stackable so I can just stack them together after events and pack it away in a box for ease of use. A lid preferably so they don't accidentally fall out or have other small objects fall into them. Features of the storage bins: Fully modular. x1, x4 and x9 bins. Bins are stackable. Please note x9 bin requires 256mm x 256mm build plates but you can print a x4 with x1 and combine to make a x9 for A1 Mini users. Two coupler versions for joining displays. Bins can be attached with the row or the quad coupler. There are both snug and loose fits so print the one best for your printers/filament calibration. Quad couplers are for holding 4 bins together or for joining large 9 bins with 4 bins. The row coupler is if you wanted to build horizontally/vertically only. Display slot version and one without. Slots are slide in and can be removed after event completion by placing it inside the bin with the keycaps for easy storage. Personally I like the slot version but I included one without in case others wanted to use these for other purposes. Stackable. Please note there is a small gap where they are stacked - this finger gap is INTENTIONAL so you can actually separate them easier without them getting stuck. (Mishaps have happened during testing...) Various lid options. x1 lids have handles and coupler holes, x4 lids have coupler holes, x9 lid have no holes. If using the handle versions for x1, please secure handles using GLUE. I could add more variations but I feel like for most people these versions should suffice. For handles I have a short and a taller version as well. There are two sizes to these in case you find them too tight to fit into the hole on the lids. Recommended Print Settings: Layer Height: 0.2mm Nozzle: 0.4mm Wall Generator: Classic Infill: 15-20% Gyroid Supports: Not required Speed: 20-50mm/s for layer 1, then 150-200 for the rest. The clicker bases and keycap models are my own and are available via my Patreon or on Etsy/Cults as a one off purchase with commercial licensing.

description: Ultimate Parametric Pipe & Cable Clip Looking for a pipe or cable clip that fits your exact needs? This fully parametric generator lets you customize almost every important dimension, making it easy to create a clip tailored to your application. Create perfectly sized clips for pipes, cables, hoses, conduits, and many other round objects without having to modify the model manually. Simply adjust the parameters and generate the size you need. Whether you're organizing cables, mounting plumbing, or securing larger pipes, this generator gives you complete control over the most important dimensions. Features Fully parametric design Adjustable pipe/cable diameter Adjustable clip width Adjustable arm thickness Adjustable opening angle Adjustable wall distance Adjustable mounting hole diameter Compatible with multiple mounting methods: Countersunk screw (default) Socket head screw Hex nut By default, the model is generated with a countersunk screw recess. If you prefer a socket head screw or a hex nut , simply adjust the corresponding parameters described in the guide below. For rigid pipes, I recommend using a slightly larger opening angle to make installation easier. For cables, you can even print the clip in TPU . Thanks to the flexibility of the material, the cable can be inserted easily while still being held securely in place. Parameter Guide Gap Angle Controls how far the clip arms are opened. Adjust this value to change how tightly the clip wraps around the pipe or cable. Do not exceed 150° , as larger values may cause the model geometry to become invalid. Wall Distance Controls the minimum distance between the wall and the nearest point of the pipe or cable . A minimum value of 10 mm is recommended, but feel free to experiment. Need to move the pipe farther away from the wall? Simply increase this value and use a longer mounting screw. Arm Thickness Controls the thickness of the clip arms. Thicker arms provide greater stiffness and strength. A value between 3–5 mm is recommended for most applications. Larger pipe diameters may benefit from thicker arms. Pipe Diameter Outside diameter of the pipe or cable. Remember to add a small clearance (for example 0.1 mm ) unless you want a tight press fit. Clamp Width Controls the overall width of the clip. Increase this value for larger or heavier pipes and cables if additional strength is required. Hole Diameter of the mounting hole. Remember to add enough clearance so the screw can pass through freely. Head Nut Depth Used when mounting with a socket head screw or a hex nut instead of the default countersunk screw. Measure the height of the screw head or nut, add a small clearance (approximately 0.2 mm ), and enter the result here. Head Size Controls the diameter of the socket head screw recess. The default value is 1 mm , which disables the recess. If you're using a socket head screw, simply measure the screw head diameter, add a small clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Nut Size set to 1 mm. Nut Size Controls the size of the hex nut pocket. Measure the nut across the flats , add approximately 0.2 mm of clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Head Size set to 1 mm. Printing Recommendations Recommended material: PETG TPU is an excellent choice for cable management applications No supports required Print flat on the build plate I designed this generator to eliminate the need for creating a new model every time you need a different pipe or cable diameter. model_name: Workshop Dust Filter Blower Shop Vac Cleaning Tool
description: Workshop Dust Filter Blower Bring clogged dust filters back to life with this simple but effective Workshop Dust Filter Blower . Designed to blow air from the inside out , this tool helps push trapped dust and fine particles back the way they entered the filter, making cleaning faster and more effective than blowing from the outside. Whether you're maintaining a workshop vacuum, shop vac, dust extractor, or other cylindrical dust filter, this blower is a quick and reusable solution that helps restore airflow and suction without complicated tools. Features Cleans filters from the inside out for more effective dust removal. Helps restore airflow and vacuum performance. Simple, lightweight, and easy to use. Reusable 3D printable design. Ideal for workshop maintenance and regular filter cleaning. Compact enough to keep with your workshop tools. How to Use Remove the dust filter from your vacuum or dust extractor. Insert the blower into the centre of the filter. Apply compressed air through the blower. Rotate the filter while blowing to remove built-up dust evenly. Reinstall the clean filter and enjoy improved airflow. Tip: Always clean filters outdoors or while wearing appropriate dust protection, as a significant amount of fine dust may be released. Printing Recommendations Material: PLA, PETG, or ABS Supports: Not required (depending on orientation) Infill: 20–30% Layer Height: 0.20 mm recommended Walls: 3–4 for added durability PETG is recommended if the tool will see frequent workshop use. Compatibility This design is intended for cylindrical workshop dust filters and may fit many common shop vacs and dust extractors. Please compare the dimensions with your filter before printing. Why You'll Love It A clogged filter reduces airflow, decreases suction, and makes your vacuum work harder. This blower makes routine maintenance quick and helps keep your equipment performing at its best.
