description: Description A fully parametric vial storage solution for 10ml crimp-top vials. Unlike 3ml vials, 10ml vials vary noticeably between suppliers — both diameter and height are Customizer settings from the start, so measure your own vials with calipers before printing. A validated alternate preset is included below. Includes optional label windows so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Two ways to print: Ready-to-print profiles for common quantities — just load the plate you need and hit print Parametric OpenSCAD file for any custom configuration your storage needs require Need a Different Size or Vial? Use the Parametric File The included OpenSCAD file lets you generate any configuration using the built-in Customizer. Layout is controlled by vials_per_row and num_rows, up to 8x8 (64 vials) — the largest grid that fits a 256mm build plate at default vial size. Vial diameter and height are fully adjustable, so this same file works with 10ml vials from any supplier. Validated Vial Presets Default: 22.01mm diameter × 54.0mm tall Alternate (short/wide): 24.02mm diameter × 49.55mm tall Customizer Settings Vial Size vial_od — vial body diameter, measured at the widest point of the straight wall. Measure YOUR vials first — 10ml vials are not standardized across suppliers vial_h — total vial height, from the base to the top of the cap slot_depth_f — how deep the vial sinks into its pocket, as a share of its height. Default 0.65 leaves the cap and neck clear of the pocket Layout vials_per_row — number of vials per row (1–8) num_rows — number of rows (1–8) render_part — set to base , lid , or both Vial Windows show_windows — turns label windows on or off. On by default, so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Note: the window cutout has a flat top edge that may need supports depending on your slicer/printer — check the slicer preview before printing, or turn this off to avoid the issue entirely Fit Tuning clearance — increases vial pocket diameter. Start at 0.5mm, adjust in 0.05mm steps if vials fit too tightly lid_gap_mode — auto or manual. Auto (default) widens the gap on small prints, which are stiffer and can squeak going on, and tightens it on larger ones. Set to manual to force an exact value lid_gap_manual — the gap used only when lid_gap_mode is set to manual Snap Feel snap_p — snap tab protrusion. 1.2mm is the PETG starting point (0.8mm is too soft for PETG at this scale) snap_z — tab position, affects how easy the lid is to pop off snap_tip_ratio — ramp shape. Lower = gentler on/off feel Recommended Materials PETG — recommended for freezer or long-term cold storage. Handles repeated freeze/thaw cycles without becoming brittle. Use snap_p of 1.2mm or higher. PLA — becomes brittle at freezer temperatures; fine for room-temperature storage or test prints only Printing Tips No supports required for the base or lid geometry itself — but if show_windows is on, check your slicer preview: the flat top edge of each window opening may need light supports depending on your printer and settings 15% infill or higher works fine — these are solid prints that don't need to be dense Print base and lid separately or use both to lay them out side by side automatically Always measure your vials and do a small test print (2x1) first before committing to a large grid — 10ml vial dimensions are not standardized Grids larger than 8x8 are possible in the SCAD file directly, but check your build plate size first Design Notes Designed in OpenSCAD, sharing the same snap-lid mechanism as the 3ml Parametric Peptide Vial Holder — a finger lift tab and chamfered entry for smooth on/off feel. Since 10ml vials vary significantly by supplier, this model was built parametric from the ground up rather than fit to one specific vial.

description: Measure your T-track, customize the runner, print and assemble a full miter gauge that actually fits your saw. No more wobbly stock gauges with sloppy side play. This is a complete, fully 3D-printed miter gauge system with a customizable T-track runner, adjustable fence, two-color angle scale (0 to 60 degrees both sides), ergonomic locking knob and a runner lock for repeatable positioning. The runner uses MakerWorld's built-in customizer, so you can dial in the exact cross-section of your T-track (check the description below) and get a snug, zero-play fit on any table saw, band saw or router table. Designed and tested on an Evolution R255TBL+ table saw. Works with any machine that has a T-slot miter channel, as long as you measure and customize the runner to match. Key features Customizable T-track runner fits any non-standard slot profile 120-degree range (60 degrees each side of zero) Two-color scale, printed separately (no AMS required) Adjustable fence (19.4 cm top, 25 cm bottom), slides along two slots for positioning Runner lock with optional spring for progressive clamping feel Reinforced pivot boss (6 wall loops) for long-term durability under side load Lightening holes reduce weight without sacrificing stiffness All hardware is standard M6, easy to source anywhere Hardware required 1x M6 x 25mm hex head bolt (pivot) 1x M6 x 45mm bolt (main locking knob) 1x M6 x 25mm bolt (runner lock) 2x M6 x 35mm bolt (fence) 5x M6 nut 1x M6 washer, minimum 10mm outer diameter Optional: spring, approximately 25mm long, any type that fits over M6 shaft (recommended for runner lock) CA glue (optional, for extra security when attaching the scale) How to get your parts This listing has two buttons: "Open in Bambu Studio" and "Customize." "Open in Bambu Studio" gives you the full print profile with all 6 plates (base, scale, knob, small parts, fence, example runner). All print settings are pre-configured. "Customize" opens the parametric runner generator. Enter your T-track measurements (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height), generate an STL, then either add it as a new plate in Bambu Studio or replace the example runner plate (plate 06) with your custom runner. Important: measure your T-track before printing the runner! The example runner included in the print profiles is sized for the Evolution R255TBL+ table saw with the following default values: bottom_width = 24.30 mm bottom_height = 4.30 mm top_height = 6.00 mm top_width = 19.40 mm Your saw almost certainly has different slot dimensions. Use the Customize button to adjust these four parameters to match your specific T-track. A caliper measurement accurate to 0.1mm will give you the best fit. Printed parts (6 plates) 01 - Scale (two-color, no AMS needed, print in contrasting colors) 02 - Base (main mitre gauge body) 03 - Knob (large locking knob + cap) 04 - Small knobs + pivot cap + scale bolts (all small parts on one plate) 05 - Fence 06 - Example runner (customize before printing) Assembly 1) Measure your T-track slot dimensions and customize the runner model (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height). Use the included example runner as a reference for print settings. 2) Insert 3x M6 nuts into the runner slots (from the bottom). 3) Align the scale with the cutout on the base, press the locating tabs in. The scale should hold on its own. Optionally apply CA glue for extra security. 4) Place the base onto the runner. Insert the pivot bolt (M6 x 25mm hex head) through the boss into the runner nut. The hole is intentionally tight to eliminate play, you may need to screw the bolt in rather than push it through. Press the cap onto the bolt head. 5) Insert the M6 x 45mm bolt from the top of the large knob (push through the hex channel, use a screwdriver to press it down). Place the M6 washer (min 10mm diameter) onto the bolt shaft from the bottom. Pass through the arc slot and tighten into the runner nut with moderate force. Press the cap onto the top of the knob. 6) Press 2x M6 x 35mm bolts into the fence holes (press-fit). 7) Insert an M6 nut into each of the two small fence knobs, close with caps. 8) Slide the fence bolts through the slots in the base, thread the small knobs onto the bolts. 9) Insert the M6 x 25mm bolt into the runner lock knob, place the spring (recommended) onto the bolt shaft, screw the assembly into the nut at the end of the runner. Press the cap onto the knob. Using it Loosen the large knob, set your angle using the scale markings, tighten the knob. The runner lock at the end of the bar lets you fix the gauge position along the T-track. For repeatable cuts, tighten the runner lock once you find your position, then only adjust the angle knob between cuts. Print hints Material: PLA works well. PETG is fine if you want extra durability. The base prints flat. The large knob prints vertically with a brim. The scale is a separate print in a contrasting color (white scale on dark base or vice versa). No AMS needed, just filament swap in the middle. The example runner profile is customized for the Evolution R255TBL+. You must customize it for your own saw before printing. If you print it, please leave a rating, it helps a lot. description: This is a remix of a remix, but I have rebuilt it from scratch in Fusion and designed it to print flat on the build plate, without the need for support. This print orientation makes the tool strong in the areas that take the most stress during use. The keyring hole is reinforced and should hold up well to everyday use. There is also a version with a pocket clip , allowing it to be attached to a shirt or trouser pocket. My wife has been using it at work as a nurse, and both she and her colleagues are very happy with it. So far, I have only printed it in PLA Dual Silk, with very good results—because the aforementioned focus group insisted that it should be “shiny and pretty”. A tougher PLA, PETG, or another durable material should work well too. The tool is, like the remix I remixed , also designed to help remove flip-off caps from medical vials. A note on durability and use This is still a 3D-printed tool. When printed in PLA or PETG, it should be regarded as a consumable item: after enough use, it will eventually wear out or fail and need to be replaced. Print a few at a time—especially since your colleagues will probably become jealous and start asking for their own. I have seen comments on similar models suggesting that the broken glass tip can fly out of the opener. This has not been an issue reported by my focus group, and it may largely depend on how the tool is used.

description: Precision Worm & Helical Gear Set A high-tolerance, 3D-printable worm drive system designed for smooth motion and mechanical reduction. Key Dimensions: Worm Gear (Gray) : ~17.88 x 17.88 x 30 mm Helical Gear (Orange) : 23 x 23 x 20 mm Shaft Bore: 6.00 mm/ 3mm redius on both gears (Fits standard 6mm D-shafts or round shafts). description: 看到社区里有电蚊子包的，有掐蚊子包的，我就想为什么不合并起来呢，一个工具两种享受。 这个工具的核心零件是 压电陶瓷 ,就是你平时打火机"咔嗒"打火的那个小东西。 需要你自己拆一个一次性打火机,把里面的压电陶瓷取出来,卡进卡槽里,把线穿过孔洞，盖上盖子，完事。 卡扣结构,无胶、无螺丝、无电路。 蚊子包的痒,本质是 组胺 在皮肤下搞事。 组胺激活 C 纤维,信号传到大脑,你就开始挠。 挠破皮 → 更多组胺 → 更痒 → 死循环。 疼痛门控效应 :大脑处理痛和痒用的是同一根神经。 来一个更强的痛信号(比如按一下、比如电一下),痒信号就被"挤"到后台去了。 这是 1965 年 Ronald Melzack 和 Patrick Wall 提出的**"门控理论"**,正经医学基础,不是玄学。 所以这工具的本质是: 手动触发痛信号,把痒信号关进小黑屋。

description: 🏹 The Tri-Shot Q-Tip Shooter: Triple the Ammo, Triple the Fun! You know and love the original Q-tip shooter, but why settle for one shot when you can unleash a triple barrage? With the tri-shot Q-tip shooter, you can load in three one-sided Q-tips and launch them simultaneously. It is the ultimate upgrade for office wars, target practice, or fidgeting at your desk. Why You’ll Love This Print 100% Print-in-Place: No assembly, no screws, and no extra hardware required. Just pop it off the build plate and start shooting! Zero Supports Needed: Designed from the ground up to print cleanly without any annoying support cleanup. Compliant Mechanism: It uses the natural flexibility of 3D-printed plastic to create its spring tension. No rubber bands needed! Fast & Low Filament: Prints in under an hour and uses only 21 grams of filament—perfect for burning through those leftover ends of spool rolls. Printing Recommendations To get the best spring tension and durability, use these settings: Material: HIGH QUALITY PLA works perfectly (and gives a great, snappy response). PETG can also be used for a slightly more flexible, long-lasting spring. Infill: 15%-20% (Gyroid or Grid recommended). Walls/Perimeters: 4 walls for extra strength in the flexible bow arms and trigger mechanism. Layer Height: 0.2mm works beautifully for a quick and clean print. How to Load & Fire Prep your ammo: Take three standard Q-tips/cotton swabs and snip off one of the cotton ends (leaving a stick with a single cotton bud). Load: Slide the bare stick ends into the three front barrels. Push them in until they gently rest against the pusher mechanism. Draw & Fire: Hold the grip, pull back the flexible bow arms, click it into the trigger lock, aim, and squeeze the trigger to unleash the ultimate tri-shot! How far did yours shoot? description: Catch the sleepiest Pokémon in its most active form with this adorable Snorlax Roly-Poly Toy! 💤 Designed as a self-righting wobble toy, this sleepy giant tumbles, rocks, and spins for a delightfully long time before rolling right back up again. This model combines real physics with playful interaction, creating a fun, hands-on experience for all ages while encouraging curiosity and exploration! ⚙️ Technical Features & Design Built to be an elegant, easy-to-print project, this model maximizes performance while remaining incredibly user-friendly: Physics-based Balance: The geometry and center of mass were meticulously optimized using advanced physics simulations, resulting in the longest and smoothest wobbles yet! NO AMS Needed: A smart multipart design lets you print all parts separately, before assembling them in 6 simple steps. One-Plate Printing: The ONE PLATE version lets you print the entire multi-color model on a single build plate with only 2 filament swaps! Zero Hardware Required: No metal bearings, screws, or added weights – this Snorlax relies entirely on its 3D-printed structure and solid infill to self-right. 🛠️ Step-by-Step Assembly Guide The assembly process is straightforward and consists of 6 simple steps . For the best results, using CA glue (superglue) is recommended. Step 1: Clean the Prints Carefully remove all support material from the printed parts. Ensure all mating surfaces are clean and smooth for a flush fit. Step 2: Prepare the Base Apply a small amount of CA glue inside the hexagonal cutout of the bottom piece. Step 3: Install the Base Connector Insert the hexagonal connector into the base. Ensure it is fully seated, then apply a little more CA glue in a circular pattern around the base connector. Step 4: Assemble the Body Align the top half of the body with the base and slot them together. Make sure the seams match up properly at the back and hold firmly until the glue sets. Step 5: Assemble the Face Take the white belly panel and insert the eyes and mouth pieces into their respective slots. This is a friction fit, so this step does not require any glue! Step 6: Final Assembly In this final step, take the completed belly panel and simply press it into the large cutout of the main body – no glue needed. Your Snorlax is now ready to wobble! description: Think you've got diver's lungs? Prove it — or prank someone who thinks they do. The Diver's Lung Tester looks like a simple blow-challenge toy: put your lips on the mouthpiece, blow, and try to spin the internal wheel as fast as you can. Turn it into a challenge: "Bet you can't spin it faster than me!" Hand it over. Most people instinctively blow straight into the main hole without plugging anything — and get a face full of flour instead of a spinning wheel. Super Leggiero is the first aircraft in the Ultralight Series , designed around the principles of minimum weight, efficient aerodynamics, and slow, floaty flight . With its ultralow wing loading and optimized airframe, it delivers long, graceful glides in indoor environments and calm, no-wind conditions. The Ultralight Series also introduces an expert hybrid construction technique , where the frame of the plane is printed directly onto lightweight tissue paper. This reduces the flying weight from 9 g to just 5 g —a 45% weight reduction —resulting in even slower flight, lower sink rate, and exceptional indoor performance. While the standard version is designed for simplicity and easy assembly, the hybrid version offers experienced builders the opportunity to explore the limits of ultralight 3D printed aircraft. Complete Lineup Ultralight Series Super Leggiero - 9 g Experimental Series Canard Glider — Experimental Series #1 Gossamer Albatross Glider — Experimental Series #2 Sky Series Cumulus 680 — slow, smooth, relaxed glides Cumulus 400 Speed Wing — faster flights Stratus 500 — balanced and versatile Stratus 500 A1 mini version - Original size Assembly guide: Camber bracket: Insert the front pin of the camber bracket into the fuselage. Insert the rear pin by bending the camber bracket into an S-shape . Then slide the rear pin into the fuselage. (See assembly video.) Make sure the camber bracket sits securely between the locating tabs on the wing. Vertical Stabilizer : Insert vertical stabilizer pins into the slots (1).Bend the locking tabs as shown to secure the stabilizer. (2) Polyhedral Wing bend: Bend both wingtips upward along the reinforced bend lines. Flying tips: Note that the plane is suited for NO wind or indoor conditions only Avoid throwing the glider too hard. If launched too fast, it will pitch up and stall . Instead, give it a gentle push and try to match the glider's natural flying speed. Launch the glider at a slight downward angle . This helps maintain speed and results in a smoother glide. Finetune the pitch by adjusting the elevator control surfaces. If the glider pitches up or stalls: add more down elevator . If the glider dives: add more up elevator . Enjoy your flights! 😊 Expert guide for Tissue Paper Hybrid Edition Note: This version requires patience and experience. It is recommended for advanced 3D printing users. 1. Prepare the paper Cut a sheet of tissue paper slightly larger than the print area. 2. Secure the paper Attach the paper to the build plate using magnets. I use Ø20 × 3 mm neodymium magnets from the Bambu Lab store. Make sure the paper is smooth and wrinkle-free. 3. Check magnet placement Before printing, verify that all magnets are outside the print path . 4. Print settings Disable Bed Leveling . Ignore the warning pop-ups. If possible, set Auxiliary Part Cooling to 0% . Excessive airflow can cause the tissue paper to flutter, reducing print quality. 6. Cut out the glider Use a sharp hobby knife and cut in the direction shown in the illustrations for the cleanest result. 7. Assemble Follow the standard assembly instructions. The tissue paper version is extremely delicate , so handle it carefully. 8. Fly! Congratulations—you've just built one of the lightest and best-flying printable gliders on Maker World. Enjoy! ✈️

description: Feed the Dino – match the color sequence! 🦖 An interactive Montessori-style toy for toddlers: the back spikes show the order in which the chips need to be fed. Drop them into the open mouth, watch them roll through the body, and check the belly window to see if your sequence is correct. 🎨 Want more color variety? Check out the Color Expansion Pack — a new pink/blue/yellow spike-strip and chip set that works with this base model. How it works: Chips drop through the mouth into an internal channel and roll down to the oval viewing window on the belly — instantly showing whether your order matches the spike sequence. To empty it, just press the rearmost spike: a built-in spring mechanism releases the channel, and all chips roll safely into the catch-tray in the base. Assembly Instructions (see below): Place the base platform flat on the table. Lay the dinosaur's back panel flat on the table, holes facing up. Insert the spring mechanism into the designated channel, pressing it in gently until it sits flush. Place the front cover panel on top and press the pins into the holes. Insert the assembled dinosaur body into the base platform. Attach the spike-strip onto the back. Done — drop in the chips and start playing! Stable base with catch-tray: The dino stands securely on an oval base platform with a built-in tray that catches released chips and doubles as handy chip storage between rounds. One part, five color sequences: The spike-strip combines all five different sequences in a single printed piece — no need to swap parts for variety. Encourages: Color recognition, sequence memory, fine motor skills, cause-and-effect understanding. Kid-friendly design: Every part is designed with rounded corners and edges throughout — large, easy-to-grip pieces, perfect even for little hands. Tool-free assembly: No screws, no tools needed — all parts simply press-fit together and hold securely on their own. Efficiently engineered: Color comes only from the outer layers, significantly reducing filament use compared to fully colored parts. The entire model is designed to work with just 4 AMS colors each plate, with no extra filament swaps required. Included: Three print plates (front and back panel with integrated chip channel, plus base platform with catch-tray), spike-strip with all five color sequences, spring-release mechanism. description: Un simpatico T-Rex puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità in un modello semplice, accattivante e piacevole da assemblare. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il T-Rex si sostiene in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico personaggio decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere adatto ai bambini: forme morbide, aspetto simpatico, sorriso inciso, dettagli scavati e dentini ricavati direttamente nel modello, senza necessità di parti aggiuntive o colori separati. Ogni singolo pezzo può essere stampato con qualsiasi colore a scelta, permettendo di creare combinazioni personalizzate e rendere ogni dinosauro unico. Puoi realizzarlo tutto dello stesso colore, in versione bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto più allegro e creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il T-Rex diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è pensato per una stampa rapida , indicativamente in circa 2 ore , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto texturizzato / PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello risulta particolarmente gradevole se stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato. description: Classic Joker Display Figure (No AMS) Every model has a story. This one is dedicated to my son, Alexander . Alexander has always loved the Joker and already had an amazing Batman on his shelf. Naturally, he wanted Batman to have his greatest rival standing beside him. I found an excellent Batman model here: Batman Display Figure But after searching for quite a while, I couldn't find a Batman: The Animated Series (DCAU) inspired Joker that was designed as a No AMS multi-part build. So... I decided to make one. What started as "I'll just make Alexander a Joker" quickly turned into a month-long journey of learning Blender. Along the way I learned mesh restoration, topology cleanup, Booleans, part engineering, hidden seams, and multi-part assembly workflows. The final model you're downloading is the result of that entire learning process. Rather than relying on an AMS, every visible color is modeled as its own individual printable component. This allows clean color transitions with virtually no purge waste while making the model accessible to anyone with a standard single-extruder printer. Features 🃏 No AMS Required 🎨 Individual color-separated parts 🔧 Engineered for straightforward assembly 📏 Approximately 300 mm (30 cm) tall 🖨 Optimized for FDM printing 🧩 Hidden seams and alignment features Printing Tips Print each component using its intended filament color. Dry-fit parts before applying glue. A small amount of CA glue is recommended for final assembly. Assemble from the torso outward for the easiest alignment. I'd recommend using a .2 nozzle for the eyes. A Personal Note This model represents far more than just a printable figure. It marks the beginning of a workflow I've been developing to transform AI-generated foundation meshes into engineered, printable multi-part kits through extensive manual work in Blender. Most importantly, it gave me the opportunity to build something special for my son. If your finished Joker ends up standing next to Batman on your shelf too, I'd love to see a photo of your build. Happy Printing! 🖖 Noblesite

Welcome to The Crystal Mines , an original PlayGrid-compatible board game where every expedition is different. Venture deep into an ancient crystal cave filled with valuable ores, unstable tunnels, hidden dangers, and one enormous Crystal Heart at its center. Your goal is simple: gather as many valuable crystals as you can and escape before the mine becomes too dangerous. Unlike traditional board games, The Crystal Mines features a changing battlefield. Players physically mine crystal deposits, remove ore from the board, and replace them with empty tiles, permanently changing the map as the game progresses. Every crystal collected makes the cave feel a little more depleted—and every decision becomes more important. Scattered throughout the mine are colorful crystal veins, rocky obstacles, mine carts, wooden bridges, ladders, water crossings, and explosive TNT. These environmental features create countless strategic choices as you explore the cave. Do you take the shortest path? Risk using explosives? Race another player to a valuable crystal deposit? Or head back to safety before disaster strikes? At the center of the cave lies the massive Crystal Heart . While it contains incredible value, disturbing the heart may trigger catastrophic consequences. Stay too long underground, and you may lose everything you've collected. Every turn becomes a balance between greed and survival. To keep the game fresh, every match uses a procedurally generated map , meaning no two games are ever exactly alike. Different crystal locations, obstacles, pathways, and hazards create a new puzzle every time you play. Features 💎 Randomly generated maps for endless replayability ⛏️ Physically mine and remove crystal deposits 🪨 Dynamic board that changes throughout the game 🛤️ Mine carts, bridges, ladders, water, TNT, and rocky terrain ❤️ Risk-versus-reward gameplay centered around the Crystal Heart 🎲 Fast setup and easy-to-learn rules 👨👩👧👦 Great for family game nights or casual strategy sessions 🗺️ Map Builder Generate a brand-new Crystal Mines board in seconds! Map Builder Link: 👉 https://crystal-mine-forge-app.base44.app/ 🎮 PlayGrid Compatibility This project is an original game designed for the PlayGrid system . The PlayGrid base module was created by @OzarkExpeditions , whose modular platform makes it possible for creators to build entirely new games using the same shared board system. This project is an independent PlayGrid-compatible expansion and would not be possible without that foundation. Be sure to check out @OzarkExpeditions and the original PlayGrid module for more amazing games and expansions! Good luck, miner… and remember: The greatest treasure isn't the crystal you find—it's making it back out of the mine alive. 💎

description: D20 Spinner – The Wheel of Fate Spin your destiny! Inspired by the satisfying feel of a fidget spinner and the iconic wheel from The Price Is Right , this D20 spinner brings a little game show excitement to every dice roll. Give it a good spin and watch the wheel whirl before it clicks satisfyingly into place on a random number. Inside are ball bearings for an incredibly smooth, low-friction spin, while hidden magnets provide crisp detents that lock the wheel securely onto each of the 20 numbers. The result is a spinner that's both fun to fidget with and reliable enough for tabletop gaming. Whether you're rolling for initiative, making a life-or-death saving throw, or just need a desk toy that begs to be spun, this spinner delivers. Features 🎲 Random D20 number generator 🌀 Smooth, long-lasting spin thanks to ball bearings 🧲 Magnetic detents snap cleanly to each number 🎮 Inspired by classic fidget spinners 📺 A tribute to the excitement of The Price Is Right wheel 🖨️ Designed for easy 3D printing and assembly Perfect for: Dungeons & Dragons Pathfinder Any tabletop RPG Board game enthusiasts Fidget toy collectors Desk décor for gamers Come on down... and let fate decide! Required Parts 2x Bearings - 17mm x 23mm x 4mm - Amazon Link 12x Magnets - 5mm x 2.8mm - Amazon Link Assembly Instructions Install the Bearings Press-fit one bearing into each side of the wheel. Ensure both bearings are fully seated and spin freely. Install the Wheel Magnets Press-fit the 10 magnets into the wheel. Important: All magnets must be installed with the same polarity facing outward . Double-check the orientation before pressing each magnet into place. Install the Wall Magnets Press-fit the 2 magnets into the magnet wall. Orient them so they attract to the magnets in the wheel (not repel). Test the orientation with the wheel before fully seating the magnets. Assemble the Axle Slide the two axle pieces together until they are fully engaged. Install the Wheel Push the assembled axle through the bearings in the wheel. Add the Spacers Place one spacer onto each side of the axle between the wheel and the side walls. Attach the Side Walls Position the two side walls on either side of the wheel assembly, ensuring the magnet wall is on the correct side. Install the Assembly into the Base Press the completed assembly into the base until it is fully seated. Test the Spinner Give the wheel a spin. It should rotate smoothly on the bearings and snap cleanly into each of the 20 positions as the magnetic detents engage.

Element Line – PlayGrid Edition brings the original Element Line strategy game to the PlayGrid platform. Designed around the official PlayGrid Core Module, this edition combines tactical gameplay with the modular possibilities of the PlayGrid ecosystem. Whether you're playing at home, traveling, or expanding your PlayGrid collection, Element Line offers a quick-to-learn strategy game with plenty of replayability. 🎮 Features 🌍 Designed for the official PlayGrid Core Module 👥 2–4 Players 🧠 Easy to learn, challenging to master 🎒 Portable travel-friendly game 🎨 AMS / Multi-color friendly 🖨️ Optimized for FDM printing ♻️ Expandable with future PlayGrid accessories 🧲 PlayGrid Assembly This model is designed to work with the official PlayGrid Core Module . (Use the same magnets specified by the original PlayGrid Core Module.) 📦 Included 4 Element Line corner modules 15 Fire tiles 🔥 15 Water tiles 💧 15 Air tiles 🌪 15 Earth tiles 🌿 1 PlayGrid Core Module 🎯 Objective Be the first player to connect 5 of your own element tiles in a continuous horizontal, vertical, or diagonal line. ⚙️ Setup Each player chooses one element: 🔥 Fire 💧 Water 🌪 Air 🌿 Earth Each player receives: 15 matching tiles The first player places one tile in the center of the board. ▶️ Gameplay Players take turns placing one tile. Diagonal corner contact alone does not count. 🔄 After all tiles are placed Once a player has placed all 15 tiles, they continue by moving one of their own tiles. Perfect for: ✨ Names 🎁 Personalized gifts 🏫 Teacher and classroom labels 🔑 Keychains 🎒 Bag tags 🏠 Desk displays ❤️ Custom messages 🎄 Seasonal words and decorations Features ✅ Fully modular snap-fit design ✅ Mix and match any letters ✅ Create words of any length ✅ Easily change names in seconds ✅ Secure snap connection ✅ Reusable bases ✅ Print only the letters you need Why You'll Love It Traditional personalized prints require a completely different model for every name or word. With this modular system you simply: Print a selection of bases. Print only the letters you need. Snap them together. Rearrange them whenever you like. Instead of printing hundreds of different base configurations, you only need a handful of reusable bases. Whether you're making a short name like Alex or a long word like Print3DFamilyFidgets , the same parts work together. This also makes it perfect for selling personalized products at markets and events—you can create custom names and words on the spot without needing to carry every possible configuration. Recommended Switches This design is built around MX-style mechanical keyboard switches , giving each button a satisfying tactile feel and an addictive mechanical click. For the loudest and most satisfying click, I recommend using Blue MX switches , which provide a crisp tactile bump and distinctive click with every press. Compatible switches can be purchased here: AliExpress: https://www.aliexpress.com/wholesale?SearchText=blue+mx+mechanical+keyboard+switches You can also experiment with other MX-compatible switches , including: 🔵 Blue – Loud, tactile click (recommended) 🟤 Brown – Quiet tactile bump 🔴 Red – Smooth linear press ⚫ Black – Heavier linear press 🟢 Green – Extra-heavy tactile click Each switch type gives the clicker a different feel, allowing you to customise the clicking experience to suit your preference. Printing Recommended Material PLA Layer Height 0.20 mm Walls 2–3 Infill 10–15% Supports None Brim Not required Print the bases upright as supplied in the files. Print the letters face-up for the cleanest finish. Important Print Notes ⚠️ The snap-fit connection has been designed with tight tolerances to provide a secure fit. For the best results: Ensure your printer is properly calibrated. Check your flow/extrusion multiplier. Verify your dimensional accuracy. Avoid over-extrusion. Remove any elephant's foot before assembly if necessary. A well-calibrated printer will produce a satisfying snap fit while still allowing the letters to be swapped with ease. Assembly Carefully remove the two gold metal pins from the bottom of each MX switch using a pair of pliers or side cutters. These electrical contacts are not required for this project. Press the switch firmly into the printed base until it is fully seated. Snap your chosen letter into the top of the base. Connect additional bases together to build names or words of any length. No glue required—everything is designed to snap together securely. description: Turn your kid into an excavator. Slide your forearm into the sleeve, grab the roller bar inside the bucket, and dig - the bucket curls on real pivots just like the actual machine. Then set the bucket between the sleeve plates, push a barrel through each side from the outside, and screw a screw into each from inside the bucket. Snug until the head meets the barrel end, then back off 1/8 turn so the bucket swings freely. Optional velcro strap through the floor slots keeps it on smaller arms. ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition ROTA Board Game ROTA (Radmühle, Terni Lapilli or Wheel Mill) is a 2-player ancient Roman and Greek strategy game. The authenticity of the game is uncertain and was found during excavations. ROTA is played on a wheel board with 9 spaces. Each player gets 3 coin tokens. The first person to align 3 tokens in a row (across the center or along the edge) wins. MILL Board Game The larger board is used to play the game MILL , where players take turns moving their 9 coin tokens to form a Mill (3 in a row), allowing them to capture opponent tokens. The game ends when a player is reduced to 2 tokens or is unable to move. “There she found the swaggering suitors, just then amusing themselves with boardgames before the doors, lounging on hides of oxen…” Translation from HOMER (Book 1 The Odyssey lines 106-108) 700BCE GAME COMPONENTS ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition set includes: 2 Level Board ( ROTA -Upper & MILL -Upper & Lower) 9 Black Coins 9 Silver Coins 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The ROTA Board Game - Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the ROTA board and coin tokens. The coin tokens are stored in the bottom of the box in a single layer and the ROTA board is stored above the tokens. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. Antiquing the Coin Tokens The coin tokens were printed with matt PLA (black) and PLA (white or light gray). The black tokens were antiqued by applying a very small amount of gold color acrylic paint using a dry brush technique by lightly brushing the tops. description: ASSEMBLY: The Trammel of Archimedes is a fascinating mechanical fidget that turns a simple rotating motion into a perfectly smooth elliptical path. As you rotate the textured handle, the two sliding joints travel back and forth through the intersecting tracks, guiding the arm around the centre in a mesmerizing continuous motion. This classic mechanism is often called an ellipsograph because a point along the rotating arm traces the shape of an ellipse as it moves. Every clearance was carefully tuned to keep the sliders moving smoothly through the tracks without feeling too loose or easily coming free. The detailed frame, mechanical arm, and textured handle give the model a clean industrial appearance while also making it comfortable and satisfying to operate. Taking less than 68 minutes to print and using under 22 grams of filament , the Trammel of Archimedes is a quick and low-cost print that is perfect for anyone who enjoys mechanical demonstrations, mathematical designs, or satisfying motion fidgets. description: Un simpatico camaleonte puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il camaleonte si sostiene correttamente in piedi, appoggiando bene sulle due zampe, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un simpatico elemento decorativo per camerette, scuole, asili o spazi gioco. Il design è pensato per essere riconoscibile e adatto ai bambini: corpo tondeggiante, coda arrotolata, espressione simpatica, occhio inciso/scavato nello stesso colore del modello e dettagli puliti che funzionano bene anche in stampa monocolore. Puoi realizzarlo tutto verde, in versione monocolore, bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto ancora più creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il camaleonte diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto PEI texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. La faccia anteriore del modello è pensata per essere stampata a contatto con il piatto texturizzato, così da ottenere una superficie frontale elegante e uniforme. Clicky Bread – Croissant Fidget Toy A golden little croissant with a satisfying clicky press! 🥐 Clicky Bread – Croissant is a cute fidget toy inspired by the classic croissant. The croissant sits on a white paper liner and a tiny wooden cutting board, creating a warm bakery-style display scene. Features Satisfying Clicky Action Press the croissant to enjoy a satisfying clicky fidget experience. The croissant is the main interactive part of the model, while the wooden cutting board base hides the internal switch and supports the clicky mechanism. Classic Croissant Shape The croissant features a rounded curved shape with soft layered details inspired by a classic bakery croissant. The design keeps the main croissant silhouette clear and cute, without making the surface too overly detailed or fragile. Wooden Cutting Board Base Unlike the previous Clicky Bread models that use woven baskets or proofing baskets, this model introduces a tiny wooden cutting board base. The cutting board creates a warm serving scene and gives the model a different display style within the Clicky Bread series. The round hole in the cutting board handle can also be used to attach your own keyring or charm hardware. Paper Liner Detail The white paper liner sits between the croissant and the wooden cutting board. It adds a bakery display feeling, visually separates the golden croissant from the wooden base, and makes the model easier to customize with different color combinations. Desk Toy or Keychain This model can be used in two ways: Desk Toy – place it on your desk and press the croissant whenever you want a small fidget moment. Keychain Charm – attach your own keyring to the hole in the cutting board handle and carry it with you. Both uses are based on the same model. No separate keychain STL is needed. Separate Parts for Easy Color Printing The model is divided into separate printable parts: Croissant Paper Liner Wooden Cutting Board Base Each part can be printed in a different color, so no additional painting is required. A multi-color printer is not necessary. The parts can be printed separately and assembled afterward. Print Profile Options Two print profiles are included. Both profiles create the same final model. The difference is the printing method for the Paper Liner. Standard Print Version This version uses the regular Paper Liner model. Supports are mainly handled by the slicer settings, making it suitable for users who prefer to adjust support settings by themselves. Paper Liner Enhanced Support Version This version includes a pre-designed enhanced support structure for the Paper Liner to help improve printing stability. After printing, the enhanced support structure can be snapped off by hand or carefully trimmed with scissors. The trimmed area will be hidden inside the assembled model, so it does not need to be perfectly smooth. Just make sure not to cut into the actual Paper Liner part. Additional Parts Required One compatible MX-style mechanical keyboard switch is required to create the clicky movement. If you want to use it as a keychain, you will also need your own keyring or suitable keychain hardware. The mechanical switch and keychain hardware are not included with the printable model files. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the square hole on the croissant. Insert the paper liner into the slot on the cutting board. Place the croissant onto the cutting board, aligning it with the cross-shaped hole. Press the croissant several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. If you want to use it as a keychain, attach your own keychain hardware to the hole in the cutting board handle. Printing Notes The croissant, paper liner, and wooden cutting board base are separate parts and can be printed in different colors. Please use the provided print profiles for the recommended orientation and print settings. If your chosen assembly method requires glue, check that all parts fit correctly and make sure the croissant can move freely before applying it. Welcome Back to Clicky Bread This Croissant design adds a new bakery display style to the Clicky Bread series. The previous models used woven baskets, proofing baskets, and square bread baskets. description: Custom Keyboard Clicker Fidgets Create personalized keyboard clicker fidgets using names, words, numbers, icons, or your own custom SVG designs. The files include 2-Slot, 4-Slot, 6-Slot, and 3x3 clicker layouts. Choose from the included A-Z letters, 0-9 numbers, controller, star, and heart keycaps, or use the blank keycap to create your own design. The multicolor keycaps are designed to print face down with an AMS, giving the letters and icons a clean first-layer finish. Switches Each clicker requires Cherry MX-style mechanical keyboard switches. 2-Slot clicker: 2 switches 4-Slot clicker: 4 switches 6-Slot clicker: 6 switches 3x3 clicker: 9 switches My recommended switches are Outemu Gold, Purple, and Red. You can use one switch type for the entire clicker or mix different switches in the same clicker. Keychain Option All versions include an optional keychain attachment hole. To print a version without the hole, delete the generic torus negative part from the model before slicing. I recommend using a lobster claw keychain for better durability and easy removal. Switches and keychain hardware are not included with the printed parts. Parts I Used Keyboard switches: https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005004285423123.html Lobster claw keychains: https://www.amazon.ca/dp/B07SW2HH7L Assembly Print your chosen clicker body and keycaps. Press the Cherry MX-style switches into the body. Press the keycaps onto the switch stems. Attach the optional keychain hardware. How to Add a Custom SVG Image Add the blank keycap to the build plate. Right-click the blank keycap. Select Add Modifier , then select SVG . Find and open the SVG file on your computer. Set the SVG depth to 0.40 mm . Resize the SVG to fit the keycap. Most designs work well between 10 mm and 13 mm , depending on the shape. Position the SVG in the center of the keycap. Make sure the operation is set to Modifier . It will not work correctly if it is set to Join or Cut. Assign the SVG modifier to your desired filament color. Slice the plate and check the preview to make sure the design appears correctly on the first layer. Simple SVG designs with thicker lines will usually print more clearly than highly detailed designs with thin sections. Switch Fit Adjustment Switch fit can vary slightly depending on your printer, filament brand, color, and type of PLA. On my Bambu Lab P2S, an X-Y Hole Compensation of 0.03 mm works well with most of the PLA filaments I have tested. Apply this setting to the clicker body. If the switches are still too tight, increase the value in 0.01 mm increments . If the switches are too loose, reduce it in 0.01 mm increments . Only adjust the setting as much as necessary so the switches remain secure.

Gravity Shift ist eine neue, dreidimensionale Weiterentwicklung des beliebten Spielklassikers „Vier Gewinnt“, speziell entwickelt für das PlayGrid-System. Die Spieler werfen ihre Spielsteine in das vertikale Spielbrett und versuchen, eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Steinen zu bilden. Doch im Gegensatz zum klassischen Vorbild bleibt das Spielfeld nicht immer gleich: Mit dem mitgelieferten Deckel kann das gesamte Spielfeld während des Spiels verschlossen und anschließend um 180° gedreht werden. Dadurch verändert sich die Richtung der Schwerkraft und alle Spielsteine fallen an neue Positionen. Eine scheinbar sichere Strategie kann sich innerhalb eines Augenblicks auflösen – oder plötzlich zum Sieg führen. Da die räumliche Anordnung der Spielsteine mit zunehmender Spieldauer immer komplexer wird, besitzt Gravity Shift eine besondere Siegregel: Wenn ein Spieler glaubt, vier Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, erklärt er sofort seinen Sieg. Anschließend wird das Spielfeld gemeinsam kontrolliert. Ist die Behauptung korrekt, gewinnt dieser Spieler. Ist die Behauptung falsch, gewinnt sofort der Gegner. Diese Regel sorgt für zusätzliche Spannung, Aufmerksamkeit und taktische Entscheidungen. Gravity Shift nutzt die Modularität des PlayGrid-Systems auf kreative Weise und erschafft ein Spielerlebnis, das mit einem klassischen Spielbrett kaum möglich wäre. Spielregeln Ziel des Spiels Bilde eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Spielsteinen. Die Reihe darf verlaufen: Horizontal Vertikal Diagonal Spielaufbau Das Spielbrett auf eine ebene Fläche stellen. Jeder Spieler wählt eine Farbe. Der Startspieler wird zufällig bestimmt. Spielablauf Der Startspieler beginnt. In seinem Zug: Wähle eine Spalte. Wirf einen Spielstein in die Spalte. Der Stein fällt bis zum nächstmöglichen freien Platz. Danach ist der nächste Spieler an der Reihe. Gravity-Shift-Regel Vor dem eigenen Zug darf ein Spieler das Spielfeld drehen: Deckel aufsetzen. Spielfeld verschließen. Das gesamte Spielbrett um 180° drehen. Deckel entfernen. Durch die veränderte Schwerkraft fallen alle Spielsteine auf ihre neuen Positionen. Dadurch entstehen völlig neue Spielsituationen und Strategien. Siegregel Sobald ein Spieler glaubt, vier eigene Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, ruft er: „Gewonnen!“ Das Spiel wird sofort unterbrochen. Anschließend überprüfen alle Spieler gemeinsam das Spielfeld. Wenn die Siegesbehauptung korrekt ist: Der Spieler gewinnt. Wenn die Siegesbehauptung falsch ist: Der Gegner gewinnt sofort. Diese Regel belohnt Aufmerksamkeit und räumliches Denken. Variante für 4 Spieler Jeder Spieler erhält eine eigene Farbe. Gespielt wird im Uhrzeigersinn. Der erste Spieler mit vier Steinen in einer Reihe gewinnt. description: My kid wanted this figure, and I had no idea what it was. Little did I know that it's a character from a really popular Youtube channel. I remixed the Loftyo figure's head and faces to fit 6mm x 2mm magnets because that's all I had on hand. I also figured that most people will have 6x2 magnets because a lot of other models use them. Filament I recommend printing at least the body in PETG to keep the joints from loosening too quickly. You could also add a dab of superglue to the joints to keep them stiff. Magnets I designed it with a pause in the print to insert the magnets. It should be a tight fit, but depending on your printer's tolerances, you may need to superglue them in first. I highly recommend N52 neodymium magnets for a strong connection. These are the ones I got: link . Magnet Orientation It's important to keep in mind the orientation of the magnets. The way that worked best for me was to alternate polarities as shown in the image below, but you're welcome to experiment. Faces I also included a plate of faces I made using the Bambu Studio paint feature while watching some of Lofty's videos. I'll add more faces if I have time, including some for Underpaid Assistant. You could also create your own. Open Magnet Design (Coming Soon) I'll upload an alternative profile with exposed magnet holes for those that don't want to deal with a pause or are using weaker magnets. Body You'll need the body from the original creator, Lofty (also, check out his Youtube channel, it's amazing). --- That's it for now. Please let me know what you think, and if you have an suggestions for improvement. You definitely want to go check out the original and his videos.

description: Benchy Voyage is a modular board game for 2–4 players, created for the PlayGrid system. Every game is different as players build a unique river using modular tiles before the race begins. Once the course is complete, it's time to launch your Benchy and see who can navigate the river and reach the finish first. Build your own river using modular tiles, place obstacles, and guide your Benchy to the finish line before your opponents. Roll the dice, navigate around slippery moss, avoid waterholes and logs, and use arrow tiles to gain an advantage—or suffer a setback! Gameplay is simple enough for new players to learn in just a few minutes, while the changing board layout keeps every match fresh and unpredictable. Roll the dice, move your Benchy, and react to the different obstacles scattered throughout the river. Every roll—can change the outcome of the race. The river is filled with special tiles that make the journey more challenging: Logs block Waterholes Moss Arrow Tiles Normal Tiles PRINTING YOUR GAME Each build plate contains only one copy of each unique piece . Optional: Before printing, use the Online Grid Editor to design your own river layout: Once you're happy with your design, count how many times each piece is used in your layout. In your slicer, duplicate each piece until you have the required quantity for your game. This lets you print only the pieces you need for your custom river, saving both filament and print time. Since the board is modular, you can arrange the river however you like. Create short and fast races, long winding rivers, or obstacle-filled challenges. No two games have to be the same, giving Benchy Voyage excellent replay value. Designed with 3D printing in mind, every part is optimized for easy and reliable printing. The pieces require no supports , print cleanly using standard PLA settings, and assemble quickly so you can start playing right away. The goal is to be the first player to earn 3 points . Each time your Benchy reaches the Finish Tile , you score 1 point by moving your marker up one space on the score counter. Then, return your Benchy to the Start Tile and continue playing. In QWIRKLE CUBES - Bookcase Edition the tokens have six faces in the same color, with each face having a different one of the six symbols. Players roll cubes, then play the cubes to build color lines and symbol lines to score points. The player with the most points wins! This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the all the QWIRKLE Cubes, 4-Part Board and Player Tokens. To store the parts, first add all the cubes to the box. Then place the boards above the cubes. The Player Tokens are stored at the inner edge of the box beside the boards. Whichever color faces up kicks next! Kicker: insert plunger shaft UP through the hole in the base BEFORE putting a coin in the pocket. Press the cap onto the shaft (tiny drop of superglue). Drop the nut into the hex pocket, push the bolt through from the other side, snug it — the leg should swing freely. Goal: glue base pads to the frame's rear face (pins align it). Slide the rod in FROM THE FRONT through the bearing (the collar stops it sliding back), then glue the handle on the rear end and the keeper on the front — the D-flat sets the orientation. Net hood slides over from behind; friction fit, glue optional. OPTIONAL ~26mm coin (2-Euro) in the base pocket as ballast — recommended for hard kicks, glue it in Spring version has a seat for a return spring. Without it the leg's weight returns the plunger as best as possible (button may rest a few mm low; printing the leg at 100% infill helps (already set up)). description: " Know Pain. Feel Pain. Accept Pain. " Bring the leader of the Akatsuki to your collection with this fully articulated 3D printable figure of Pain from Naruto Shippuden . Captured in his iconic, imposing stance, this model is designed for fans and collectors who want to display the power of the Six Paths on their shelf. Key Features: Fully Articulated: Ball-jointed shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles allow for a wide range of dynamic poses. The neck and torso also feature articulation for expressive combat stances. Anime-Accurate Design: Sculpted to reflect Pain's tall, lean physique, with attention to his signature orange-red hair, the Rinnegan eyes, and the iconic Akatsuki cloak with its red clouds . Compact Scale: Stands at approximately 14-15 cm tall when assembled—matching the scale of other figures in this series and similar to the official S.H.Figuarts release . Includes One Set of Hands: Comes with one set of hands (open palms/fists). Additional hand options can be printed from the Dummy 13 base model at 1.5x scale. Snap-Fit Assembly: Parts connect with integrated pins and sockets. Please note: Due to the high detail and tight tolerances of this remix, some parts may have a very snug fit. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: A CHALLENGING BUILD ⚠️ This is not a beginner-friendly model. It is a complex remix designed for experienced makers who enjoy a challenge. Please be prepared for the following: Difficult Fit: The Akatsuki cloak and clothing details are designed to fit closely over the base frame. Expect a tight, sometimes frustrating fit. Be patient and persistent. Reprints are Likely: Some parts, especially joint pins and connection points, may need to be reprinted to achieve the perfect fit. Do not be discouraged if your first attempt is not perfect. Multiple Test Fits: You will need to test-fit parts multiple times, sanding or heating connections slightly to get everything to work together smoothly. High Detail: The model features fine details (hair, facial features, cloak folds) that require careful printing and handling. Printing Notes: Supports Required: Due to overhanging parts (especially the hair and the Akatsuki cloak), supports will be needed for a successful print. Enable supports in your slicer. Recommended Layer Height: 0.12mm – 0.16mm for the best detail on the face, hair, and cloak. Recommended Material: PLA or PETG. For the frame/skeleton, PETG is recommended for maximum strength and flexibility. Infill: 15–20% for body parts; 100% for small joint pins if printing them separately. Assembly: Warm the receiving holes slightly with a hair dryer if joints feel too tight. Move each joint carefully after assembly to break in the articulation. Do not force parts —if something doesn't fit, reprint or carefully sand the offending area. What's Included in the Download: Complete STL set for the articulated figure (including Akatsuki cloak details) One set of hands (open palms/fists) Scale: ~14-15 cm (5.5-6 inches) tall when assembled. This size is optimized for detail and joint mobility. While you can scale the model, note that scaling down may reduce joint mobility and make the tight fits even worse. The official S.H.Figuarts version is approximately 15.5 cm, so this matches well . Post-Painting Friendly: The model is not split into color zones, so it prints as a single-color model—perfect for painting Pain's distinctive orange-red hair, the black Akatsuki cloak with red clouds, and his pale skin with your own custom finishes. Alternatively, a multi-color printer can be used to achieve an impressive, paint-free result. Disclaimer: This is a fan-made artistic tribute. Pokémon TCG Deck Box This deck box is designed to store and protect a standard 60-card Pokémon TCG deck while keeping it compact, organized, and ready to carry. The internal space is compatible with standard-size card sleeves, making it suitable for regular play decks, casual collections, tournaments, or display use. The design combines a clean rectangular body with a secure front closure and a themed upper section inspired by different Poké Ball styles. Its vertical format keeps the deck easy to access while reducing the amount of space required inside a backpack, drawer, or gaming bag. Poké Ball Variants Several themed versions are available, each featuring different colors and decorative details inspired by iconic Poké Ball designs. The current collection includes the Classic Poké Ball, Great Ball, Ultra Ball, Master Ball, and Team Rocket's Ball versions. Each variant maintains the same general structure and card capacity, so you can choose the design that best matches your favorite Pokémon, deck theme, or personal style. Additional Poké Ball versions are already planned and will be added in future updates. Interchangeable Base Designs The base is available in multiple versions featuring different logos, symbols, and decorative designs. These alternatives are provided in a separate print profile, allowing you to combine your preferred Poké Ball body with the base design that suits your deck or collection. The Orbital Gear Fidget combines gears and linkage mechanisms to create a unique and satisfying motion. The pin has a square profile, so make sure it is correctly aligned before pushing it into place. Insert both small rods as shown below. Use 2 C-clips to hold the rods in place. Insert the large rod. It should pass through the handle and both pins, as shown below. Use the remaining 3 C-clips to secure the large rod. Your fidget is now complete! Troubleshooting If the mechanism doesn't feel smooth, gears may be a few teeth out of alignment. Try repositioning it so that both sides are as evenly spaced as possible. This is a fun toy capsule vending machine for classrooms, parties, playrooms, etc. It is designed to work with 2-inch (50mm) plastic capsules. Fill the capsules with toys, candy, messages, clues, fortunes, etc. A single crank yields a single, random capsule. No coins required! Points of Interest Two bin sizes (both hold dozens of balls “Standard” maintains a uniform, more slim profile from bottom to top “Big Bin” maximizes the volume and evokes a more traditional vending machine aesthetic Ratcheting crank handle mimics operational sound and feel of a traditional vending machine Highly modular design allows countless creative color combinations, even for single-color printers Robust design should last for years of intended use Easy, glue-free assembly also allows for easy repairs should any part eventually fail Minimal non-printed bill of materials Required Materials 2-inch/50mm Capsules For example https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CNJXH9DV One M8 x 400mm Fully Threaded Rod (standard 1.25mm thread pitch) For example https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D3TJTYY7 One standard M8 Hex Nut (standard 1.25mm thread pitch-- NOT LOCK NUT) For example https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DRF8KCB7 Four common 608-2RS Roller Skate Bearings For example https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09PKD8QZZ One M3 x 6mm Machine Screw (for securing the handle to the crank) Really anything from 5-8mm is fine #4 or #5 x ¼" is likely also fine Required Tools Driver for M3 screw Small hammer or mallet ( optional for gear assembly ) Adjustable wrench ( optional for threaded rod insertion ) Required Prints Most of these (except for the gears) come configured for PLA, as this will introduce the least issues with potential warping on the large, round parts. However, if you're experienced and comfortable with it, PETG is the superior choice for durability and impact resistance. I do not recommend PLA for the gear asssembly (especially the stem/shaft) as it tends to be too stiff and brittle to handle the repeated torque. Be aware, this is a large print. Expect to use around 2.2-2.5 kg of filament over a total of around 3 days of printing. Choose: EITHER Standard Bin: Plate 1: Standard Cap Plate 2: Standard Bin Plate 3: Standard Upper Base OR Big Bin: Plate 5: Big Cap Plate 6: Big Bin Plate 7: Big Upper Base Base Plate 4: Mid Base Plate 8: Carousel (and spacers) Plate 9: Lower Base This is the only one that requires supports. They are pre-painted for you, but you can tweak them if you like (e.g., use a special support material for transition) Plate 10: Bottom This is pre-colored for multi-color printing. The bottom and the ball chute are integrated into a single component. I do NOT recommend printing them separately as this is also the main structural component of the print. The chute ends up somewhat hidden, so if you need to, a single color is probably fine. Final Bits Plate 11: Misc (Crank and Top Nut) This, too, is multi-color, as each number on the clock is intended to have a color distinct from the base. Likewise the handle has a colored arrow on top. I've also included blank versions of these as separate files if you want to print them blank or design your own. Plate 12: Gears As noted, these probably should be printed in PETG or PA or similar tough and slick material. Assembly Insert threaded rod into printed Bottom. The metal rod just screws into the hole in the middle of the chute. This should bottom out at the correct height. Don't overtighten (it's metal on plastic afterall), though if you need extra leverage, you can use two nuts as jam nuts (put both on the end of the rod and hand tighten them together--then tighten the rod by using a wrench to turn the top nut clockwise and loosen by turning the bottom nut counter clockwise). Assemble the gear mechanism. These should all be pretty tight, so use a small hammer or mallet if needed. Add bearings to the slots on both sides of the gear “Case” Place one side of the case on a table with the “fingers" pointing up and insert the gear into the hole in the middle of the bearing. Insert the gear stem into the corresponding hole in the gear. The “short” side goes into the gear and it should seat fully with the raised shoulder. Slide the other half of the gear case onto the gear stem and slide to engage and fully seat the fingers as shown in the figure on the right. Insert gear case into lower case. Slide gear case through the bottom so that the stem extends through the crank hole. Slide the gear lock panel into the lower case to secure the gear case in place as shown in the figure on the right. Attach printed bottom and lower base. The lower base should slide easily over the chute on the bottom, with the lower base's gate being aligned with the bottom's chute exit. Fully seat the lower base into the associated slots on the bottom; it should be a snug friction fit. Add crank face and handle. Slide printed face onto the gear stem. This may be a tight fit so use a little force if needed, but be careful not to bend or break the stem. Fully seat the face onto the lower base; it will pass through the gear stem hole in the lower base and align vertically using two alignment nibs. Slide the crank handle onto the end of the gear stem. Secure the handle by screwing an m3 x 5mm (up to 8mm) screw into the side of the handle. It will self-tap threads into the hole in the stem. Turn the handle and ensure that the gear turns easily and smoothly. Attach mid base (carousel housing) to lower base. Slide the printed mid base onto the threaded rod. This will be snug, but the rod should “sand” the opening enough to slide down easily from the top. Align the gear slot with the gear and fully seat the mid base into the appropriate slots in the lower base. Attach and align the carousel. First insert a bearing into the cutout in the middle of the bottom of the carousel. Slide the carousel onto the threaded rod; the rod will go through the middle of the bearing. Slide the smaller “inner” carousel bearing spacer onto the threaded rod and down into the cavity in the middle of the carousel. Slide the final bearing onto the threaded rod and seat it fully into the cutout at the top of the carousel. At this point you will be able to lift and lower the carousel assembly onto the gear teeth. While holding the crank handle with the arrow facing up, align the carousel such that the ratchet flaps (pawls) are in the middle of one of the areas empty of any ratchet teeth. The crank should be able to spin freely from 11 to 1 before engaging with any of the ratchet teeth. This is how you know your carousel is properly aligned. Add the final two carousel bearing spacers to the threaded rod so that the “bulb” is at the top near the end of the threaded rod. Attach the upper base so that the hole cover is at the front-left of the machine, covering the chute entrance. Add the bin, aligning the tabs as required to seat the bin in the slots in the upper base and the part of the bin without holes is at the rear. Add the cap. Assemble and secure the top nut. Insert a single M8 hex nut into the slot in the top nut. Slide the top nut insert into the slot to lock the hex nut into place. Screw the top nut into place to secure the cap. Enjoy!! A collection of seven compact magnetic sliders, each with its own texture and sensory intensity. I created this set in part for the @Pipin.World BONBON Capsules Design Contest . The variety of textures makes each one a fun little surprise to discover from a gachapon capsule, and printing the full set lets you find the one that suits you best! Seven Textures Classic : Smooth and simple, with only the embossed icon on the slider. Spiky : The most intense option, with pronounced points that are especially satisfying to press and run your fingers across. Geometric : Similar to Spiky, but less intense and more rounded, with a structured repeating pattern that still provides plenty of tactile variation. Industrial : A subtle diamond plate texture with a gentler sensory effect. Knitted : A detailed woven pattern with a comfortable medium level of texture. Dots : A playful medium-intensity texture that's surprisingly nice to rub along the sides. This one is my personal favorite. Fuzzy Skin : A soft, understated texture for anyone who prefers something more subtle. The set is designed to cover a wide range of preferences. Spiky sits at the most intense end, Geometric offers a similar experience in a more rounded form, Dots and Knitted land around the middle, and Industrial and Fuzzy Skin offer a more subtle touch. Classic is there for anyone who prefers a smooth surface. Magnetic Snap Each slider uses four 6x3mm magnets. Three are placed inside the base, while one is enclosed inside the moving piece. The center magnet repels the moving magnet, helping the slider snap toward either end with a satisfying magnetic response. Printing and Assembly The print includes two pauses for inserting the magnets. Secure each magnet with superglue before continuing the print so they'll remain fully enclosed inside the finished parts. Check the magnet orientation carefully before gluing. The center magnet in the base must repel the magnet inside the slider for the snapping effect to work correctly. Before snapping the slider into the rails, make extra sure it's oriented vertically in the correct direction. The top of the slider is square, so check the shape on the bottom to determine its orientation. Don't try to insert it sideways, which means it's been rotated 90 degrees from the correct position. Once it's correctly aligned, carefully snap it into the rails. If it doesn't go in with reasonable pressure, stop and check the orientation again. Forcing it in while it's sideways may damage the rails. Each completed slider requires: 4 x 6x3mm magnets Superglue Troubleshooting Depending on the filament, the rails where the slider snaps into place may deform slightly during assembly. I've found this is more likely with softer materials, including certain spools of matte PLA. If the slider doesn't travel all the way to either end, a section of the rail probably bent inward while the slider was being pressed into place. Carefully inspect the full path and either trim the deformed plastic or gently straighten it by prying it back into position with a craft knife. Remove or adjust only as much material as necessary. The slider may also feel stiff at first even when nothing is visibly blocking it. Once you've confirmed that it can travel fully to both ends, slide it back and forth several times. This will usually straighten out minor deformation and make the movement smoother. For an even smoother feel, you can brush a small amount of lubricant onto the rail surfaces. Only do this after the slider already travels freely to both ends without lubricant. Print one texture or collect all seven and discover your favorite!

Load: Slide the bare stick ends into the five front barrels. Push them in until they gently rest against the pusher mechanism. Draw & Fire: Hold the grip, pull back the flexible bow arms, click it into the trigger lock, aim, and squeeze the trigger to unleash the ultimate barrage! IMPORTANT: Read Before Printing! Description This project started after the original water tank broke when the water gun fell to the floor. Instead of simply recreating the damaged part, I redesigned the entire reservoir to solve another problem the original product already had: it was awkward to store, unstable when laid down, and could leak while not in use. The new tank works both as a replacement for a broken original reservoir and as a practical upgrade for an intact water gun . Its angular shape forms a stable integrated stand, keeping the toy upright, easy to see and comfortable to grab whenever it is needed. There is no separate holder or additional base—the water reservoir itself performs both functions. Despite the completely different shape, the redesigned tank holds approximately the same amount of water as the original. The wider lower section provides a stable footprint while preserving the grip angle and normal handling of the water gun. Once installed, the toy remains balanced and ready to use without needing to be placed on its side. The tank was designed and tested in PETG for better impact resistance, sealing and long-term durability. The provided print profile uses reinforced walls and a slightly increased object flow ratio to improve strength and sealing. The finished reservoir was tested filled with water to verify the connection and watertight performance. A transparent PETG version also makes it easy to see the remaining water level, while opaque colors can create a more tactical or customized appearance. Because similar water guns may be sold under different names or with small manufacturing variations, a fast Fit Test is included. Print this small part first to confirm that the mounting interface fits your toy before spending time and material on the complete tank. A STEP file of the tested connection interface is also provided for makers who want to design their own custom reservoir, larger tank or compatible accessory. Ultra-Light Reusable Filament Spool I designed this reusable filament spool to solve two problems I found with many existing designs: they were either unnecessarily heavy or didn't hold the filament securely, causing tangles during printing. This spool weighs only 82 grams in total ( 41 grams per half ) while remaining strong where it matters most. Why this design is different The unique spoke pattern isn't just for looksit was designed to maximize strength while minimizing material use. Only 82g of filament for a complete spool Approximately 1.5 hours to print each half Spokes intersect in the center, creating high structural density where the spool experiences the greatest loads. The outer edge uses less material because it doesn't require the same level of reinforcement. This results in an elegant, lightweight, and efficient structure that uses filament only where it is needed. To my knowledge, I haven't seen another reusable filament spool using this type of spoke structure. Easy and familiar to use The locking mechanism is compatible with the same twist-lock concept used on Bambu Lab reusable spools, making assembly quick, secure, and intuitive. Features Ultra-lightweight (82g total) Strong spoke-optimized structure Securely holds filament to reduce tangles Fast print time (about 1.5 hours per half) Reusable and filament-efficient Familiar Bambu-style twist-lock assembly I designed this spool to be as light as possible without sacrificing strength or reliability.
