description: First-Layer-Flussraten-Kalibrierungstest Finde mit einem schnellen und materialsparenden Test die optimale Flussrate für die erste Schicht deines Filaments und Druckprofils. Diese Kalibrierungsplatte enthält 16 einzelne Testflächen, die jeweils mit einer unterschiedlichen Flussrate für die erste Schicht von 0,85 bis 1,15 gedruckt werden. Nach dem Druck kannst du die Oberflächen direkt miteinander vergleichen und den Wert auswählen, der die gleichmäßigste und vollständig geschlossene erste Schicht erzeugt. Warum dieser Test sinnvoll ist Eine falsch eingestellte Flussrate der ersten Schicht kann zu folgenden Problemen führen: sichtbare Lücken zwischen den Drucklinien schwache Haftung der ersten Schicht raue oder überfüllte Oberflächen erhöhte Rillen durch zu viel Material ungleichmäßige Unterseiten Mit diesem Test kannst du mehrere Werte in nur einem Druck vergleichen, anstatt jeden Wert einzeln testen zu müssen. Enthaltene Flussraten Obere Reihe: 1,08 · 1,10 · 1,12 · 1,15 Zweite Reihe: 1,00 · 1,02 · 1,04 · 1,06 Dritte Reihe: 0,92 · 0,94 · 0,96 · 0,98 Untere Reihe: 0,85 · 0,87 · 0,89 · 0,90 Nutze das beigefügte Referenzbild, um den jeweiligen Wert der einzelnen Testfläche eindeutig zuzuordnen. So wertest du den Test aus Drucke die enthaltene 3MF-Datei, ohne die individuellen Objekteinstellungen zu verändern. Löse die Testflächen vorsichtig vom Druckbett. Vergleiche die Oberflächen aller Testflächen. Halte die einzelnen Teststücke gegen eine helle Lichtquelle. Wähle den Wert, bei dem die Drucklinien vollständig miteinander verbunden sind und die Oberfläche gleichzeitig glatt und gleichmäßig aussieht. Flussrate zu niedrig sichtbare Lücken zwischen den Linien Licht scheint deutlich durch schwache oder leicht trennbare Oberfläche Flussrate zu hoch raue oder wellige Oberfläche erhöhte Rillen zu viel Material zwischen den Linien Optimales Ergebnis Drucklinien sind vollständig miteinander verbunden glatte und gleichmäßige Oberfläche keine deutlichen Lücken oder übermäßigen Rillen Übernimm den ermittelten Wert anschließend als Flussrate der ersten Schicht in dasselbe Filament- und Druckprofil, das du für den Test verwendet hast. Wichtiger Hinweis Dies ist ein Test für die Flussrate der ersten Schicht und kein Z-Offset- oder Druckbett-Nivellierungstest. Für zuverlässige Ergebnisse solltest du dieselben Einstellungen verwenden wie bei deinen späteren Drucken: Filament Düse Druckplatte Temperatur Filamentprofil Druckerprofil Effiziente Kalibrierung 16 Werte in einem Druck etwa 23 Minuten Druckzeit etwa 6,02 g Filament keine Stützstrukturen erforderlich keine Montage erforderlich Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch können je nach Drucker, Filament und verwendeten Einstellungen leicht abweichen. description: Full-Bed-First-Layer-Verifikationstest Mit diesem Test kannst du deinen bereits ermittelten First-Layer-Flow-Ratio-Wert auf einer großen, zusammenhängenden Fläche überprüfen und fein abstimmen. Das Modell besteht aus einer einzigen, 0,20 mm hohen Schicht und deckt in der Ausgangsgröße nahezu ein komplettes 250 × 250 mm Druckbett ab. Dadurch werden Unregelmäßigkeiten sichtbar, die bei kleinen Testflächen möglicherweise nicht auffallen. Wofür ist dieser Test geeignet? Der Full-Bed-Test hilft dir dabei: den zuvor ermittelten First-Layer-Flow-Ratio-Wert zu überprüfen feine Über- oder Unterextrusion auf großen Flächen zu erkennen die Gleichmäßigkeit der ersten Schicht über das gesamte Druckbett zu beurteilen lokale Haftungsprobleme sichtbar zu machen verschmutzte, fettige oder problematische Bereiche der Druckplatte zu erkennen Rand- und Eckbereiche des Druckbetts zu kontrollieren die Druckbett-Nivellierung und Flächenkonsistenz besser einzuschätzen Empfohlener Ablauf Ermittle zunächst mit einem Flow-Ratio-Kalibrierungstest den passenden Wert für die erste Schicht. Trage diesen Wert im Slicer unter „Flussverhältnis der ersten Schicht“ ein. Passe das Modell bei Bedarf an die Größe deines Druckbetts an. Slice und drucke das Modell als einzelne Schicht. Prüfe die Oberfläche direkt auf dem Druckbett. Löse die Fläche nach dem Abkühlen vorsichtig ab und halte sie gegen eine helle Lichtquelle. So wertest du das Ergebnis aus Flussrate zu niedrig sichtbare Lücken zwischen den Drucklinien Licht scheint deutlich durch schwache oder leicht trennbare Bereiche unvollständig geschlossene Oberfläche Flussrate zu hoch raue oder wellige Oberfläche erhöhte Rillen sichtbare Materialanhäufungen ungleichmäßige oder überfüllte Bereiche Optimales Ergebnis vollständig miteinander verbundene Drucklinien glatte und gleichmäßige Oberfläche keine deutlichen Lücken keine übermäßigen Rillen gleichmäßiges Erscheinungsbild über die gesamte Fläche Für verschiedene Druckbettgrößen geeignet Das enthaltene Modell ist standardmäßig auf 250 × 250 mm ausgelegt, kann aber im Slicer problemlos an andere Druckbettgrößen angepasst werden. Wichtiger Hinweis zur Skalierung Verändere nach Möglichkeit nur die X- und Y-Abmessungen. Die Z-Höhe darf nicht mitskaliert werden, da das Modell sonst aus mehr als einer Schicht bestehen kann. Model Features Cute black cat and cherry blossom design Three-color layered print No AMS required Only two manual filament changes Easy color customization Thin and lightweight Flat print orientation No supports required Designed for a 0.4 mm nozzle Suitable for PLA and PLA Matte Small hanging hole at the top Great gift for cat lovers and book lovers Model Dimensions Width: approximately 50 mm Length: approximately 160 mm Thickness: approximately 1.68 mm Recommended Print Settings Printer used: Bambu Lab A1 Nozzle: 0.4 mm Layer height: 0.08 mm Initial layer height: 0.16 mm Material: PLA or PLA Matte Wall generator: Arachne Wall loops: 2 Top shell layers: 5 Bottom shell layers: 3 Supports: No Print orientation: Flat on the build plate Build plate: Textured PEI Plate Brim: Auto Brim, 5 mm Final height: 1.68 mm For the best detail, use the included print profile and keep the model at its original size. Color Change Instructions The included 3MF uses the following color order: White – base layer Pink – cherry blossom and accent details Black – cat, branches, outlines, and top details The included profile contains two color-change points: Change from White to Pink at approximately Z = 0.88 mm Change from Pink to Black at approximately Z = 1.28 mm In Bambu Studio, these color changes appear around: Layer 10: White → Pink Layer 15: Pink → Black Because slicer layer numbering may vary slightly between versions or profiles, use the included 3MF or verify the color-change positions by their Z heights before printing. No AMS Required This model does not require an AMS or AMS Lite. To print with a single-filament printer: Start the print with White filament. At the first color-change pause, unload White and insert Pink. Resume the print. At the second color-change pause, unload Pink and insert Black. Resume the print and allow it to finish. Before resuming, make sure the new filament is loaded correctly and extruding cleanly. If your printer does not automatically recognize the color-change commands, add manual pauses at approximately: Z = 0.88 mm Z = 1.28 mm Customize Your Colors The White, Pink, and Black combination is only the original sample palette. You can replace all three colors without modifying the model geometry. For clear contrast: Use a light color for the base. Use a bright or soft accent color for the flowers. Use a dark color for the cat, branches, and outlines. description: The SnapMaker U1's SpoolBox design by CC3DProjects is beautiful, but one of the biggest problems for any filament spool holder for the SnapMaker U1 is the loss of the RFID filament detection feature. The SnapMaker U1's RFID detection requires the tags to be as close to the side panels as possible. For best results, the RFID tag should touch the side panel. Requirements You must have purchased the SpoolBox by CC3DProjects already paxx12 firmware must be installed on the SnapMaker U1 to allow detection of custom RFID tags To enable OpenSpool NTAG215 RFID tags, load in your browser http:// /firmware-config Snapmaker Components > Filament Detection > OpenRFID (force generic vendor) This allows NTAG215 to be detected by Orca Slicer, even for unrecognised brands I cannot share the SpoolBox base plates, as you need to purchase them separately. Instructions (IMPORTANT) Load the CC3DProjects SpoolBox 3MF Adding negative part from STL. Export the negative object in the last plate as an STL file Open SpoolBox 3MF Select the base plate Right-click “Add negative part” “Load” Select the SpoolBox Mount Negative.stl file Position it as shown in the pictures. Reference positions (mm)/rotations below. You don't need them to be so precise; these are just what I have in my slicer. Snapmaker Spool Box LH Plate 1 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: 7.88, 37.09, 56.16 Rotation (absolute): -180, -90, 180 Snapmaker Spool Box LH Plate 2 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: 12, 62.33, -7.83 Rotation (absolute): -180, -180, 138.35 Snapmaker Spool Box RH Plate 1 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: -12.45, 61.69, -7.88 Rotation (absolute): 0, 0, 41.45 Snapmaker Spool Box RH Plate 2 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: -50.68, 44.55, -7.88 Rotation (absolute): 0, 0, 0 For each cutout, create a support-enforcer cube with the same size, position and rotation. As the SpoolBox 3MF defaults to manual supports, you need support enforcers on the cutout. Select the base plate Right-click “Add support enforcer” “Cube” Resize and reposition the cube over the negative object. After you slice, make sure that the supports appear under the flaps. Printing the RFID teardrop wrappers Open the SpoolBox-RFID-Wrapper 3MF Edit the text objects to customise your labels Remember to use the actual filament you want as your base colour, and black or white as the text colour. Purchasing NTAG215 discs Discs must be 25mm in diameter Search your local online shops, or at AliExpress. There are many listings. Here's one: https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005012682271345.html Writing to your RFID discs No app needed; write to your RFID discs here: https://printtag-web.pages.dev/ Push the RFID disc into the RFID teardrop wrapper Loading filament Slide the RFID into the cutout pockets before loading filament, as shown in pictures. Assembly Demonstration Maker’s Note I’m a hobby modeler, and I'm trying to enter MakerWorld contests with designs that push me beyond my limits. This is my biggest project so far, and it took many weekends of modeling, printing, testing, breaking parts, and going back to the drawing board. (I have an ever increasing pile of failed prototypes) My long-term goal is to create a free, easy-to-print and easy-to-assemble parametric generator that lets anyone generate a set of toy fingers fitted to their own hand. I do have a slight tendency toward maximalism, so I’m not ready to publish the fully customizable version until I’ve confirmed that it works reliably across a wide range of finger sizes, but in the meantime, I wanted to see how people react to the idea and whether it is worth putting the extra work into the generator. Please try the current version with an open mind, and feel free to leave constructive feedback. I’ll do my best to incorporate the feedback into the customizable version. Background I first came across this type of finger extension in this Adam Savage video. It immediately looked like something that would be incredibly fun to build and wear… Then I looked at the price tag :D (after spending so much time on this, I fully understand the pricing. Gary's fingers are truly a work of art both aesthetically and mechanically) That sent me down the rabbit hole of researching how I could make my own. While looking through existing projects and mechanisms, I found the work of Dragonator , whose notes were invaluable during the development process. A big shoutout to him. Seeing his amazing model, I’m sure he is one of the few who understand both the pain of designing a mechanism like this and the joy of finally putting it on for the first time and feeling the fingers move with your hand. Design Considerations I’ll demonstrate the main design decisions with pictures below, but these were the areas I focused on most: Cylindrical, adaptive geometry The mechanism is built around mostly cylindrical finger sections. This makes a final design I find aesthetic. I believe most similar finger have an adaptable base section that goes around the fingers, and the rest of the mechanism is interchangeable. I wanted the whole finger to be driven by parameters. Low-profile control shaft movement One thing I struggled a lot with is how to keep the controller shaft as low to the body as possible both at the two end states, and during the movement. With a few tradeoffs, I think I well achieved both. Easy assembly This was the thing I feared the most. In the commercial version, there is obviously no assembly required, it is put together beautifully with additional hardware. I tried different ways of connecting parts, and after multiple failures came up with a snap-in design, which I'm truly proud of. Clean seam lines I wanted the finger to have a clean, cylindrical look when it's straight. However cylinders generally have problems with seam lines. I intentionally placed a straight groove at the bottom of the parts, so you wont need to paint seam lines yourself, you can just hit print and know the lines will look acceptable. The support tradeoff This is the price I decided to pay. Many things in my design are supported, and while many I could have eliminated, I decided the one-time price of removing the supports is well covered by the gains I got in aesthetics and assembly. How the Mechanism Works The finger sections are linked together so that movement from your real finger is transferred through the control shafts to the extended segments. description: Master Sword in Bloom – Korok Forest Pedestal ⚔️🌸 This is my take on the Master Sword resting in Korok Forest after the Great Calamity. Zelda left the sword under the protection of the Great Deku Tree, trusting that Link would eventually return to reclaim it. I imagined it sitting there untouched for the next hundred years, with vines and flowers inspired by the Silent Princess slowly growing around the blade as the forest reclaimed its resting place. It is not meant to recreate one exact scene from the game. It is more of a “what might it have looked like?” version of the Master Sword just before the hero finally returned. 🔹 Model Details ✔ Master Sword surrounded by sculpted vines and flowers ✔ Silent Princess inspired flower details ✔ Raised Hylian crest on the front of the pedestal ✔ Sword and pedestal print as separate sections ✔ Alignment connector included for assembly ✔ Works well as a single color print or painting project ✔ Sized for a desk, shelf, or gaming display 🔧 Printing Notes The flowers, vines, crossguard, and smaller details benefit from a lower layer height. The included profile uses: ✓ 0.08 mm layer height ✓ 0.4 mm nozzle ✓ Supports already configured ✓ Separate sword and pedestal sections ✓ Alignment connector between both pieces The upper sword section contains several small overhangs and detailed areas, so support removal should be done carefully. Flush cutters and a small pair of pliers can help around the vines and flowers. Slower outer-wall speeds can improve the visible surface finish, especially around the blade, crossguard, flowers, and raised crest. Matte PLA works especially well because it helps the sculpted details stand out without creating strong reflections. Assembly The sword section and pedestal are printed separately and joined using the included alignment connector. Dry-fit both pieces before permanently joining them. Make sure the peg sits fully inside the socket and that the sword is standing straight. 🧼 Before Printing Clean the build plate before starting. Oils or dust can cause lifting or failed adhesion, especially beneath the pedestal and smaller support contact points. Recommended preparation: ✓ Wash the plate with dish soap and warm water ✓ Dry it completely before printing ✓ Avoid touching the cleaned print surface ✓ Watch the first layer before leaving the printer ✓ Use glue only if your plate or filament normally needs it ✓ Add a brim if you notice lifting or instability For a textured PEI plate, a properly cleaned surface should normally be enough. 🟢 More Zelda Prints If you like this print, check out my other Zelda props and collectibles below: Zelda Props & Collectibles Collection (Click the image): I’ll be adding more Zelda-inspired props, Elden Ring models, cosplay accessories, anime-related prints, and collectible display pieces regularly. What is the v40 Mini Grenade? The V40 Mini Grenade is an unusually compact fragmentation hand grenade developed in the Netherlands that is roughly the size of a golf ball. description: Want a replica of a US WW1 grenade? This is the original "pineapple" grenade from WW1 that was the predecessor to the Mk2 grenade we all know from WW2. This grenade has a spoon handle that flies off when you pull the pin, just like the real thing would. Background: Introduced in 1917, the US Mk1 Grenade was the first fragmentation hand grenade developed by the United States for use in World War I. It was notoriously complicated to operate in the field, often requiring the user to manually ignite the fuse before throwing. Due to soldiers struggling to arm it under pressure, the Mk 1 grenade was quickly recalled and replaced by the improved Mk 2 grenade fuze in 1918 (which this model depicts). Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Basic Bronze Dark gray filaments are also period appropriate Silk+ Silver Assembly takes seconds Metal Spring Version 1. Insert the peg into the topper while its upside down. 2. Then insert the metal spring in the same way. 3. Then screw the grenade topper onto the body of the grenade. Doing so upside down is easiest. description: Description A modular cyberpunk / sci-fi gauntlet armor kit designed to turn a simple glove into a futuristic wearable cosplay prop. The model includes separate armor plates for the fingers, thumb, knuckles, back of the hand and wrist area. The pieces are printed separately and then glued onto a real glove. I used a fleece glove, but the parts can be attached to many types of fabric gloves depending on surface, flexibility and glue compatibility. I also included a raw full-glove reference file with all parts placed together, so you can see where each element is intended to go before assembly. This file is mainly for placement reference; for printing, use the separated armor parts / print profile. Sizing / Scaling This gauntlet was designed for my hand size: 20 cm from the wrist crease to the tip of the middle finger . To resize it for your hand, measure the same distance on your own hand and use this formula: Scale (%) = Your hand length / 20 cm × 100 Examples: 18 cm hand → 18 / 20 × 100 = 90% 19 cm hand → 19 / 20 × 100 = 95% 21 cm hand → 21 / 20 × 100 = 105% 22 cm hand → 22 / 20 × 100 = 110% Apply the same scale to all armor parts so the proportions stay consistent. Hand width, finger thickness and glove stretch can vary, so I recommend printing one or two finger plates first and testing the placement before printing the full set. Assembly Print the separate armor plates. Place the parts on the glove and check the full layout before gluing. Start with the larger hand and wrist pieces, then continue with the fingers and thumb. Glue the parts onto the glove one by one. I used hot glue for assembly. Be careful: hot glue can pass through thin fabric and burn your hand. I recommend wearing a second glove underneath the glove you are working on while positioning and pressing the parts. Test each part placement before gluing permanently. Printing Notes The included print profile has support settings tuned for easy removal. The model does use supports, but in my test print they came off cleanly and without much effort. Approximate material use from my print: Total material: around 120 g Supports: around 40 g The model was created as a wearable prop, so the armor plates are separated to make assembly easier and to allow the glove to remain flexible. The print profile was created and tested on a well-calibrated printer with a clean build plate and properly tuned filament settings. description: Want a life-size replica of the iconic Bazooka Rocket from WW2? The Bazooka was the US and allied anti-tank rocket launcher used during world war 2. The name is so famous that now the term "bazooka" is used interchangably in popular culture to mean any rocket launcher. This model requires no AMS, even for the text. The WW2 Bazooka was a shoulder-fired, rocket-propelled anti-tank weapon that gave infantry soldiers the unprecedented ability to destroy armored vehicles . It fired a high-explosive, shaped-charge warhead from a reusable steel tube, relying on venting gases out the back to eliminate dangerous recoil. Named after a novelty musical instrument due to its odd tubular shape, it became one of the most iconic "tools of victory" for the Allied forces. Geralt’s steel sword from The Witcher game series, designed for slaying humans. The silver sword consists of a total of 14 3D-printed parts. Like the other swords from my production, this sword is assembled using an M5 threaded rod that runs through the entire length of the sword. Everything is fully concealed and not visible anywhere. Thanks to the use of the threaded rod, the sword is very sturdy, suitable even for fencing, and will not break. All parts of the sword are connected by an M5 threaded rod with a length of 1000mm , which runs through the center of all components. M5 lock nuts are installed at both ends of the threaded rod. One M5 nut is located in the Blade_4 part, and the other in the Pommel part. Start screwing the threaded rod into the Blade_1 part until the end of the rod is 974 mm from the bottom of the Blade_1 part . Then slide the remaining parts onto the threaded rod according to the assembly drawing. The nut in the Blade_1 and Pommel parts are embedded during printing. To insert the nut, a pause is created in the print profile, allowing the nut to be placed into the 3D print. Blade_1 and Pommel are printed on a separate build plate in order to minimize potential losses in case the nut insertion into the 3D print is unsuccessful. For the first time on this sword, an improved anti-rotation system has been used to prevent the blade sections from twisting relative to each other. The alignment pins are now integrated directly into the printed parts, so there is no need to print and insert them separately. Enjoy the print, and I hope you like Geralt the Witcher’s silver sword. Inspired by this concept, the CYBERPUNK OUTCAST FLINTLOCK MUSKET is a fully 3D-printable elastic-powered toy dart blaster that combines the appearance of a cyberpunk firearm with the operation of a traditional flintlock musket. Rather than simply resembling a flintlock, it recreates the complete firing sequence with a functional cock, frizzen, powder pan, trigger, sear, and half-cock safety. The blaster is muzzle-loaded. Insert the dart into the barrel, seat it with the ramrod, cock the lock, aim, and fire. The entire loading and firing sequence is designed to resemble the operation of a historical flintlock while using a completely different internal propulsion system. The model features a compact folding design. Both the stock and the front assembly lock securely in their folded and deployed positions, allowing the blaster to be stored or transported in a much smaller package while remaining ready for use within seconds. Designed primarily for PETG printing, the model is almost entirely 3D printed. No metal springs, screws, glue, filament retaining pins, or other additional hardware are required. The only non-printed components are the elastic bands used for propulsion and mechanism operation. In addition to the original HEX 13 mm dart version, the project also includes a separate conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts. Features Fully functional flintlock-style firing mechanism Functional half-cock safety Muzzle-loaded operation with ramrod Folding stock with adjustable length of pull Folding front assembly for compact storage 99% PETG 3D printed No metal springs, screws, glue, or additional hardware. Bambu filaments used Warhead at the top Basic Yellow Silk+ Titan Gray Overture Silk Copper ( Amazon link ) Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Rocket Body Basic Light Gray A white filament would work as well Silk+ Red Silk+ Silver (for the mid-body fins) Polymaker Metallic Silver ( Amazon link ) Basic Silver would work great too Engine Metal Iridium Gold Silk+ Gold would work too Assembly is super easy The parts simply screw together, so if you make a mistake you can just unscrew and re-screw in seconds, no problems. Make sure you don't over tighten – they are quite strong, but all plastic screws can eventually break under enough pressure – you should be able to screw them until they feel snug. 1. Screw the main body together, which includes 4 longer white/gray segments, one shorter red segment, and one short white/gray segment. 2. Then take each of the silver fins and connect all 4 to a base by sliding them together. It may take a little bit of forcer, pushing down on a table can help. 3. Now the assembled fins and clip them into the tall gray section. They should snap in easily if you line it up right. If you can't get the fins to snap in, try a different (probably lower) angle. 4. Next begin screwing on the other parts one by one to the far right end (the end with the red strip). 5. Then, assemble the warhead portion at the tip with the pegs provided like you see below and screw it onto the top of the rocket. 6. Lastly, begin connecting the rocket motor by connecting the top threaded piece to the bottom piece with the two long pegs provided. 7. Then the final step is to attach the fins to the rocket motor – the will snap into place with little force. Note that they must be facing clockwise , not counter clockwise. If you insert them counter clockwise you will find that they don't fold all the way.

description: Spartan/Trojan War Hound Dog Helmet – Fully Articulated Bring the glory of the ancient world to your furry companion! This isn’t just a costume piece; it’s a high-detail, 3D-printable tribute to the legendary warriors of Troy and Sparta, specifically designed to fit the unique anatomy of a dog. Whether it’s for a photoshoot, a convention, or just to show the neighborhood who the real "Alpha" is, this helmet is the ultimate accessory for your four-legged warrior. 🏛️ History of the Model The design is inspired by the Corinthian-style helmets used by ancient Greek hoplites and later stylized in Trojan lore. Historically, these helmets were symbols of strength, protection, and status. I wanted to translate that intimidating, majestic silhouette into something comfortable and wearable for pets. The intricate swirls and Celtic-inspired patterns on the cheek guards add a "mythical" flair, bridging the gap between historical accuracy and high-fantasy cosplay. ⚙️ Functional Design & Assembly This model is unique because it features fully functional articulated cheek guards (flaps) . The Hinge System: Unlike static models, this helmet uses custom-designed hinges. You will need to print the included hinge pins separately. Assembly: Once printed, align the cheek guards with the main helmet body and slide the 3D-printed pins through the knuckles. This allows the flaps to swing outward, making it much easier to put on and take off your dog while ensuring a comfortable fit against their jawline. Durability: The crest is reinforced to handle the "zoomies," but it remains lightweight enough for medium to large breeds to wear comfortably. 📏 Sizing and Fitting Your Warrior Because every "Good Boy" is a different size, scaling is critical. Measurement: To get the perfect fit, I highly recommend using my Cosplay Calipers Measuring Tool . Measure the width of your dog's head between the ears and the length from the brow to the back of the skull. Scaling & Orientation: If you need to scale this up for a Great Dane or down for a Terrier, or if you need to slice it to fit a smaller print bed, check out my comprehensive guide: How to Size, Scale, Cut, Pin, and Orient Armor in Bambu Studio . 🛠️ Printing Tips Filament: Looks incredible in Silk Silver PLA or "Antique Gold." Support: Tree supports are recommended for the internal dome and the hinge knuckles. 🔄 Remix Potential & Alternate Uses This model is a fantastic base for further creativity! Cat Version: Scale down to roughly 40-50% for a "Battle Cat" aesthetic. Entonces es hora de abrazar el silencio eterno. Te presentamos el kit completo de modelado 3D de la armadura de El Penitente , una réplica digital milimétrica diseñada para los devotos del cosplay que no temen purgar su paciencia en el nombre del Milagro Doloroso. 📜 Una Historia Escrita en Sangre y Silencio En las tierras malditas de Cvstodia, la culpa no es un sentimiento; es una fuerza física que deforma la carne y la piedra. El Penitente, último superviviente de la hermandad del Lamento Mudo, recorre un mundo devastado por la manifestación caprichosa de "El Milagro". Su armadura no busca protegerlo del dolor, sino amplificarlo como una forma de comunión. Coronado por el icónico Capirote , un cono de bronce envuelto en espinos que imita la penitencia del Primer Milagro, este guerrero silencioso avanza purgando las aberraciones de la religión ortodoxa. La Unión del Acero y la Tela: La armadura del Penitente es una fusión de placas metálicas rudimentarias y ropajes desgastados. Las piezas de los hombros y las rodilleras cuentan con ranuras internas ocultas para pasar correas de cuero auténtico y remaches físicos, asegurando que el peso se distribuya correctamente sin romper el plástico.

Spider-Man Popcorn Bucket – Hinged Edition Porta al cinema un bucket diverso da tutti gli altri. Questo modello è stato progettato e modellato interamente da zero, ispirandosi al popcorn bucket ufficiale dedicato a Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Ogni dettaglio è stato studiato per ottenere un modello fedele, pulito e semplice da assemblare, mantenendo al tempo stesso un meccanismo robusto e piacevole da utilizzare. Il sistema a cerniera è una progettazione originale e rappresenta il vero punto di forza di questo progetto. Contenuto del file Il modello è composto da 3 parti: Testa principale Meccanismo della cerniera Tappo posteriore Istruzioni di assemblaggio 1. Preparazione della cerniera Prima del montaggio, riscalda delicatamente con una piccola fiamma (o altra fonte di calore controllata) le due linguette elastiche del meccanismo della cerniera. Una volta ammorbidite, allargale leggermente con le dita . Questa piccola operazione aumenta la tensione del meccanismo, rendendo l'apertura e la chiusura più stabili ed evitando che la cerniera risulti troppo libera. 2. Inserimento della cerniera Comprimi leggermente le linguette della cerniera con le dita e inserisci il meccanismo nell'apposita sede presente all'interno della testa fino al corretto posizionamento. 3. Fissaggio del tappo Applica una piccola quantità di colla sulla superficie di incollaggio prevista, posiziona il tappo e premi con decisione fino al completo accoppiamento dei pezzi. Lascia asciugare completamente seguendo i tempi consigliati per l'adesivo utilizzato. Il modello è pronto! Una volta completato l'assemblaggio, il tuo Spider-Man Popcorn Bucket sarà pronto per essere utilizzato e portato al cinema. model_name: Halo Energy Sword - life-sized and light up!
tags: halo|halo energy sword|elite|elite energy sword|arbiter|master chief|halo cosplay|energy sword
description: Ever wanted a life-sized Halo energy sword? Me too! I was surprised that I couldn't find a print for this, so I made one myself. Coming in at just over a metre long, this is a faithful replica of the iconic Halo weapon. It looks great printed in either translucent blue or clear PETG, with light channels down the middle of each blade and compartments on both blades for electronics (batteries - sized for 18650 cells, control boards etc). Everything is designed to key together to allow for easy printing and assembly. This print takes up 5 full plates on my P2S and took a few days to print, with around 1.5kg of blade material. Each plate is as packed as it can reasonably be. It can of course be printed on smaller printers like the A1 and can be scaled down appropriately to suit this. Key assembly steps: Print and attach hilt sections together. I printed these in a grey PLA+, then stuck them together with CA glue. The fit is tight and may need a bit of force. There is a channel down the inside of the hilt to route wires for lights or switches. Optional - sand, prime, paint hilt. I painted with a base of black acrylic and then steel / silver acrylic on top, then sanded paint down in places to give a weathered look. Print blade base parts and attach to hilt. The fit between the hilt and blade base is a bit looser than any of the other joins, as this gives a bit more tolerance for any accumulated accuracy errors throughout the print. The intended attachment method is to use an M8 nut / insert / T-nuts heat-set into the handle, and an M8*40mm bolt through the blade into this nut / insert. You could however just use a suitable epoxy to bond the two parts well. Either way, this should be a secure connection once properly glued / torqued down. Attach blade pieces to blade base, finishing up with the optional reinforcing bar (secured using M3 heat inserts and M3*10mm bolts into the blade sections). You could use a suitable glue to attach these together, though the keyed fit is pretty tight. Optional finishing steps. I used a UV-set clear resin to fill the join lines between sections and make things look a bit more continuous. This certainly isn't a magic fix as it is obviously still printed in pieces, but it does help! You can then install electronics if desired. I found LED rope or LED-strips worked well (ideally with high density RGB COBs. If they're too far apart you get a less diffuse effect). The original energy sword sculpt was done by the extremely talented Sigil0fSaturn on the Sketchfab site, linked here ( Energy Sword - Halo Prop - Download Free 3D model by Sigil0fSaturn (@Sigil0fSaturn) [8dda2fc] )

Want a replica of the frag grenade from game PUBG (Player Unknown Battleground)? This grenade even has a spring-loaded handle that flies off when you pull the pin. The PUBG frag grenade is similar to the real-life M67 grenade, however, there are some distinct differences in its rounded shape and differences with the fuze that this model reflects. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring is what this model is designed to work with. Pen springs work as well though, many different types have been tested and work fine. You can often cut pen springs in half and get two grenade springs since this model only needs a 12mm long spring and pen springs tend to be about 24mm. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Silk+ Silver Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Matte Dark Green works too Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Use the two pegs to connect the two halves of the grenade together. 2. Flip the silver top upside down and insert the peg. Make sure the peg is sticking out of the top, if not rotate 90 degrees. 3. Insert your spring into the silver top next, just like you did with the peg. 4. Screw the silver top onto the grenade – keeping the silver top upside down makes this easier (so spring doesn't fall out while screwing it on). That's it – now you can attach the spoon handle, put in the pin, and use it – enjoy! Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Use the two pegs to connect the two halves of the grenade together. 2. Flip the silver top upside down and insert the spring. Make sure the spring's peg is sticking out of the top, if not rotate 90 degrees. 3. Screw the silver top onto the grenade – keeping the silver top upside down makes this easier (so spring doesn't fall out while screwing it on). That's it – now you can attach the spoon handle, put in the pin, and use it – enjoy!

Inspired by the terrifying infected creatures from HBO’s The Last of Us and the iconic Naughty Dog video game franchise, this model captures the grotesque, organic geometry of the Cordyceps brain infection bursting from a human skull. The front of the mask features the signature split, cauliflower-like fungal blooms completely overtaking the upper face, layered over an underlying structure of exposed, decaying teeth and infected skin tissue. Designed with cosplay comfort in mind, the rear of the print is ergonomically contoured to comfortably sit against a human face, making it the ultimate centerpiece for your next convention, Halloween costume, or horror display. Functional Use & Wearability This is a wearable cosplay prop. The internal face cavity is smooth to allow for the addition of foam padding, and the side profiles include clean integration points for a leather or elastic head strap. Because a full Clicker transformation leaves the host blind, this mask is designed for authentic tracking. However, for safe convention wear, the open mouth cavity and deep recesses within the fungal plates can easily be lined with black mesh fabric from the inside—allowing you to see out and breathe comfortably while keeping the actor's face completely hidden from the outside. For Rugged Outdoor/Con Wear: If you want extra temperature resistance against hot summer conventions, step up to SUNLU PETG Filament . Note: If you plan on modifying this model into a multi-color print using an AMS setup, be sure to watch my tutorial: How to Remesh and Color Prints Effectively in Bambu Studio . Assembly Instructions Depending on your printer build volume, you may choose to print this mask in sections. For a permanent, rock-solid bond that won't snap when under tension from the head strap, I highly recommend using ARKA KRAFTPROTZ UNIVERSAL Superglue . It fuses the printed seams flawlessly, ensuring your mask survives the chaos of a busy con floor. Fan made design Liberator carbine from Helldivers 2 Its pretty much all there with the exception of the pouch. Not quite good enough yet to get that part done properly. *Edit 7/19/26: Wall mount print profile has been added. Fully assembled it is almost 24 inches long. Features: Working picatinny rail with attachments. Sights can be quick swapped with each other or a scope if you go with 8x2 magnets. 2 different threaded muzzle options 2 sight options 1 scope option 1 under barrel “flashlight / laser combo” (2 parts held together with magnets) 1 under barrel grip Most parts are separated out for easy color printing. I'll provide an AMS profile for some of the main parts & accessories if you want to go that route. (Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. For armor, you want something strong and with great layer adhesion. I highly recommend printing this in a rugged material like PETG-CF (PETG Carbon Fiber) or ASA . PETG-CF offers excellent strength and rigidity, making it less prone to warping than regular PETG, and it sands beautifully. description: This one is for Squidward who relentlessly pushed for me to make the model, and then was so grateful when I got started! I hope you enjoy it! I designed this mask a bit different from my others and I am happy with the outcome. Essentially, I incorporated the mesh eyes directly into the mask so they don't need to be added or printed separately. If you would prefer to print it all in one color (to save time and money), you should be able to easily paint the mesh portion black with some black acrylic paint. I also experimented with how the horns are printed and attached to the head to make them more integrated into the design and also to avoid needing supports on them. My first version was a bit to tight to fit on my head, but it fit on everyone else's in my home. In this version I tweaked the hole size for the head and flattened the bottom of the print a bit to improve printability and eliminate some of the supports. I believe this should fit any head pretty easily now. One under appreciated part of my work is figuring out how to get a model absolutely maximize the space of a p1s sized printer. In this case of this print, lots of adjustments were made to get it just right. For this hobby (designing and 3d printing models) I certainly go through phases. After filling up all the wall space in a room with Hollow Knight masks, I prioritized new areas. This was a nice break from my current phase which has been pond fountains, I think I have one more of those left in me before switching again. I am experimenting with designing a toy for kids during long car rides, I am excited about it and hope to share it soon!

description: A fully 3d printed Single-shot Cap-powered BB pistol! Fully 3d printed springs. Has 10 bodies to print, can fit on an a1 build plate at minimum. Semi-auto hammer and trigger system though it is single shot. hammer action works well. The larger spring is the hammer spring, simply slot into the holes in the hammer and the main body. The smaller spring is the Trigger spring, do the same. The two main halves of the pistol snap together, may need a spot of glue on the joints. To use, get a standard 8-shot ring cap, then cut off an individual cap using a utility knife, being careful with fingers. Break the barrel (shown in images) by pressing the barrel release latch (shown in images as well) on the left hand side of the pistol body, then lift the barrel, tilting it upwards from the end near the hammer. Load the singular cap into the recess at the end of the barrel, making sure it sits snug. To lock the barrel, manually push the barrel release latch now protruding from the right hand side back into its original position. this can be fiddly ads the hole is quite precise. This is a muzzle loader-so from the muzzle, cut out a small square of tissue. Place it on the muzzle and get a standard 6mm BB. place the BB on top of the tissue wad and using a blunt skewer, ram the BB and the wad into the barrel until you feel it stop (do not ram too hard as the cap holder will snap). Then you are ready to fire! To reset the trigger, pull the hammer back manually and hold it, then let go of the trigger and it should spring back into place. You can pull it gently to help with this. *DISCLAIMER* I am not at fault for misuse of this toy causing damage to living beings and surroundings. model_name: Mandalorian Grav Charge With Lightup Mod (Breach)
description: This is my version of the Grav Charge and holder from the show The Mandalorian. I designed it looking at pictures from the show to be as accurate as I could but also be a light up prop. To that end I designed it around these little magnet operated light up warning lights: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMTJQRYX . The lights have a reed sensor in them that when the magnet is on the back they don't do anything but when you remove the magnet they light up. And the pattern is similar to the actual grav charge, close enough without needing expensive electronics or wiring anything. The back of the holder has some indents of 15mm magnets. Glue some magnets to the back and that will be strong enough to keep the light off. When you pull the grav charge off the holder the reed switch turns the unit on and the lights start to flash then after about 10 seconds go to the circular pattern. I added magnets on the bottom of the grav charges themselves also so you can still stick it to something like in the show but without affecting the light. Place it back on the holder and it turns back off. I went with these lights because they also turn themselves off after a couple minutes so they won't kill the battery if you leave them out. Print Details I printed the body and holder in Bambu ABS - Silver. The body has scarf seam turned on in its object settings which leaves less of a seam on the outside but does sometime affect the color slightly in that spot. If you are going to paint them leave scarf seam on, if you are going to leave them as is you may want to turn that off so the color is more consistent but the seam will be more noticeable. The cover is Bambu PETG Translucent Clear that I then used a red Sharpie oil based paint pen on because I couldn't find a good clear red filament. The combination ended up looking really good so that's what I would recommend or even possibly just a red marker. For printing the cover I have the speeds set to 20mm/s and a custom Bambu Transparent PETG setting that turns off cooling. It's the only way to get a mostly clear lens but you can of course use standard settings, the lens just might not be as clear and the LEDs won't be as distinguishable. Or you can buy a after market clear lens sized for about 28mm. I tried to optimize the print so no supports are required and the 2 x 4 magnets on the bottom should be press fit although I'd add a dab of glue behind them. The holder for the light also is press fit but you can also glue that in to be more secure. Since the lights turn themselves off the batteries should last for years so personally I glued them in.

History & Origin Originally designed in France by Louis Dolne during the late 1860s, these unique firearms were famously known as "Apache" revolvers—a moniker given by Parisian street gangs. description: Instant Ronin Double Tanto - Magnetic Knives Channel your inner samurai with the Instant Ronin - Double Tanto (Magnetic Edition) ! This isn't just a pair of sleek 3D-printable props—it's a fully mechanical, dual-sword ecosystem. By utilising a precise arrangement of 5-off 6mm x 3mm magnets per sword, these Tantos completely ditch traditional metal springs for solid-state physics. But here is the real kicker: One sword acts as the activator for the other. Mating the companion sword into the other triggers the magnetic mechanisms, releasing the internal locks and allowing for an instant, seamless locking - and the reverse when withdrawing. Absolutely zero glue required. Every magnet pocket has been engineered for a perfect, satisfying, push-fit. Print two, link them up, and prepare to lose hours of your life to the ultimate fidget experience. Features Triple-Action Magnetic Mechanics: Uses opposing and attracting magnetic fields to safely lock the blades closed, assist the deployment, and lock them open. 5-Magnet Precision Layout: Optimised specifically for standard, high-strength 6mm x 3mm cylinder magnets (5-off per sword). 100% Glue-Free Assembly: Meticulously tuned tolerances mean every magnet snaps tightly into place. Save the superglue for fixing the things you break with the Tanto. Zero Mechanical Springs: No metal springs to find, bend, fatigue, or lose tension over time—magnetism doesn't wear out! Dual-Tanto Blade Profile: A sleek, aggressive geometric aesthetic that looks as sharp as the mechanism feels. Maximum Fidget Factor Magnet Assembly Guide ⚠️ Crucial Tip: Because these are a push-fit, double-check your magnet orientation before you press them home. Getting a backward magnet out of a tight 3D-printed pocket is a special kind of pain you don't want to experience. Use a spare magnet as a reference tool! Follow this exact sequence to ensure the polarity works flawlessly, see my sectioned CAD image and assembly pictures to help with the below: The Master Slider Magnet [1]: Push a magnet into the bottom pocket of the Blade Slider . This can face any direction you like. Once it’s in, this magnet is the "Master" that dictates the rest of the build. The Extended Lock [2]: Press a magnet into the lower forward pocket of the Handle . This magnet must REPEL Magnet #1. (This repelling force is the secret sauce that lifts the slider up into the notch to lock the blade open!) The Retracted Lock [3]: Press a magnet into the bottom rear pocket of the Handle . This magnet must ATTRACT Magnet #1, snapping the blade securely closed so they doesn't slide apart when closed. The Kinetic "Spring" Caps [4]: Press one magnet into each of the two Circular Caps at the top hilt. Both of these magnets must REPEL each other, creating that crisp, snappy detent.

After this insert the longer tube (barrel) into the top hole of the receiver, then insert the bottom one as well. Make sure the flared end of the second tube is AWAY from the receiver (this is what the heat shield will later rest on/touch). Add the assembled stock to the other end (make sure to join the two stock sides in the correct orientation). Afte this simply slide on the assembled heat shield and the foregrip to the bottom tube! Saber:Rail is a redesigned modular wall display system for lightsaber hilts, made for makers and collectors who want a clean display that can easily grow with their collection. The system keeps the layout and functionality of the previous version, but has been rebuilt from the ground up with cleaner dimensions and improved assembly. The existing Lightsaber Wall Mount Add-On – Push-Fit Nameplate remains compatible with Saber:Rail. It can be used to label individual hilts, characters, replicas, or collection sections. After a longer wait than I hoped, the supported version of my unexpectedly popular flamberge print is ready!! This was the first ever success that I had with taking a large video game sword and making a good, 3D printed version of it. I identified some problems with the original design and I have added some very minor details to the model and added a channel for a 4ft/1.22m long, 5/16"/.794cm diameter fiberglass rod through about 3/4 of the length of the prop sword. The sword is 5.6ft/1.71m long when fully assembled. In the U.S. I have found that the easiest access to rods like this is by purchasing driveway markers from a hardware store like Home Depot or Lowe's. To assemble, start with the end of the hilt, add your rod, and start stacking the pieces from there. If a piece doesn't slide easily over the rod and overlapping section of the piece below it, there's a good chance that it needs to be rotated 180 degrees. IMPORTANT FOR ASSEMBLY: Please do NOT print this version if you can't find a supporting rod - the rod doesn't leave space for meaningful printed structure (keying blades only) and the blade will snap with ease if assembled without support. Also note that the last 1.6ft/.5m of length are unsupported in the interest of balance and weight reduction - this means that hitting something with more than gentle force will likely snap the end of the blade. That said, I think that with appropriate caution this version should work well to take to conventions/festivals. My build was done with SUNLU PETG. I would recommend PETG or a material with high impact toughness, especially if you want to take it out and about at an event!

The dust of unknown alien crystals stained the collar of his spacesuit, deep space surveyor Rien paused his step, this weird dagger was half buried under the melted reactor core of the abandoned outpost ⚫️. As an expendable crew of the Galactic Union survey project, he only needed to log the coordinate of this outpost that lost contact 15 years ago, no one expected to find any intact artifact on this planet marked as "dead rock". But this dagger changed everything 🗡️. The moment Rien wrapped his hand around the scaly hilt, vague whispers exploded in his ear, foreign neural impulse crawled along his veins to the back of his brain. Fragments of memory flooded into his mind: a starship captain cut through the thick exoskeleton of a Xeno creature, a frantic researcher stabbed it into his own chest, a galactic inquisitor nailed it to the chest of a dimension heretic, and at the end of all messy memory fragments, there is endless dark abyss, countless eyeballs staring quietly at any person who dares to hold the blade 👁️. Rien shook his head to get rid of the chaos, the whisper faded quickly, only the cold touch of the blade left on his palm. He touched the back of his neck, a small scale-like bump quietly grew there. The comms in his pocket squealed with request signal from the base one light-year away, asking him for a status report. Rien stared at the flowing dark light in the hollow of the blade, and did not reach for the comms. He looked at the growing translucent scales on the back of his hand, and understood that this outpost was never lost, it was just a lighthouse waiting for the next qualified host of the blade, and the door to the abyssal void is about to open again 🌌

description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

description: Kneeling in the concrete dust of the abandoned outpost’s core control room, interstellar bounty hunter Jax freezes when his reinforced gloved hand brushes the carved cold surface of the dagger half-buried under the broken server racks⚫. The job he took three weeks ago sounded simple enough: retrieve an unknown classified artifact from the derelict research station drifting in the dead zone between Alpha Centauri and the old solar system, the offered pay was enough for him to buy a brand new stealth frigate and retire from the risky life of chasing bounties across the galaxy🔹. He didn’t ask why the anonymous employer was willing to pay ten times the normal market price for a random relic from a station that lost all contact with human civilization 300 years ago, didn’t question why all eight salvage teams sent here before him never sent a single message back after entering the dead zone’s boundary🔸. The interwoven thorn patterns on the dark handle seem to be breathing under his touch, faint cool light seeps out from the gaps of the deep carving, and a low hum that doesn’t match any frequency in the known universe vibrates up his arm, straight into his temporal lobe, stirring up blurry images that don’t belong to his memory🌌. He sees twisted black spires piercing a hazy purple sky that never sees daylight, sees countless unblinking eyes slowly opening between the cracks of those spires, and the patterns carved on this dagger are exactly the map of that alien world that should not exist in any human’s consciousness🔯. Jax tries to yank his hand away from the handle, but his fingers won’t obey any commands from his brain, they have already wrapped tightly around the dark handle on their own, and the veins on the back of his hand have already twisted into the exact same thorn shape as the carving on the blade. The locator on his wrist suddenly beeps loudly, it’s an incoming message from his anonymous employer, the text on the screen only has one short line: "Welcome to the new anchor of the Void Gate, the darkness has been waiting for you for hundreds of years"😈. He can already feel the alien will stored in the dagger slowly merging with his own consciousness, he is no longer the hunter holding the weapon, the dagger is using his body to walk back into the crowded human world, to re-open the door that the dead researchers sealed 300 years ago with all their lives🚪

description: 7月24日最后一次更新（小尺寸钥匙扣） 需要用到ams多色打印，雏菊配件用胶水粘合（风车雏菊在安装良好的情况下也能迎风转动） 7月15日更新（香薰底座） 当我完成风车雏菊的时候我就在想，它放在我的电脑桌前，风从它的背后吹到我的脸上，除了风车能转动，它还能带来什么？我觉得它应该有一种淡淡的香味！所以我制作了一个可以放置香薰的底座！你可以把你喜欢的香薰藏在底部。 你还可以打印一些雏菊装饰它，让它变得更加美观跟清新！（雏菊制作完后用打火机燎一下，然后让所有的叶片翘起来） _________________________________________________________ 为什么做这个模型？ 我是一直很喜欢《玩具总动员》里的所有角色，尤其是巴斯光年！但最近却被三眼仔彻底圈粉了——特别是GD主理的PEACEMINUSONE和迪士尼、Toy Story合作的特别版，那个雏菊元素真的太戳我了。可惜国内一直买不到，心里痒痒的，就干脆自己动手，用SolidWorks建模设计了一个还原度比较高的外观。 正好夏天到了，我在电脑前常开风扇，就突发奇想： 能不能让雏菊转起来？ 于是就有了这个“三眼仔 × 风车雏菊”的互动模型——它既是摆件，也是一个可以迎风转动的小风车，放在桌面特别有趣（我非常喜欢它转动时发出的声响）。 🛠 设计与结构 全程使用 SolidWorks 建模（不是AI生成，每一个曲面和卡扣都是手工调整的，花了很多心血）。 完全无胶水组装 （除了嘴巴那块薄片，我暂时搞不定，如果有大神有妙招，恳请指点！）。 零件可替换 ：如果某个部位坏了，或者你想换颜色，直接拆换对应零件就行，非常方便。 🌼 雏菊的两种形态 我做了两套雏菊配件： 还原版 — 尽量贴近原版PEACEMINUSONE的雏菊造型（静态装饰）。 风车版 — 保留雏菊元素，但优化了叶片角度，可以迎风旋转。 你可以根据心情随时替换，一个模型两种玩法。 📦 后续计划(0715已经更新) 我本来还打算设计一个专用底座，用来收纳多余的雏菊配件，也让三眼仔有个“家”，但比赛时间太紧，没来得及完善。后续我会陆续上传底座和更多配件，欢迎关注。 组装顺序请参考附图

description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours. Absolutely NO A.I. was used to make these models nor the images. Do not reupload my files somewhere else. I will upload them where I want. DO NOT SELL THEM!
